Search is a hybrid: (a) enumerative bottom-up search over its OWN library, weighted by a learned prior (a simple bigram model over primitives, updated nightly), and (b) a proposal from the local Qwen3-4B, grammar-constrained by a GBNF compiled directly from the DSL so it CANNOT emit an invalid program. Candidate programs execute against a cheap copy of local world-state (this is the agent's 'imagination'); the winner executes for real, in the real deterministic sim, and reality gets the final vote. Every program that measurably reduced a need is appended to corpus.jsonl with its context and its measured delta. SLEEP (nightly, 03:00, ~4 minutes of CPU): run stitch_core.compress() over the last N=8000 successful programs. Stitch returns abstractions ranked by compression gain. The top-k (k~3, gated by minimum utility) are minted as NEW NAMED PRIMITIVES and injected into the DSL, the GBNF grammar is regenerated, and one Haiku call names each one and writes a one-line etymology in-world ('they call it emberkeep — to smother the fire so it wakes'). Those primitives are now vocabulary. Tomorrow's search operates one level higher. That recursion is the entire compounding mechanism, and it is the same mechanism that made DreamCoder rediscover Newtonian laws and classic list routines from scratch. THE CULTURAL TWIST that makes it a civilization instead of a library: an abstraction does not belong to the tribe, it belongs to the MINDS that hold it. carriers = set of agent ids with mastery > 0.3. Teaching is a scheduled interaction costing labor-hours; the child receives the abstraction with mastery = parent_mastery * (1 - noise) AND with probability p a corrupted AST (one argument permuted, one subterm dropped, one constant jittered). Corruptions usually fail. Occasionally a corruption is better — that is a second, independent invention channel, and it is pure cultural transmission noise doing the work. If every carrier of an abstraction dies before teaching it, it is deleted from the world. The tribe can lose fire. Writing is not authored either: if search ever finds a program whose effect is a durable, legible mark on a low-decay_rate surface, the engine detects that the program's output object satisfies (legibility > 0.5 and decay_rate < eps) and unlocks inscribe(surface, library_entry) as an affordance. From that moment abstractions can be stored outside heads at mastery 1.0, decaying at the medium's rate. The invention-rate curve visibly changes regime the night that happens.
all.why_unbounded: The reachable space is programs of bounded depth d over a vocabulary V, which is roughly |V|^(b*d) — and |V| GROWS every night as compression mints primitives. Each new primitive is a chunk that used to cost 6 nodes and now costs 1, so a depth-8 search after 200 abstractions reaches what would have been depth-40 raw programs. That is not a list a designer wrote; it is a recursive re-parameterization of the search space by its own successes, and it is the same argument Arthur makes in The Nature of Technology (combination begets combinables) and Kauffman makes about the adjacent possible (each new thing enlarges the set of next things). WHERE IT ACTUALLY BOTTOMS OUT, honestly: the BASE primitives and the physics' state variables are a hard wall. If your physics has no pressure field, no steam engine is reachable, ever, no matter how much compression happens. The library can only get deeper inside the expressiveness you shipped. This is why the substrate is continuous fields and a composition vector rather than an item list — the number of DISTINGUISHABLE material states is then astronomically large and the wall sits very far out, but it exists and you should know exactly where it is: it is the set of numbers in the object struct.
all.depth_ladder: WEEK 1 (with a 10-primitive DSL and no LLM yet): agents carry water, feed fire, huddle, dry meat, and Stitch mints its first abstraction — probably something dull-but-real like 'carry-then-place-near-heat'. Delight moment: it names a chunk you never thought of, because it noticed the chunk repeated 400 times. REAL RUNGS, in the order they will plausibly fall: banked fire (cover + ash + wait, discovered because agents keep waking to cold embers); cordage (twist + soak + dry over cellulose fibers); hafting (bind + strike composed); fired clay (kiln failures teach that an open fire never crosses 900C, which forces the earthwork); charcoal (cellulose + starved airflow — the sim's airflow field makes this a genuine discovery, not a recipe); bellows (hide + cord + chamber, only reachable AFTER cordage and hide-working); bloom iron (charcoal + iron-oxide sand + forced airflow above threshold); lime/plaster if you include a carbonate; and inscription, which changes everything. WILDEST PLAUSIBLE ENDPOINT with a load/stress and flow field in the physics: a water-driven trip hammer — because 'apply repeated strike without labor-hours' is a compression the system will WANT once labor is the binding constraint; a granary with a stored inscribed corpus (a library building whose presence multiplies teaching bandwidth); and a specialist caste that emerges because the abstraction depth exceeds what one lifetime can master, which the sim measures directly as teaching-hours-required > remaining-lifespan.
all.what_selects: Kcal and core temperature, on an hourly tick, with a winter that is genuinely lethal. Childbirth and childhood mortality. Injury from failed programs (a bad hafting throws the axe head). And competition: 2-5 tribes share the basin, wood and clay deposits are finite and rivalrous, and a tribe holding more high-utility abstractions produces more kcal per labor-hour, so it outbreeds and out-settles. Explicit extinction is the point — a tribe that loses its cordage abstraction in a bad flu season will visibly fall down the ladder, and you will read about it. Abstractions themselves are under selection: each carries carriers_alive, teach_count, and measured kcal-per-labor-hour delta; low-utility ones stop being taught and quietly die.
all.changing_worlds: Three layers. (1) SLOW: a deterministic climate signal per world seed — three superimposed sines at ~40, ~400 and ~4000 day periods — so there are hard centuries and soft centuries and the tribe cannot tune to a static optimum. (2) SHOCK: seeded events sampled from a fixed table with long return periods — ashfall that zeroes photosynthesis for 90 days, a river avulsion that moves the clay deposit, a blight that removes one food species permanently. (3) NEW BASINS: every ~2 weeks of wall-clock a new basin is generated (different resource abundances AND different threshold constants — the clay here fires at 1050C, the ore is manganese-rich) and a gate opens. Tribes may migrate carrying only what their living members know. Abstractions tuned to the old constants FAIL in the new basin; the tribe keeps teaching them anyway for a few generations, which the engine labels ritual. Every basin runs as its own deterministic process; a world-index page shows all of them.
all.novelty_detector: Three layers, and the third is the good one. (1) FIRST-EVER: canonicalize the program AST (alpha-renamed, sorted commutative args), hash it, check a bloom filter over all history. Cheap, high recall, high noise. (2) BAYESIAN SURPRISE: maintain Dirichlet counts over event-type bigrams and over binned world-state features; push when KL(posterior || prior) for the day exceeds a running 99th percentile. This catches regime changes (the day everyone starts sleeping indoors) without knowing what to look for. (3) ASSEMBLY INDEX (Sharma/Cronin/Walker, Nature 2023): for every physical object in the world, compute the minimum number of DSL steps to build it from freely-available materials — that is literally the assembly index, and it is cheap because you already have the build DAG. Track max_assembly_index and the copy_number of every high-index object. A push fires when the basin's max assembly index increases, or when a high-index object's copy number crosses a threshold (meaning it is being REPRODUCED, i.e. it is now technology and not an accident). This is the single best civilizational-depth metric I know of that is actually computable, and it is what the phone card leads with. Haiku is called only for items that clear these filters — typically 5-30 a day, not thousands.
all.phone_view: One card, no scrolling. Line 1: 'Day 611 · Ashpan · 2 tribes · 47 alive · winter'. Line 2, the headline, always the highest-novelty event: 'NEW: emberkeep (assembly 9). Sura taught it to 3 children, then died at 41.' Line 3: max assembly index sparkline (the civilization's depth over time) and population sparkline, 60px tall. Line 4: three-node diff of the library graph — what was minted, what went extinct, what is down to one carrier ('cordage: 1 carrier left, age 63' is the most alarming sentence the app can print, and it should be red). Line 5: the Haiku chronicle paragraph, 40 words, written in a chronicler's voice. Tap anywhere → full force-directed library graph colored by carrier count, tap a node → its etymology, its inventor, its death. ntfy push fires at most 3x/day and only on layer-3 novelty.
all.hardware_use: Honest sizing for 8GB. llama.cpp server with Qwen3-4B-Instruct at Q4_K_M (~2.5GB weights), -np 6 parallel slots, 4k context each, KV cache at q8 (~0.6GB) → ~3.5-4GB VRAM, leaving room for the browser and the compositor. Expect roughly 90-130 tok/s single-stream on a laptop 5070 and maybe 250-400 tok/s aggregate across slots; the published 5070-class benchmark I found is ~86 tok/s for an 8B at Q4_K/4k, and a 4B should be comfortably faster, but a LAPTOP 5070 is thermally limited and will sit below desktop numbers. Budget planning number: 5-10M generated tokens/day, i.e. ~60-100k short grammar-constrained program proposals. That is far more than the sim needs — the sim is the bottleneck, not the GPU. The sim itself is CPU: numpy fields (or a Rust core via pyo3 once you care), and 64GB RAM means the whole event log stays in page cache. Stitch is Rust, runs on CPU, seconds to a couple of minutes over 8k programs. NO TRAINING, so no VRAM contention. Set a 65% GPU duty cycle so the fans are livable overnight. Haiku: naming (5-30/day), the chronicle (1/day), a Sunday essay (1/week) — 150-300 batched calls/day. At $1/$5 per MTok with the Batch API's 50% off, ~300 calls x (1k in / 600 out) ≈ $0.15 in + $0.90 out ≈ under a dollar; cut it to 150 calls if you want headroom. Prompt caching (90% off reads) helps the live path but not batch, so lean on batch and short prompts.
all.input_cadence: Zero required, ever. The thing runs 24/7 and writes to you. Optional god-tier nudges, all one-tap from the PWA: drop a resource seam, trigger a climate shock, open a gate to a new basin, kill a tribe, or 'pin a question' that the nightly chronicler must answer in tomorrow's paragraph ('is anyone still teaching cordage?'). Realistically the only recurring chore is the one you will actually enjoy: extending the DSL and the physics when you see the library plateau, maybe an hour every few weeks.
all.tech: Python 3.12 sim core (numpy for the fields), SQLite in WAL mode as the event/lineage store (tables: agents, kin_edges, abstractions, carriers, teachings, programs, artifacts, events, novelty_scores) — one file, greppable, trivially backed up. stitch_core (pip) for compression. llama.cpp server for Qwen3-4B with a GBNF grammar auto-generated from the DSL on every library update. FastAPI read-only JSON API. Vanilla-JS canvas PWA (your home turf) served over Tailscale Serve for the live view, PLUS a nightly static snapshot committed to GitHub Pages so the phone still works when the laptop sleeps. ntfy.sh topic for push. This is the shared substrate you reuse across all future projects: headless deterministic sim + SQLite event log + novelty scorer + PWA chronicle + ntfy. Benchmark hygiene: NOTHING in the fitness path touches wall-clock — utility is measured in kcal per labor-hour and sim ticks, both deterministic, so thermal throttling cannot corrupt evolution.
all.first_weekend: Saturday: physics with 6 materials, a heat field, hunger, cold, death; 8 DSL primitives; a tree-walking interpreter; one tribe of 12; enumerative search only, no LLM at all. Get them to keep a fire alive. Sunday morning: log every successful program to corpus.jsonl. Sunday afternoon: pip install stitch_core, dump 500 programs in, print the abstractions. THAT is the moment — Stitch will hand you a named chunk you did not author, used 200 times, and you will immediately want to know what to call it. Wire one Haiku call to name it, print the etymology to the terminal, and you have the whole loop in miniature. LLM proposals, teaching, mortality of knowledge, and the PWA are week two.
all.six_months_later: Four or five basins running as separate seeds. A library graph of 150-400 abstractions with real depth structure — you can see the trunk (fire, cord, heat-holding) and the branches. At least one lineage that invented inscription and one that did not, and the difference is visible in their invention rate as a kink in the chart. A dozen extinction events where an abstraction died with its last carrier, each one a story. Tribes migrating between basins carrying knowledge that no longer applies. You will have extended the DSL twice and the physics once. The morning ritual is real: coffee, one card, 'wait, they did WHAT'.
all.honest_ceiling: Two plateaus, and they arrive at different times. (1) COMPRESSION PLATEAU, ~6-10 weeks: once the task distribution is stationary, Stitch stops finding high-gain abstractions and mints junk. Climate cycles and new basins are the deliberate fix, and they buy months, not years, because non-stationarity from a fixed generator is itself eventually stationary. (2) EXPRESSIVENESS WALL, ~3-6 months: the physics' state variables are the hard limit on what can ever be invented. This is the one that ends the project if you ship 6 materials and 2 fields; ship 9 composition dimensions and 4 continuous fields and the wall moves out a long way, but it is still a wall you built. There is also a search-depth problem: a 4B's program proposals get weak past depth ~8, at which point enumeration dominates and this quietly becomes a compute-bound search project rather than an LLM project. That is fine, but know it. Real work: DSL and physics design is the actual craft here and it never fully ends. Expect a debugging week where compression mints degenerate abstractions (constants baked in, arity-0 wrappers) and you add utility gates.
all.research_notes: VERIFIED: DreamCoder — Ellis et al., 'DreamCoder: bootstrapping inductive program synthesis with wake-sleep library learning', PLDI 2021, dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3453483.3454080 (wake/sleep + refactoring via e-graph matching to build a deepening library). Stitch — Bowers et al., 'Top-Down Synthesis for Library Learning', POPL 2023; repo github.com/mlb2251/stitch; Python bindings stitch_core (pip), docs stitch-bindings.readthedocs.io, API is stitch_core.compress(programs, iterations=...) returning abstractions + usage stats; the paper explicitly claims scaling to corpora intractable for prior deductive approaches, which is exactly the regime you need. LILO (arxiv.org/abs/2310.19791) is the LLM-augmented successor that also auto-DOCUMENTS abstractions — directly relevant to naming them in-world. Assembly theory — Sharma, Czégel, Lachmann, Kempes, Walker, Cronin, Nature 2023, arxiv.org/abs/2206.02279: assembly index = minimal steps to build an object from basic parts, copy number = observed instances; the pair is designed to distinguish selection-driven complexity from noise, which is precisely a novelty detector for an invention sim. llama.cpp GBNF grammars: github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/grammars/README.md — JSON-schema-to-GBNF conversion is built in and the server accepts response_format; server has slot-based parallel decoding (-np). Model sizing: Qwen3-4B Q4 is ~2.5-3.4GB; a published RTX 5070 (desktop, 12GB) recipe reports ~85.8 tok/s for Qwen3-8B Q4_K at 4k context (smeltcore.com) — treat that as an optimistic upper bound for the 8GB laptop part. Haiku 4.5 pricing confirmed at anthropic.com/claude/haiku: $1/MTok input, $5/MTok output, up to 90% off with prompt caching, 50% off with the Batch API. Not used but checked: Voyager (arxiv.org/abs/2305.16291, github.com/MineDojo/Voyager) is the skill-library precedent; Project Sid (arxiv.org/abs/2411.00114) is the many-agent precedent.

audit.name: Embertongue
audit.ceiling: Two stops, and the real one is far earlier than they think. (a) The advertised wall is the physics threshold table; the ACTUAL first wall is sparse reward over long horizons. Fitness = 'a program that measurably reduced a need' gives literally zero credit for building a kiln, gathering ore, or a 4-hour firing that pays off tomorrow. Enumerative search plus a 4B proposer cannot cross a 6-step delayed-payoff chain with no gradient, so the library plateaus at depth-2/3 compositions of immediate-payoff actions (fetch-place-heat, huddle, dry-meat) at roughly WEEK 2-4 — before charcoal, and nowhere near bellows or bloom iron. Those ladder rungs are unreachable without reward shaping the designer would have to author, at which point he has authored the tree. (b) Even if solved, the discoverable set equals the count of qualitatively distinct threshold rules in the 400-line physics — call it 15-30 — exhausted in 8-14 weeks. (c) Deadliest detail: Stitch keeps minting abstractions after both stops, so the 'library is growing' chart stays healthy while nothing new happens. That is the most dangerous failure mode in the whole batch because it looks exactly like success.
audit.authored_content_risk: High and under-acknowledged. 'No authored recipes anywhere' is false. 'Clay above 900C for 4h becomes irreversibly hard' and 'iron-oxide + carbon + airflow above 1200C yields a bloom' ARE recipes — written in numbers instead of names. The depth_ladder is a list of things the author put in the physics file, in the order he put them there. What IS genuinely unauthored is the path and the chunking: Stitch's abstractions are real structure nobody wrote, and that part is honest. So: real search over an authored landscape. Better than a tech tree walked by bots; not open-ended. The writing unlock is worse — legibility>0.5 AND decay_rate<eps is an authored affordance with a physics-shaped trigger, i.e. a tech-tree node in a trench coat. Deepest conceptual error: DreamCoder's compounding came from a human-authored curriculum of increasingly hard task batteries, not from the library. Compression is a POSTERIOR operation — it re-encodes what already succeeded and never proposes a harder problem. Here the task distribution is homeostatic and satiable: once kcal/labor-hour clears winter, nothing pulls programs deeper. Their own 6-10 week compression plateau prediction is therefore structural, not tunable.
audit.compute_honesty: Mostly honest — GPU sizing is conservative, Stitch on 8k programs is seconds-to-minutes on CPU, SQLite is right. Two real omissions. (1) They dropped DreamCoder's neural recognition model ('NO TRAINING'), which is the half of the loop that keeps search tractable as |V| grows. Without it, adding primitives INCREASES branching factor, so search degrades over time — the exact opposite of 'depth-8 reaches what would have been depth-40'. A 4B with a GBNF over 200 invented primitives named 'emberkeep' has no useful prior over them; by month two this is a CPU enumeration project with an LLM ornament. (2) Unbudgeted: imagination rollouts. Candidates x sim-steps over continuous fields with multi-hour processes, per agent, per need. That is the real bottleneck and it is unsized. Also a metric bug: assembly index measured in DSL steps is not comparable across nights once minting collapses 6 steps into 1 — max_assembly_index will move on abstraction events rather than on invention, corrupting the headline chart.
audit.semantic_risk: Medium. Programs are typed and physics-grounded, so outputs are not drivel. But Stitch abstractions are frequent-substring artifacts and only sometimes functional units; Haiku naming plus an in-world etymology confers apparent meaning on syntactic noise, and the chronicle will render it as culture. Fix before shipping the namer: require an abstraction to have a measurable, context-independent effect delta before it earns a name.
audit.dubious_claims: DreamCoder 'rediscovered Newtonian laws' — true, but inside a curated symbolic-regression battery; it is not evidence of open-endedness and is used here as if it were. Assembly index 'is literally the assembly index and it is cheap because you already have the build DAG' — WRONG: the build DAG yields the shortest OBSERVED construction (an upper bound); computing the true minimal assembly index is NP-complete (npj Complexity 2025 / arXiv 2406.12176), and assembly theory's claim to detect selection is actively contested (Zenil et al., PLOS Complex Systems; arXiv 2403.06629, 2408.15108). Fine as a depth proxy, do not cite it as rigorous. Cost math: 180k output tokens at the batch rate ($2.50/MTok) is $0.45, not $0.90 — they used list price after claiming the discount. 'Prompt caching helps the live path but not batch' is likely wrong and directly contradicts Grist's own note; caching applies within Batch requests, and Grist's version is the correct one. The RTX 5070 ~85.8 tok/s figure is an unverifiable vendor blog; a ~115W laptop 5070 with 8GB will be materially slower, and -np 6 x 4k KV on top of a 2.5GB model is tighter than stated.
audit.one_change: Ship an autocurriculum. Replace the satiable homeostatic objective with pressure that scales with capability: unbounded population growth against rivalrous depletable resources, plus an explicit proposer that logs UNMET needs as standing tasks, plus credit for programs that expand the reachable state space (not only kcal delta) so multi-step chains get partial credit. DreamCoder's depth came from its curriculum, not its library — without one, Stitch compresses junk by week 8 no matter how good the physics is.

all.name: Saltmark
all.pitch: An artificial chemistry with an infinite molecule space, and tribes who can only exploit it as fast as their LANGUAGE lets them talk about it — so the real invention being made, generation by generation, is a compositional naming system. You watch a lexicon go from holistic grunts to 'ash-bitter-thick' and watch the discovery rate jump the week it happens.
all.world: No grid needed at first; a small set of hearth-sites connected by travel time. The substrate is a deterministic artificial chemistry: molecules are strings over a 6-symbol alphabet; reactions are ligation (concat) and cleavage (split), and whether reaction R is catalysed by molecule M is decided by a fixed hash rule — hash(M, R) < threshold. This is Kauffman's binary polymer model in its cheapest computable form (cf. Sayama's 'Non-Spatial Hash Chemistry as a Minimalistic Open-Ended Evolutionary System', arXiv 2404.18027). No content is authored: the entire chemistry is a hash function and two operators. A pot at a hearth is a multiset of molecules with a temperature and a duration; ticking a pot runs mass-action kinetics for those molecules. Each molecule gets a small number of LEGIBLE physical properties derived deterministically from its string — nutrition, toxicity, adhesion, burn temperature, dye hue, bitterness — via fixed projections, so that agents (and you) can actually perceive it as food/poison/glue/pigment rather than as noise. Agents are bodies with hunger, poisoning load, and a LEXICON: a mapping from signals (strings over a syllable inventory) to meanings (regions of property space), plus a set of remembered procedures.
all.invention_engine: Two engines, coupled, and the coupling is the idea. ENGINE A — CHEMISTRY DISCOVERY: agents mix, heat, wait, strain, and re-seed pots. What comes out is computed by the chemistry, not chosen by anyone. Nightly, run a RAF detection pass (reflexively-autocatalytic and food-generated set detection — Hordijk & Steel's algorithm is polynomial and about 200 lines) over the reaction network the tribe has actually realised, to identify self-sustaining loops. A discovered RAF is a *living* technology: a starter culture, a fermentation, a self-renewing catalyst supply. Losing it means losing an entire industry, and it can be lost by letting a pot go cold. ENGINE B — ITERATED LEARNING OF NAMES: this is the cultural engine. Each generation, adults produce signals for substances; children observe only a BOTTLENECK subset of (signal, substance) pairs and must generalise. Implemented concretely: the local Qwen3-4B plays teacher and learner in short referential games (teacher sees a substance's property vector and its lexicon, emits a signal; learner picks from N distractors), and the resulting learner lexicon is stored as an explicit trie, not as vibes. The bottleneck plus a communication pressure is the classic Kirby iterated-learning setup, and it reliably produces COMPOSITIONAL structure — signals decompose into morphemes that track property dimensions. Recent work replicates this specifically with LLM agents (Kouwenhoven et al. 2025, iterated referential games with generational transmission; 'From Signals to Structure', arXiv 2607.00233, finds compositionality needs BOTH a discriminability pressure and a compression pressure). THE COUPLING: a compositional lexicon lets an agent describe a substance it has never seen to someone who has never seen it, which mechanically unlocks (a) recipes transmitted verbally without co-presence, (b) trade orders for substances by description, (c) a child correctly PREDICTING a substance's properties from its name before tasting it — which stops it dying. So language quality feeds directly into discovery rate and survival, and you can plot the two curves on the same axes. That plot is the artifact.
all.why_unbounded: The molecule space is strings over an alphabet: countably infinite, with reachable depth limited only by energy and time. RAF sets nest — a RAF whose food set includes the output of another RAF is a strictly deeper industry, and there is no upper bound on nesting. The lexicon is an open vocabulary over an open meaning space. Nothing here is a list. HONEST BOTTOM: most of an infinite chemistry is uninteresting slop, and 'unbounded' is worthless if 99.999% of it is indistinguishable garbage. The *interesting* subspace is bounded by the number of legible property projections you define (I said six) and by the fitness pressures attached to them. Two, maybe three of those properties will carry all the drama. Also, the language transition happens ONCE per world — compositionality, once achieved, is stable (that is the whole point of iterated learning). So the repeatable, evergreen content is language BIRTH, which means new worlds with new chemistries are not a bonus feature here, they are the content pipeline.
all.depth_ladder: WEEK 1: agents eat random strings, poison each other, and one hearth accidentally keeps a pot warm long enough to produce something with nutrition > 0. First names are holistic — one arbitrary syllable-blob per substance, no structure, and children mostly fail to learn them. REAL RUNGS: a two-step preparation (leach a toxin out, then heat) that no single agent designed; a fermentation that runs overnight (first RAF); a catalyst that can be harvested but not made, which creates a place worth walking to and therefore a trade route; the same catalyst becoming makeable, which collapses the trade route and impoverishes a hearth; the first MORPHEME — a syllable that reliably means 'bitter' across many names — detectable as a spike in topographic similarity between signal-space and meaning-space distances; recipes transmitted by description alone to a hearth that has never seen the ingredients; a nested RAF (industry A's waste is industry B's food); written marks for morphemes, i.e. an alphabet, which is a much more natural origin story for writing than 'they invented writing'. WILDEST PLAUSIBLE ENDPOINT: a seed culture — a living autocatalytic starter physically passed down for 40 generations, maintained by a ritual nobody understands, whose loss during a famine causes a measurable civilizational regression; and a schism over two dialects whose morphemes carve the property space differently, so the two tribes literally cannot exchange recipes and diverge into different chemistries. That is emergent religion and emergent ethnolinguistics out of a hash function and a bottleneck.
all.what_selects: Toxicity kills fast, malnutrition kills slow. Catalysts are scarce and rivalrous. Pots need fuel and attention, so labor allocation is a real constraint. Between tribes: the one whose children learn the lexicon faster loses fewer people to poisoning and can run deeper pathways, because deep pathways need reliable multi-person coordination which needs reliable naming. Learnability is fitness — that is the pressure that drives compositionality, and it is grounded in corpses, not in a loss function.
all.changing_worlds: The FOOD SET (freely available molecules) drifts seasonally and differs per region, so pathways go dead and dormant knowledge becomes valuable again later. Each new world is a new hash seed, which means a completely different chemistry — nothing transfers except the IDEA of naming, and the tribe's morphology (their syllable inventory, their morpheme-slot order) does transfer, so you get language families with shared grammar over unrelated vocabularies. That is a gorgeous, cheap, and completely mechanical way to have 'multiple worlds' mean something. Run 3-6 seas concurrently; the world index page is a map of chemistries.
all.novelty_detector: (1) First synthesis of a molecule whose assembly index (min ligation/cleavage steps from the food set — the chemistry gives you this exactly) exceeds the world record. (2) RAF-set jump: nightly RAF detection returns a set whose size or nesting depth increased. (3) THE LANGUAGE METRIC, and this is the special one: topographic similarity (Spearman correlation between pairwise edit distance in signal space and pairwise distance in meaning space) measured over each generation's lexicon, plus held-out generalisation accuracy — can this generation's children correctly name a substance NO ONE has named before? A jump in either is the compositionality transition and it deserves a push notification with a fanfare. (4) Bayesian surprise over event-type counts for everything else. Push budget: 2-3 a day max.
all.phone_view: Card: 'Sea of Kell · Day 1,204 · 3 hearths · 38 alive'. Headline slot alternates between chemistry and language: 'FIRST: a substance 11 steps deep. They call it *kessa-thu-mar*.' Then two sparklines side by side that are the whole thesis: max assembly index, and topographic similarity of the lexicon — when the second one jumps and the first one follows two weeks later, you have SEEN culture cause technology, and no caption is needed. Then a 6-word gloss of the newest morpheme ('-mar now means: sticks to skin'). Tap → the lexicon trie, and the reaction network rendered as a graph with RAF loops highlighted. Also a LISTEN button: the sonification station (see tech) is genuinely the best passive check-in of the six ideas, because a chemistry is already a stream of discrete timed events.
all.hardware_use: The lightest of the six. The chemistry is pure integer/hash work — numpy or a 300-line Rust core does millions of reactions per second on CPU, and 64GB RAM lets you keep the entire realized reaction network resident. The GPU only does referential games: Qwen3-4B Q4_K_M with -np 8, short prompts (a property vector, a lexicon slice, 4 distractors), ~80 output tokens per exchange. A generation of 30 children x 200 exchanges = 6000 calls, ~500k tokens, which is under 30 minutes of GPU. You can run a full linguistic generation every few hours comfortably and still have the GPU idle most of the day. Realistically you could run 4-6 seas concurrently on one laptop. Haiku: the nightly chronicle plus a WEEKLY LINGUIST'S REPORT (give it the lexicon diff, the topsim numbers, and 20 example names; ask for a field-linguist's memo) — that report is the single most enjoyable output any of these six ideas produces, and it costs about 3 calls x 2k output. Total Haiku well under $0.30/day, leaving budget to run more seas.
all.input_cadence: Zero. Optional nudges: introduce a new food molecule, poison a well, split a tribe, or force a migration between seas. One genuinely fun manual lever: you can ADD a syllable to the world's phonology and see whether it gets adopted.
all.tech: Rust or numpy chemistry core with a fixed hash (xxhash, seeded per world) — determinism is non-negotiable and must be tested with a replay-from-seed check in CI. SQLite for molecules, reactions, lexicons-per-generation, teachings, deaths. RAF detection: Hordijk-Steel closure algorithm, ~200 lines, runs nightly. llama.cpp + Qwen3-4B with GBNF constraining signals to the world's phonology (so the model literally cannot emit a syllable that does not exist in this culture — a lovely use of grammars). topsim via scipy.stats.spearmanr. PWA over Tailscale + nightly GitHub Pages snapshot + ntfy. SONIFICATION: map each molecule to a timbre by hashing its string into (fundamental, harmonic profile, decay), each reaction to a note event, each hearth to a stereo position; render 24h of the day's reaction log to a 3-minute Ogg with a tiny WebAudio offline render or sox, and publish it as a podcast RSS feed the phone can subscribe to. Leave it on while you work; you will learn to hear a fermentation.
all.first_weekend: Saturday morning: the chemistry — strings, ligation, cleavage, hash-catalysis, property projections. Print a random walk of it and tune the threshold until reactions are neither dead nor exploding (this tuning IS the weekend's real work, budget 3 hours). Saturday night: pots, hunger, toxicity, 12 agents, death. Sunday: the referential game with the 4B and a bottleneck, run 5 generations, compute topographic similarity per generation, plot it. If the line goes up, you have replicated a 20-year-old cognitive-science result on your gaming laptop over a weekend, in a world where being wrong kills you. That is the delight moment and it is very achievable.
all.six_months_later: Five seas with five unrelated chemistries and five language families. A couple of hundred generations of lexicon history you can scrub through. At least one documented case of a tribe losing a starter culture and regressing, and at least one schism. The weekly linguist's memo has become the thing you look forward to. You will have added property projections twice and probably added a spatial layer so trade routes are physical.
all.honest_ceiling: The compositionality transition is a ONE-TIME event per world — expect it at week 2-6 per sea, and after it happens the language mostly just accretes vocabulary. Chemistry discovery plateaus when the tribe has exploited the shallow high-nutrition region and deeper molecules stop paying for their labor cost; realistically 2-4 months per sea. So the honest model of this project is: each sea is a 2-3 month STORY with a clear arc, and the project's longevity comes from running new seas, not from one sea deepening forever. That is a real limitation and it is also, arguably, fine — it makes each world a novel rather than a soap opera. Second risk: hash chemistry can feel meaningless. If your property projections are badly chosen the whole thing reads as noise with names on it, and no amount of LLM prose will fix that. Spend the tuning time.
all.research_notes: VERIFIED: Sayama, 'Non-Spatial Hash Chemistry as a Minimalistic Open-Ended Evolutionary System', arXiv 2404.18027 — hash-based catalysis is the cheapest known way to get an open-ended artificial chemistry, no reaction table needed. Kauffman binary polymer model + RAF theory: Hordijk & Steel's autocatalytic-set line of work (polynomial RAF detection); see also 'Autocatalytic Sets and Assembly Theory: A Toy Model Perspective', Entropy 26(9):808, mdpi.com/1099-4300/26/9/808, and 'From correlation to causation: unraveling the impact of closure on open-ended evolution within the Kauffman model' (biorxiv 2024.10.30.621154 / BioSystems 2025) — both confirm this substrate is actively used for open-ended-evolution research right now, not a dead 1990s toy. Assembly index for depth: Sharma et al., Nature 2023, arXiv 2206.02279. Iterated learning: Kirby's framework; 'Compositionality and systematicity emerge from iterated learning in deep linear networks', PNAS 2025 (doi 10.1073/pnas.2509739123); Kouwenhoven et al. 2025 — LLMs in an iterated referential game with generational transmission go from holistic to compositional; 'From Signals to Structure: How Memory Architecture Drives Language Emergence in LLM Agents', arXiv 2607.00233 — compositionality needs BOTH communication (discriminability) and compression (learnability) pressure, which tells you exactly what two pressures to build. Topographic similarity is the standard emergent-communication compositionality metric (see 'Emergent Language: A Survey and Taxonomy', arXiv 2409.02645). llama.cpp GBNF for constraining generated signals to a phonology: github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/grammars/README.md.

audit.name: Saltmark
audit.ceiling: The chemistry has no gradient, and that is the whole ballgame. Properties are fixed projections of a string under hash-based catalysis, so either the projection is hash-like — structure-to-function is white noise, an 11-step molecule is no better in expectation than a 3-step one, and NOBODY has any reason to go deep — or it is a readable projection (count of symbol A drives nutrition), in which case one degenerate optimum is found in week 1. The '3 hours of tuning' budgeted to find the middle is an open research problem, not a Saturday afternoon. Absent a structured structure-to-function map, chemistry discovery bottoms out once the shallow high-nutrition region is enumerated: 3-6 weeks per sea, not the claimed 2-4 months. RAF nesting is the one genuinely unbounded axis, but nested RAFs only MATTER if deeper products pay, which loops straight back to the gradient problem. The language side stops harder: they concede compositionality is a one-time transition per world, and over 6 legible dimensions of which 2-3 are load-bearing, the lexicon saturates within days of the transition. Honest model: each sea is a 4-8 week arc, and the project's longevity is a content pipeline, not depth.
audit.authored_content_risk: Lowest of the six on chemistry — a hash function plus ligation/cleavage is genuinely unauthored, and the reaction network will surprise its author. But MEANING is entirely authored: the six property projections are the world's whole semantics, so the interesting subspace has exactly the dimensionality the designer typed, and he already predicts 2-3 will carry all the drama. The fatal risk is elsewhere and it is a VALIDITY problem, not an authoring one: Kirby-style iterated learning requires a fresh, capacity-limited learner each generation. Here every generation is the same frozen Qwen3-4B carrying English morphology priors, prompted. Nothing is reset; the bottleneck is not at the level the theory requires. Topographic similarity will rise because a pretrained LM composes by default, and the 'compositionality transition' push notification will be measuring Qwen's prior rather than this world's cultural evolution. The headline plot — topsim jumps, assembly index follows — is confounded by construction unless he ships a null control (identical pipeline with no bottleneck; and a scrambled-meaning control).
audit.compute_honesty: Yes — the most honest of the six. Integer/hash chemistry genuinely does millions of reactions/sec on CPU; 6k short referential exchanges per generation is well under 30 minutes of GPU; RAF detection is genuinely polynomial and small; 4-6 seas concurrently is plausible. Haiku spend under $0.30/day is right. Sonification is free. No hidden datacenter anywhere in this design.
audit.semantic_risk: Highest of the six, and he half-admits it. Hash chemistry buys combinatorial novelty, not functional novelty — Sayama's actual reported result is unbounded growth in the SIZE of replicating higher-order entities, which is precisely novelty-without-meaning. Names attached to hash outputs are drivel with syllables. 'FIRST: a substance 11 steps deep, they call it kessa-thu-mar' is a meaningless headline unless depth correlates with something an agent can want. Everything downstream — trade, recipes-by-description, the linguist's memo — inherits whatever meaning the six projections carry and no more.
audit.dubious_claims: arXiv 2607.00233 EXISTS (Talebirad, Redman, Parsaee, Zaiane, 30 Jun 2026) but is materially mischaracterized: it is about MEMORY ARCHITECTURE (persistent private notebook vs stateless) in two-agent Lewis signaling games, not 'compositionality needs both discriminability and compression pressure' and not generational transmission. That claim is Kirby et al. 2015, echoed by Kouwenhoven's finding that LLMs go degenerate without compression pressure. Do not build the design's two-pressure justification on 2607.00233. PNAS 2025 (Jarvis, Klein, Rosman, Saxe; doi 10.1073/pnas.2509739123) is real, but its actual conclusion cuts AGAINST the design: iterated learning yields only 'weak systematic generalization' and requires an extremely large dataset — the opposite regime from 30 children x 200 exchanges. Sayama 2404.18027 is real (IEEE CEC 2024) but delivers unbounded growth in entity size, a weaker result than 'cheapest way to open-ended chemistry' implies. Assembly index: NP-complete to compute exactly, and contested as a selection detector (see Embertongue).
audit.one_change: Kill the hash property projections. Derive properties from a cheap STRUCTURED map — fold the string with an HP-lattice-style rule and read nutrition/toxicity/adhesion/burn off features of the folded shape. Then similar strings usually behave similarly (exploration has a gradient, and a compositional name is genuinely PREDICTIVE, which is the exact thing the whole design exists to demonstrate) while rare folds flip behaviour (real discoveries, real poisonings, real cliffs). One change; it simultaneously gives the chemistry a reason to be deep and gives the language something worth being compositional about.

all.name: Grist
all.pitch: Infinite Craft's unbounded combination space, but every verdict the LLM issues is compiled into a row of NUMBERS in a deterministic materials ledger and then never asked again — so the world is infinite in what can exist, and hard-physical in whether it helps you survive the winter. Recipes are secrets held by guilds, taught lossily, stolen, traded, and lost.
all.world: A river valley with clay, timber, stone, ore-sand, reed, hide, tallow, grain, and salt. Tiled, deterministic, hourly tick. Everything that exists is a row in the KINDS ledger: {id, name, tags[], mass_per_unit, hardness, temp_stable_c, energy_density, workability, toxicity, decay_per_day, requires_tool_hardness, era_tier}. Agents act with a small verb set — combine(a, b, method, tool) where method ∈ {heat, strike, grind, soak, ferment, twist, cut, bury, mix} — plus gather, build, eat, teach, trade, hide, spy. Survival math is entirely numeric: kcal from energy_density, tool effectiveness from hardness ratio, shelter warmth from a structure's material properties, poisoning from toxicity. The LLM never touches survival math. It only ever answers one question, and only once per question: 'what KIND results from doing this to these?'
all.invention_engine: THE COURT OF KINDS. When an agent attempts combine(a, b, method, tool): look up the triple in the verdicts table. Hit (which after two weeks is >99% of attempts) → deterministic result, zero tokens, microseconds. Miss → the attempt is queued for the Court. Overnight, the queue is adjudicated in a Batch API run: Haiku 4.5 receives a CONSTITUTION (the world's physical laws, ~700 tokens, fixed forever, cached), the two full ledger rows, the method, the tool hardness, the ambient temperature, and the current era_tier, and must return either NOTHING_HAPPENS or a new ledger row under a strict JSON schema. Then MECHANICAL GATES reject bad verdicts before they ever enter the world: mass conservation within tolerance; energy_density cannot exceed max(inputs) by more than a fixed factor; hardness cannot exceed the hardest input unless the method is heat AND an ore tag is present; era_tier cannot exceed current_max_era + 1 (this is the anti-'they invented plasma' gate, and it is essential); name must not collide, must not contain banned modern vocabulary, must be derivable from the culture's existing morphemes. One repair retry, then NOTHING_HAPPENS. A surviving verdict is compiled into the ledger and is now physics, permanently, for every agent in every future run of that world. PRECEDENT AND DRIFT: monthly, re-adjudicate a random 1% of historical verdicts with a fresh call; if the new verdict contradicts the old, the OLD ruling stands (correct engineering: determinism beats freshness) and the contradiction is logged as a heresy — a visible drift metric, and in-world flavour. THE CULTURAL LAYER, which is what makes this a civilization: a verdict entering the ledger does not mean anyone KNOWS it. Knowledge of recipe R is held by specific agents with a mastery float. Recipes are taught (lossy: mastery decay, and with probability p the taught recipe has a wrong parameter — wrong temperature, wrong duration — which produces a DIFFERENT, sometimes better, verdict, which is itself an invention channel). Guilds form endogenously: when a recipe's kcal-per-labor-hour value exceeds a threshold, holders begin refusing to teach outside kin (a two-line rule that produces guild secrecy, apprenticeship, and industrial espionage as emergent behaviour). Recipes can be stolen by observation, traded, and permanently lost. Writing, once a low-decay legible medium exists in the ledger, turns recipes into objects that can be burned, buried, and rediscovered.
all.why_unbounded: With |S| substances and |M| methods there are ~|S|^2 * |M| / 2 experiments, and |S| grows every time one succeeds — so each new kind adds ~2|S||M| new unexplored triples. The space grows superlinearly forever and Infinite Craft is the live proof that an LLM adjudicator never runs out of nameable outputs. The critical difference from Infinite Craft, and the reason this is not a novelty toy: an invention is not real because the LLM said a word, it is real because the numbers it emitted make a tribe eat more per labor-hour, and the SIM decides that. Most verdicts are useless kinds that nobody makes twice. HONEST BOTTOM: the ceiling is the model's imagination and its characteristic failure modes. Left unconstrained, an LLM adjudicator drifts toward pop-culture nouns and toward compressing 10 real steps into one magic word — Infinite Craft famously degenerates that way. The era_tier gate, the numeric conservation gates, and the morpheme-derivation naming rule are what hold it back, and they are a real, ongoing engineering burden. Also: verdict SPACE is unbounded but verdict QUALITY is not; after a few thousand kinds you will notice the model producing variations on a theme rather than new categories. That is the true ceiling and it is about taste, not tokens.
all.depth_ladder: WEEK 1: sharpened stick, fire, cooked grain, dried hide, cordage. Boring, correct, and it proves the loop. REAL RUNGS: charcoal (heat timber with a bury method — note the method set makes this discoverable rather than authored); a kiln as a BUILT structure whose material properties determine achievable temp_stable, which gates everything above; fired clay; a crucible; a copper-ish alloy once the ledger contains an ore and a flux; lime mortar; a lever/press (mass and hardness give you mechanical advantage without new physics); soap from tallow + ash-leachate (a genuinely surprising one that the Court gets right); parchment or fired tablets → WRITING → the recipe-book regime change; a guild that controls a crucible recipe and prices it; a rival tribe that reverse-engineers it from a stolen sample by attempting combinations the sample's tags suggest. WILDEST PLAUSIBLE ENDPOINT within honest gates: a water-powered mill, glass, a rudimentary chemistry of acids and salts with real numeric effects, a monetary standard emerging from the highest value-density kind, and — my favourite plausible outcome — a codified STANDARD: a written specification of a kind's parameters that lets two guilds in different towns make interchangeable parts. Standardisation is the actual hinge of industrial history and it falls naturally out of writing plus trade plus numeric tolerances.
all.what_selects: Winter, injury, disease with a seeded return period, and rival towns. Tools wear out (integrity decays with use), so a tribe must continuously reproduce its technology or fall back down the ladder — this is the single most important rule in the design, because it means technology must be MAINTAINED, not just discovered. Kcal per labor-hour is the master fitness number and it is what the phone card charts. A guild that hoards too hard gets outcompeted by a town that teaches freely and scales; a town that teaches freely gets its recipes stolen. That tension is not authored, it falls out of the numbers.
all.changing_worlds: Worlds differ by their BASE ledger — which raw kinds exist and with what numbers. A world with no ore-sand can never reach metals and will go deep on ceramics, fiber and chemistry instead, and its tech tree will look genuinely, structurally different because the Court is adjudicating from a different starting set. That is the cheapest possible way to make multiple worlds mean something and it is very strong here. Within a world: seasons, floods that destroy stored goods (destroying stored goods is how you get regression stories), a trade caravan that arrives with a foreign kind whose recipe nobody knows, and web visitors — an anonymous visitor to the public site can leave one OMEN per day, a short phrase, which is deposited in the world as a portent that biases which combinations agents try next (implemented as a prior boost over triples whose tags match the omen's embedding). Visitors are cheap non-stationarity and they will absolutely try to make the tribe invent something stupid, which is the fun.
all.novelty_detector: Four gates, ANDed down to a trickle. (1) A verdict that is not NOTHING_HAPPENS (already rare). (2) The kind gets MADE A SECOND TIME by someone other than its inventor — reproduction is the line between accident and technology, and it is exactly assembly theory's copy-number criterion. (3) The kind's introduction moves the town's kcal-per-labor-hour or winter-survival projection by more than 2% — an ECONOMICALLY significant invention. This is the best filter in any of these six designs because it is unarguable. (4) Assembly index (min steps from base ledger) exceeds the world record. Also fire on: guild formation, first theft, first written recipe, recipe extinction (last holder died), and heresy events from drift checking. Everything else goes in the log and never touches your phone. Expect 1-4 pushes a day.
all.phone_view: Card: 'Vetch Ford · Day 388 · 2 towns · 71 alive · kcal/labor-hr 4.1 ↑'. Headline: 'NEW KIND: greyglaze (assembly 7). Made twice. Winter survival +6%. Held by 3 people, all Orrin's kin — they have stopped teaching it.' Then the master sparkline: kcal per labor-hour, the one number that means 'is this civilization actually getting better'. Then a 3-row ledger diff. Then the chronicle sentence. Tap → the ledger as a searchable table (surprisingly fun to browse — it is a materials encyclopedia of a world that does not exist) and the recipe-knowledge graph showing who knows what. Second tab: THE COURT DOCKET — last night's rulings, including the rejected ones with their rejection reason. Reading the rejects is genuinely hilarious and it is free.
all.hardware_use: The local 4B does agent decision-making (what to try next, who to teach, whether to trade) with tight grammar-constrained outputs — 60-120 tokens per decision, a few thousand decisions a day, trivial for a 5070 at Q4. Optionally use the local 4B as a FIRST-PASS judge: it adjudicates the combination, and you only escalate to Haiku when the local verdict fails the mechanical gates or when the local model's logprob-confidence is low. That cuts Haiku volume by maybe 60% at the cost of a duller ledger; I would run Haiku-only for the first month to establish a good corpus of precedent, then switch to escalation. COST: the honest math. Novel adjudications actually attempted per day settle around 200-500 once the cache warms (agents only try what their culture suggests, which is a narrow beam). At 500/day via Batch API with a cached 700-token constitution: input ~500 x 1.1k = 550k @ $0.50/MTok = $0.28; output 500 x 250 = 125k @ $2.50/MTok = $0.31. Plus chronicle and drift checks: call it $0.70/day. Hard-cap it: a daily adjudication quota that, when exhausted, puts the Court IN RECESS — a diegetic rate limiter that shows on the phone as 'the Court sits again at dawn'. That is both honest engineering and good writing. GPU sits at maybe 20% duty cycle; you can run three valleys.
all.input_cadence: Zero required. The one thing worth doing occasionally (monthly, 20 minutes, and it is fun not chore-like) is reading the Court docket and editing the constitution — tightening a law because you saw a verdict you disliked. That is god-tier nudging in its purest form: you are amending physics.
all.tech: Python sim + SQLite (kinds, verdicts, recipes, holders, guilds, trades, thefts, events). Anthropic Batch API for the nightly Court (submit at 02:00, poll, compile at 06:00 — the 24h SLA is irrelevant since results typically land in minutes-to-hours and the sim just stalls those experiments until dawn, which is diegetically perfect). JSON-schema-constrained output on the Haiku side; GBNF on the local side. FastAPI + vanilla-JS PWA over Tailscale Serve, nightly static export to GitHub Pages, ntfy push. Public read-only mirror with the omen guestbook (rate-limited, moderated by a cheap classifier call). Same shared spine as the other ideas: deterministic sim + SQLite event log + novelty scorer + PWA + push.
all.first_weekend: Saturday: the ledger, the verb set, the survival math, 12 agents, hunger, winter. Hard-code 8 base kinds and ZERO recipes. Saturday night: wire the Court with a 20-line constitution and no gates yet, let it rip for 200 sim-days, and read the ledger. It will be delightful and slightly broken — that is the delight moment, day one. Sunday: add the mechanical gates and the era_tier cap, watch the ledger get sane, add the second-time-made novelty filter, and put a single card on your phone via ntfy. You will end Sunday with a world that invented something you did not author and told your phone about it.
all.six_months_later: A ledger of a few thousand kinds, of which maybe 200 are actually load-bearing technology that gets reproduced. Three valleys with structurally different tech because of different base ledgers. Guilds, at least one recipe monopoly and at least one recipe that died with its last holder in a flu winter. An omen guestbook full of strangers trying to make your tribe invent cheese. The kcal-per-labor-hour chart is a real, legible civilization curve with plateaus and jumps, and you can point at each jump and name it.
all.honest_ceiling: 2-4 months before the ledger reads as variations rather than kinds — this is the sharpest of the six ceilings and it is a taste problem, not a tokens problem. Verdict drift and the model's pull toward anachronism require active gate maintenance; budget an evening a month. The Court's numeric attributes are also only as meaningful as your survival math consumes: if hardness only matters for one thing, the LLM's careful hardness numbers are decoration. Realistically only 4-6 of the ledger's attributes will ever be load-bearing, so define those well and treat the rest as flavour. Finally: this idea is the most dependent on paid tokens of the six, so if you ever want a fully-offline run, plan the local-4B-as-judge escalation path from day one.
all.research_notes: VERIFIED: Infinite Craft's mechanism is exactly per-pair caching with LLM fallback — Arthur O'Dwyer's analysis (quuxplusone.github.io/blog/2024/02/08/infinite-craft/) confirms the backend caches every pair so the same pairing always gives the same result globally and only NEW pairings hit the model; open clones exist and are readable: github.com/bufferhead-code/opencraft, github.com/CharlesFauman/infini-craft (the latter runs a local Llama for adjudication, which is the precedent for the local-first-pass judge). Anthropic pricing verified at anthropic.com/claude/haiku: Haiku 4.5 is $1/MTok in, $5/MTok out, prompt caching up to 90% off reads, Batch API 50% off both directions and stacks with caching. llama.cpp supports JSON-schema→GBNF conversion natively and the server exposes response_format (github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/tools/server/README.md), so both judges can be schema-locked. Assembly theory's copy-number criterion (Sharma et al., Nature 2023, arXiv 2206.02279) is the formal justification for the 'made a second time' novelty gate. W. Brian Arthur, The Nature of Technology (2009) — technologies are combinations of existing technologies, and new combinations enlarge the combinable set — is the theoretical frame; Kauffman's adjacent possible is the same claim from the biology side.

audit.name: Grist
audit.ceiling: The invention space is the model's memory of human technological history, and the design has built rails to walk it in order. era_tier <= current_max_era + 1 IS a hand-authored tech tree with the node names left blank for Haiku to fill in. The listed ladder — charcoal, kiln, fired clay, crucible, alloy, lime mortar, glass, water mill — is not a prediction about the sim; it is a recitation of what the model already knows comes next, and it will emerge in that order because the gate forbids any other order. Where it stops: when the era ladder outruns what the survival math can consume. He concedes only 4-6 attributes are load-bearing, so anything whose value is mechanical power, chemistry, information or institutions has nowhere to land numerically. Ledger reads as variations at 3-8 weeks; the ECONOMICALLY significant invention rate (his own filter #3, the best filter in the batch) goes near zero well before that. Note the second authoring channel: every anachronism he dislikes becomes a new gate rule, so six months in the constitution IS the tech tree, hand-written by him one rejection at a time.
audit.authored_content_risk: Maximal, and it is exactly the failure mode named in the brief — except the author is the pretraining corpus rather than the designer. This is Wikipedia's tech tree, revealed in an order the designer constrained to be historical, then filtered for whether it helps. To be fair, the filter is real and it is the good part: kcal/labor-hour as master metric, tool wear forcing continuous REPRODUCTION of technology, guild secrecy from a two-line threshold, recipes dying with their last holder, theft and reverse-engineering. Those are the best-specified social/economic dynamics of the six and they are genuinely emergent. Just do not call the ledger discovery: it is retrieval with an economic referee.
audit.compute_honesty: Yes on tokens; the arithmetic checks out at roughly $0.60-0.70/day (~$250/yr) — cheap but the only design that stops working when payment stops. Two soft spots. (1) '200-500 novel adjudications/day once the cache warms' is an assumption, not a measurement; a curious-agent policy over |S|^2 x |M| triples can blow through it on any day the ledger jumps, and 'the Court is in recess' means the invention rate is set by a budget cap — a strange thing to have sitting in the fitness path. (2) The offline escalation path is a fiction: a 4B emitting calibrated hardness / energy_density / temp_stable_c for a novel material is producing plausible noise, and the mechanical gates check conservation, not correctness, so escalation mode silently degrades the ledger to random numbers that pass.
audit.semantic_risk: The names will be fine; the NUMBERS are the problem and this is what I would fix first. Each verdict is an independent LLM guess with no global consistency constraint. After 3,000 kinds you hold 3,000 uncalibrated hardness estimates produced in 3,000 different contexts, and the survival math takes RATIOS of them (tool hardness vs requires_tool_hardness). The ledger is not a physics, it is a scatter of vibes, and it will become quietly incoherent — tools that should work won't, soft materials will gate ore. Pairwise mass/energy gates cannot detect this class of failure, and it will look like bad luck rather than a bug.
audit.dubious_claims: Infinite Craft's per-pair caching mechanism and Haiku pricing are correct. The era_tier gate is circular: it prevents anachronism using an era label assigned by the very model whose anachronism it polices. Assembly-theory copy-number justification: the 'made a second time' heuristic is sound on its own merits, but AT's claim to distinguish selection from noise is contested (Zenil et al., PLOS Complex Systems; arXiv 2403.06629 / 2408.15108) and minimal assembly index is NP-complete — 'min steps from base ledger' is an upper bound from observed recipes. On Batch + prompt caching, Grist's note (they stack) is right and Embertongue's contradicting note is wrong.
audit.one_change: Stop letting the model emit properties. Restrict the Court's output to COMPOSITION + PROCESS — a vector over ~10 elements/phases plus temperature, duration, and mechanical work — and compute every numeric property deterministically from that composition. The ledger becomes one consistent physics, hardness ratios mean something, anachronism becomes structurally impossible (you cannot reach steel without reaching the composition, so the era gate can be deleted), the offline 4B path becomes viable because the model is only proposing a plausible composition, and the LLM is demoted from oracle to namer and chemist's-intuition proposer, which is the only job it is actually good at.

all.name: Kithmind
all.pitch: Each tribe's culture is not text — it is a QLoRA adapter, trained every week on only the trajectories that survived. Tribes diverge into genuinely different minds you can measure, teaching is weight-level distillation through a bottleneck, conquest is model merging, and a dead civilization's adapter lies in a barrow waiting to be dug up and partially remembered.
all.world: Deliberately modest and hard: a 64x64 tiled valley, hourly tick, deterministic, with a small but real survival economy — forage, hunt, store, build, keep warm, birth, teach, raid, trade. Six to ten tribes. The SYMBOLIC technology layer is borrowed wholesale from Embertongue or Grist (a growing library of named programs, or a materials ledger) — you need a visible tech tree, because weights alone are not watchable. The novel layer is the MIND. All tribes share one frozen base (Qwen3-4B-Instruct, Q4 for inference, 4-bit for training) and each tribe owns a LoRA adapter, rank 16, maybe 40MB. The adapter is queried for every non-trivial agent decision, always grammar-constrained. Two tribes in the same situation with the same knowledge will act differently, and the difference is in the weights, which is exactly what 'culture' means and is very hard to fake with prompts.
all.invention_engine: Two coupled engines. SYMBOLIC (the visible tech tree): whichever engine you borrow — library compression or the ledger — produces the named technologies. SUBCONSCIOUS (the novel part): STaR / rejection-sampling self-training with SURVIVAL as the verifier. Every week of sim time, for each tribe, collect the decision trajectories from agents who are still alive and whose tribe's stores went UP, filter to trajectories that mechanically passed (the child lived, the tool worked, the winter was survived), and QLoRA-finetune that tribe's adapter on them with Unsloth. New checkpoint must beat the old on a FROZEN held-out benchmark of 200 seeded survival scenarios, scored by sim outcome (days survived, kcal stored) — not by loss, and never by wall-clock. Fails the gate → discard, keep the ancestor, log it as 'a generation that learned nothing'. TEACHING AS DISTILLATION THROUGH A BOTTLENECK: a child tribe (a splinter settlement) does not inherit the parent adapter. It trains a fresh adapter on ONLY the transcripts the elders produced while teaching — a small, biased, deliberately incomplete sample of the parent's competence. That is iterated learning implemented at the weight level, and it guarantees generational loss and drift, which is the whole point. CONQUEST AND SYNCRETISM: when tribe A absorbs tribe B, merge the adapters (TIES-merge or DARE, weighted by population) — the resulting culture is a real hybrid with real interference artifacts, which is a much more honest model of syncretism than concatenating two prompt strings. BARROWS: when a tribe goes extinct its adapter is archived, not deleted. A later tribe that excavates the ruin gets a low-weight partial merge (alpha 0.1-0.2) — mechanically, they start doing things the old people did, without knowing why. That is archaeology and revival as a weight operation and I have not seen anyone do it.
all.why_unbounded: I will be straight with you: the WEIGHT layer is not unbounded and claiming otherwise would be dishonest. Adapter space is vast but capability on a narrow sim saturates fast. The unboundedness in this project comes from the borrowed symbolic engine (library compression, which is genuinely recursive) — the adapters supply DIVERGENCE, not depth. And divergence is genuinely combinatorial in an interesting way: with 8 tribes, a merge/split/extinct/revive lineage process over months produces a phylogeny whose branch structure never repeats, and behavioural distance between tribes on a fixed probe set is a real, growing, measurable quantity. So: unbounded in cultural PHYLOGENY, bounded in individual capability. Frame it as a culture-divergence engine and it is honest and still exciting; frame it as a capability engine and it will disappoint you by week 6.
all.depth_ladder: WEEK 1: all tribes are identical because they share the base model; the first adapter round is where it gets interesting — after one finetune the tribes are already measurably different on the probe set even though nothing in the world differed much. REAL RUNGS: measurable behavioural divergence (KL between tribe policies on 100 fixed probe states) crossing a threshold; a tribe that develops a stable BIAS you can name from behaviour alone (hoarders vs. sharers, cautious vs. exploratory) and that you did not prompt; a splinter tribe whose bottlenecked adapter is visibly a degraded, superstitious version of its parent; a merge that produces a genuinely weird hybrid; a barrow excavation that partially restores an extinct behaviour pattern; and — the deep one — a tribe whose adapter has internalised a TABOO (it reliably avoids an action that once killed many of its ancestors, even in situations where that action is now safe), which is maladaptive culture measurable as a fitness cost. WILDEST PLAUSIBLE ENDPOINT: a probe-set phylogeny with 20+ nodes that matches the historical lineage tree you never told it about; and a documented case of two tribes whose merged adapter performs WORSE than either parent, i.e. a cultural collision you can point at with numbers.
all.what_selects: Standard survival plus raiding plus the held-out benchmark gate on every adapter update. Crucially, tribes with worse adapters actually die, so weight-space selection has real teeth. Model collapse is a genuine failure mode here and it is also, mechanically, a civilizational decline story — a tribe whose training corpus became too self-similar loses behavioural diversity, stops exploring, and gets outcompeted. You can literally measure entropy of its action distribution and predict its fall.
all.changing_worlds: New valleys with different resource layouts and hazard tempos, entered by migration. The interesting bit: an adapter trained in a forest valley is measurably WRONG in a coastal one, so migration produces a visible competence crash followed by a re-training recovery, which is exactly the arc of a people arriving somewhere new. You can also do a 'dark age': hold adapter training for 20 sim-generations and watch the symbolic library and the weights decay together.
all.novelty_detector: (1) Behavioural distance jumps: nightly, run every tribe's adapter over a FIXED 200-state probe set (cheap — 200 short generations per tribe), embed the action distributions, and push when any tribe's distance from its own past self, or from the population centroid, jumps past a threshold. This is a proper, quantitative 'a culture changed' signal and it is the heart of the project. (2) Benchmark gate outcomes: pushes on 'the Weft learned nothing this generation' or 'the Kell's new mind beat its ancestor by 14%'. (3) Symbolic-layer novelty inherited from the borrowed engine (assembly index, first-ever programs). (4) Merge/split/extinction/excavation events. Push volume naturally low: maybe 1-2 a day.
all.phone_view: Card: 'Kell Valley · Day 244 · 6 tribes · 118 alive'. Headline is always a MIND event, not a world event: 'The Weft trained last night and FAILED the gate — their new mind was worse than their grandparents'. They keep the old one. Third failure running.' Below it, the one visual that carries this whole project: a small dendrogram of the six tribes by behavioural distance, drawn from last night's probe run, with branch lengths that grow over weeks — you can see cultures separating at a glance, and it is legible in three seconds. Then two numbers: population and mean kcal/labor-hour per tribe as tiny bars, plus a red dot on any tribe whose action-entropy is collapsing (the early-warning sign of a culture going rigid). Then the chronicle sentence. Tap → the full phylogeny with merges, splinters, extinctions and barrow excavations drawn as edges; tap a tribe → its probe-set fingerprint versus its ancestor, with the 5 probe states where they most disagree shown as literal quoted answers, which is the most fun screen in the project because you are reading two cultures answer the same question differently.
all.hardware_use: THIS IS THE ONE WITH REAL 8GB PAIN, and you should know it going in. Inference: base Qwen3-4B Q4 + N LoRA adapters is fine — llama.cpp supports hot-swapping LoRAs, or you keep 3-4 hot and swap the rest, ~3-4GB total. Training: Unsloth 4-bit QLoRA on a 4B fits comfortably in 8GB (their published table has 8B at ~6GB and 11B at ~7.5GB for 4-bit QLoRA), BUT you must stop the inference server during training — you cannot hold both. So the schedule is: sim runs 23h with the server up; at 04:00 the sim pauses, the server unloads, one or two tribes train for 20-40 minutes each, the gate benchmark runs, the server reloads. Round-robin so each tribe trains every 4-5 days. Blackwell sm_120 is a real install hazard: stock PyTorch wheels historically top out below sm_120 and you need the CUDA-matched wheels (uv's --torch-backend=auto, or the Blackwell-specific install path Unsloth documents) — budget an evening for this and do it BEFORE building anything else, because if it does not work the whole idea is dead. Thermals: training on a laptop at 04:00 is fine; just never let wall-clock into the fitness signal (the gate is sim outcomes, so you are safe by construction). Haiku: chronicle plus a weekly 'anthropologist's report' comparing tribes' probe-set behaviour — maybe 30 calls/day, well under $0.30.
all.input_cadence: Zero required, but this one has the highest chance of needing a rescue: if adapters collapse, you intervene. Realistically an hour every couple of weeks tuning LoRA rank, learning rate, and the trajectory filter. Be honest with yourself that this is the least chore-free of the six.
all.tech: Sim: Python + SQLite as elsewhere. Inference: llama.cpp server with LoRA hot-swap, or vLLM if you want multi-LoRA serving (tighter on 8GB — llama.cpp is the safer call). Training: Unsloth + peft, 4-bit QLoRA, rank 16, on trajectory JSONL. Merging: mergekit (TIES/DARE) or 40 lines of task-arithmetic on the LoRA deltas directly — for LoRA deltas the arithmetic is simple enough to write yourself and you will understand it better. Probe-set evaluation harness with fixed seeds. PWA + Tailscale + GitHub Pages snapshot + ntfy. Adapters and their lineage stored as files with a manifest table — the barrow is literally a directory.
all.first_weekend: Weekend 1 is an install weekend and you should accept that: get Unsloth training a 4B QLoRA on the Blackwell laptop, end to end, on toy data. Then a minimal sim (hunger, forage, winter, 2 tribes), collect 2000 decision trajectories with the base model, filter to survivors, train two DIFFERENT adapters on two tribes' data, and run both over 50 probe states. The delight moment is the diff: two minds, same base, measurably different answers to the same question, and the difference came from who survived. That is achievable in a weekend IF the install cooperates.
all.six_months_later: A phylogeny of 20-40 adapters with a real lineage tree, merges, splinters, extinctions and two or three excavations. A behavioural distance matrix you can render as a dendrogram and that actually recapitulates history. A couple of named cultural traits that emerged with no prompting. Several hundred MB of barrows. The weekly anthropologist's report is the artifact you would show someone.
all.honest_ceiling: The shortest capability ceiling of the six: a 4B self-training on a narrow sim saturates in roughly 4-8 weeks, after which the gate rejects most checkpoints and the charts flatten. What KEEPS going is divergence and phylogeny, which stays interesting for months but is a subtler pleasure than 'they invented the kiln'. Model collapse (documented as a cultural-evolution phenomenon in arXiv 2605.23054) is a live risk, not a theoretical one — expect at least one tribe to degenerate into repetitive behaviour and plan the entropy monitor from the start. Operationally this is the highest-maintenance idea and the one most likely to break on a driver update. My honest recommendation: build Embertongue or Grist FIRST, get the world working, and add Kithmind as a second-year layer on top — the adapters are much more interesting when there is already a technology tree for them to be differently good at.
all.research_notes: VERIFIED: Unsloth's published minimum-VRAM table has 8B at ~6GB and 11B at ~7.5GB for 4-bit QLoRA, so a 4B on 8GB has real headroom; their December-2025 release claims ~3x speedup and ~30% less VRAM from new Triton kernels and padding-free packing. Blackwell/sm_120 is a documented install hazard — stock stable PyTorch wheels have lagged sm_120 and installs need the CUDA-matched path (uv --torch-backend=auto or Unsloth's Blackwell section); do not assume pip install works. STaR-style rejection-sampling self-training with a mechanical verifier is the same skeleton as the builder's Ouroboros idea; the open-ended-archive framing (keep every ancestor, allow revival from the archive rather than only the current best) is from the Darwin Gödel Machine, arXiv 2505.22954, repo github.com/jennyzzt/dgm — its central empirical lesson is that the ARCHIVE plus open-ended exploration beats greedy hill-climbing, which is exactly why barrows should be revivable. Model collapse as cultural evolution: arXiv 2605.23054 — treat it as a mechanic, not just a bug. Iterated learning at the weight level (resetting/retraining a learner each generation induces easier-to-learn, more compositional representations) is supported by the PNAS 2025 deep-linear-network result (doi 10.1073/pnas.2509739123) and the LLM iterated-learning literature. Multi-agent-society precedent for emergent specialization and cultural memes: Project Sid, arXiv 2411.00114 (PIANO architecture; specialization emerged only WITH social awareness — a strong argument for making tribe minds differ).

audit.name: Kithmind
audit.ceiling: He is honest that weights are not a depth engine; I will go further and say the advertised phenomena mostly will not appear. A rank-16 LoRA finetuned on a few thousand short grammar-constrained decisions produced by its OWN base model, filtered by survival, is a weak nudge on an already-fixed policy. What gets measured after round 1 is drift — divergence driven by sampling noise in each tribe's trajectory set — and there is no specified way to distinguish that from culture. The named payoffs are the least likely parts: a 'taboo' requires state-conditional avoidance that generalizes counterfactually to newly-safe situations, which is a capability claim a 4B+LoRA on a few thousand examples will not satisfy. Hoarder-vs-sharer might appear weakly because it is a one-dimensional prior shift. His 4-8 week saturation estimate is generous; the gate will start rejecting checkpoints within 2-3 rounds, which the design cleverly reframes as 'a generation that learned nothing' — a narratively perfect way to never notice the engine has stopped. Structurally: this idea has NO invention engine, it borrows one, so it cannot answer the brief at all. It answers a narrower question (do cultures diverge measurably) rather well.
audit.authored_content_risk: Low on the mind layer — genuinely unauthored, the weights really do differ, and merge/barrow/excavation are real operations rather than prose, which is more than any prompt-based 'culture' can say. High on the READOUT layer: a nightly Haiku 'anthropologist's report' narrating probe-set diffs will manufacture compelling cultural personality out of noise every single night, and he will believe it. This is the design most at risk of self-deception, and the risk sits in the interpretation, not the mechanism.
audit.compute_honesty: The only one with real 8GB pain and he says so — credit for that. Unsized costs: the gate is 200 seeded scenarios SCORED BY SIM OUTCOME, i.e. 200 full rollouts x many LLM decisions each, per candidate checkpoint, plus a nightly 200-state probe run x 6 tribes with adapter swaps. That is plausibly more GPU-hours than the training itself and it lands inside the window when the sim is paused. Round-robin at 20-40 min/tribe means each tribe updates every 4-5 days, so ~35 generations in six months — a thin phylogeny for the dendrogram he wants. llama.cpp LoRA hot-swap works but quantized-base + adapter has quality caveats; multi-LoRA vLLM on 8GB is not realistic (he agrees). TIES/DARE over LoRA deltas from a shared base is arithmetically fine.
audit.semantic_risk: Not drivel — outputs are grammar-constrained sim decisions. The risk is the semantics of the METRIC: behavioural distance between adapters is uninterpretable without a null model. Train two adapters on random splits of the SAME tribe's data and show within-tribe distance is much smaller than between-tribe distance; without that permutation control, every number on the phone card and every line of the anthropologist's memo is unfalsifiable.
audit.dubious_claims: Blackwell sm_120 PyTorch lag is OUTDATED — CUDA 12.8 wheels have shipped sm_120 since 2025, so 'budget an evening and if it fails the idea is dead' over-weights a solved problem.
