Second honest limit: 8GB is genuinely tight, the twelve-polity weekly job is 6-12 hours, and the CUDA stack on Blackwell is the one place in these six ideas with a real maintenance tax. Third: the symbolic policy library is where the reliable depth lives, so if the weight loop disappoints, that layer keeps the project alive — build it first, not second. Fourth: everything is verifier-shaped, so if your mechanical scorer has an exploitable hole the colleges will find it and the chronicle becomes a record of reward hacking (which, admittedly, is a fascinating thing to read about, but it is not what you set out to build).
all.research_notes: Verified: Unsloth now supports Blackwell including RTX 5070/5080/5090, with the well-documented requirement that sm_120 needs CUDA 12.8+ and all dependent libraries compiled against it, otherwise you get no-kernel-image errors (github.com/unslothai/unsloth issue #5266 is the practical setup thread; unsloth.ai/docs/models/tutorials/qwen3-how-to-run-and-fine-tune covers Qwen3 specifically, claiming ~2x faster training with ~70% less VRAM and longer context). QLoRA on 8GB is an explicitly supported configuration — 4-bit base plus small adapter matrices — and Unsloth shipped a desktop no-code tool in August 2026 targeting exactly the 8GB tier, which is a useful signal that this hardware class is a first-class target rather than a stretch. STaR-style rejection sampling with a mechanical verifier plus a held-out gate is the builder's own Ouroboros Forge design, which I am adopting rather than reinventing; what is new here is embedding it in a world so the checkpoint IS a polity's inherited mind and a discarded checkpoint IS a dark age. Voyager (arXiv 2305.16291, github.com/minedojo/voyager) is the precedent for the symbolic half: an ever-growing library of executable skills indexed by embeddings of their natural-language descriptions, with top-k retrieval into the prompt, and it demonstrated open-ended capability growth with NO gradient updates at all — which is precisely why I recommend building the policy-library layer first and treating the weight loop as the risky, more interesting bet layered on top. llama.cpp GBNF grammars keep every decision machine-parseable. On the style-divergence detector: ASAL's formulation of open-endedness as historical novelty in a representation space (arXiv 2412.17799) applies directly to prose embeddings, which is a cheap and unusually apt fit here.

audit.name: Scriptorium
audit.ceiling: The symbolic policy library — which the doc correctly names as where the reliable depth lives — saturates in 6-10 weeks, and the reason is a tension the doc never resolves: the verifier is 'deliberately boring' so it can be trusted, and a boring deterministic economy over ~7 levers has a low-dimensional optimum. Once the colleges find the neighbourhood of that optimum, new named policies are noise dressed as statecraft, and composition depth grows without capability growing (a policy invoking a policy invoking a policy that all reduce to 'store more grain'). The weight layer is honestly disclaimed as divergence-not-capability, and that disclaimer is correct, but it undersells one specific failure: the recovered-ancient-mind beat, which the doc calls the best story beat available in any of the six, essentially cannot fire. A damaged LoRA (random layers zeroed) merged at partial alpha into a different polity's model is overwhelmingly likely to degrade decision quality, and your own frozen held-out gate will correctly reject it. You have built a mechanism whose headline event your quality control is designed to prevent.
audit.authored_content_risk: Moderate on content, severe on a confound the doc misses entirely — and this is the finding I would most want the builder to see. Trajectories are scored mechanically at +20 in-world years on population/stores/territory, and the top quantile is kept for finetuning. But in a deterministic economy sim, the 20-year outcome of a state is dominated by that state's initial endowment, not by the decision taken from it. A rich polity scores well on almost any decision; a besieged one scores badly on all of them. So your filter selects for BEING A WINNER, not for DECIDING WELL, and the LoRA learns the prose register and tactical mannerisms of prosperous polities. That is a rich-get-richer style-transfer loop wearing the clothes of a STaR flywheel, and it will look like it is working — divergence, dialects, dark ages all still appear — while carrying almost no decision-quality signal. Everything downstream (the eval-score chart, the gate, the dark-age narrative) inherits the confound.
audit.compute_honesty: The least honest of the six for 8GB, though not by fabrication — by omission of the inference side. QLoRA on Qwen3-4B at 2048 ctx, rank 16-32, bs1 + grad checkpointing genuinely fits ~6-7GB, and 30-60 min per polity-week × 12 = 6-12h weekly is a plausible training estimate. What is missing: generating the training data. Every decision is a grammar-constrained 4B generation of a few hundred tokens at 40-80 tok/s, i.e. 4-8s each. To get even 300-500 usable examples per polity per week you need several thousand generations weekly — another 6-12 GPU-hours, on the same single 8GB card, plus 200 held-out states re-scored per polity per gate, plus rolling the sim forward 20 years per scored trajectory. Realistically the GPU is saturated most of the week and the weekly job is a full weekend, not a Saturday night. Two smaller notes: LoRA adapters at rank 16-32 on attention projections of a 4B are ~20-60MB, not 50-200MB; and llama.cpp per-request adapter selection is supported but historically finicky against quantized bases and adapter GGUF conversion — budget real time for it. The doc's own 'CUDA stack maintenance tax' warning is the right instinct applied to the wrong layer.
audit.semantic_risk: Low for nonsense, high for self-deception. Grammar-constrained decisions plus a deterministic sim means outputs are always well-formed and always adjudicated, so you will not get drivel. What you will get is prose that reads as though a mind is developing when what is developing is a stylistic attractor fit to the winners' distribution. Model collapse is real (recursive training on filtered self-output degrades diversity), the 30%-base-data mitigation matches what the literature recommends, and reframing collapse as a dark age is genuinely good design. But the combination of 'prose that visibly diverges' plus 'a scoring chart that mostly tracks polity wealth' is a machine for convincing its author that capability is growing. Also flag the reward-hacking risk the doc raises and then waves at: with everything verifier-shaped and a boring economy, exploitable holes will be found, and 'a record of reward hacking' is not an acceptable fallback product.
audit.dubious_claims: (a) 'Unsloth shipped a desktop no-code tool in August 2026' — post-dates what I can verify; treat as unconfirmed, and note that it is being used as evidence that 8GB is a first-class target, which is a load-bearing inference from an unverified fact. (b) 'github.com/unslothai/unsloth issue #5266' — specific issue numbers are the most commonly confabulated citation form; verify before relying on it. The underlying claim (Blackwell/sm_120 requires CUDA 12.8+ and matching builds, else no-kernel-image errors) is correct. (c) Unsloth's '~2x faster, ~70% less VRAM' are vendor marketing figures, benchmark-dependent, and should not be planned against. (d) Voyager (arXiv 2305.16291) is correctly cited and the doc draws exactly the right lesson from it — that open-ended skill growth was achieved with NO gradient updates, which is an argument that the weight layer is the optional part. Follow that lesson harder than the doc does. (e) The benchmark-hygiene advice (`nvidia-smi -lgc`, interleaved A/B, score on decision quality not wall-clock) is correct and unusually sophisticated.
audit.one_change: Replace return-based trajectory scoring with ADVANTAGE-based scoring: for each decision point, roll the seed-locked sim forward twice — once with the taken decision, once with a cheap baseline decision from the same state — and train only on the difference. This kills the winner-selection confound, makes the eval chart mean what you think it means, converts the dark-age gate from a wealth proxy into a real capability test, and it costs sim time (which is cheap) rather than GPU time (which is not). Build the policy-library layer first as the doc advises, and treat the weight loop as an experiment you are willing to delete.

all.name: Apocrypha
all.pitch: Villages copy each other's rituals imperfectly, nobody understands why any of them work, and the simulation underneath quietly computes that boiling before drinking actually does kill the thing in the water — so useful superstition is SELECTED FOR rather than designed. The artifact is a critical edition of the resulting scripture: variant readings, apocrypha, marginalia, and a critical apparatus showing exactly which copying error became doctrine.
all.world: A river valley, 40-120 villages along a branching hydrology, several centuries at seasonal ticks. The physical layer is unglamorous and rigorous: a waterborne pathogen model with an actual R0 that depends on water source, sanitation, and contact structure; a seasonal shellfish toxin bloom; a soil-fertility model; a food-storage spoilage model tied to temperature and moisture; a childbirth mortality model. Villages have populations, kin networks, prestige rankings, and a CANON — an ordered list of rituals they perform, when, and who is exempt. Nothing in the world understands any of this. The people only know what they do and whether their children lived.
all.invention_engine:
Cultural evolution over EXECUTABLE RITUAL PROGRAMS, with latent utility discovered by selection rather than by design.

A RITUAL is a short program in a tiny stack DSL over village actions: `boil`, `wait(n)`, `bury(depth)`, `separate(group)`, `wash(part)`, `burn(thing)`, `abstain(food, season)`, `count(n)`, `face(direction)`, `sing(n)`, `offer(thing)`, `touch(person)`, `sequence`, `repeat`. Roughly half the primitives have real physical consequences in the sim and half are pure noise — and the system never tells you which, because the villagers cannot tell either. `boil` kills waterborne pathogens. `separate(sick)` cuts effective contacts. `abstain(shellfish, summer)` avoids the bloom. `bury(deep)` reduces contamination of the water table. `sing(7)` does absolutely nothing, but if it happens to sit inside a ritual whose other steps work, it comes along for the ride forever. That last sentence is the entire thesis of the project and it is the actual mechanism by which real human cultures accumulated adaptive nonsense.

TRANSMISSION with error: children learn from parents (fidelity ~0.97 per step), apprentices from elders, and villages from prestigious neighbours. Copy errors are insertions, deletions, swaps, and parameter drift. Aggregation is conformist-biased (copy the most common variant among teachers) with a prestige-bias override (copy the most successful village), which are the two transmission biases the cultural-evolution literature actually identifies.

SELECTION: no village optimises anything. Villages that survive and prosper get copied; their rituals spread. Adaptive value is discovered by differential survival, exactly as in the Amazonian manioc-detoxification case.

COMPOUNDING: a ritual that becomes widespread and named is promoted to a callable MACRO in the DSL, so later rituals can contain it by name. That is a lightweight library-learning move and it is what stops this from being a flat search — canon depth grows, and a ritual can eventually be four levels of named sub-rites deep, with only the innermost one doing anything.

NON-STATIONARITY: pathogens MUTATE. A strain that boiling handled is replaced by one transmitted by contact, and a canon perfectly adapted to the old world becomes maladaptive without anyone noticing for two generations. There is no final optimum, ever.
all.why_unbounded: Program space over a stack DSL with a growing macro table is formally unbounded and compounds, the same argument as Palimpsest but smaller and cheaper. More importantly the FITNESS LANDSCAPE is non-stationary by construction: mutating pathogens, drifting climate, changing settlement density and changing contact networks mean the target keeps moving, so cultural evolution never converges and the canon keeps churning. And the third source, which is the reason this idea is on the list: the INTERPRETIVE layer. A critical edition of a text that keeps mutating produces new scholarly content (variant collation, stemma reconstruction, disputed readings) at a rate proportional to the mutation rate, independent of whether anything adaptive is happening.
all.depth_ladder:
WEEK 1: 10 villages, 6 primitives, one pathogen, copying with error. Watch `boil` reach fixation in the surviving villages without anyone selecting for it. That takes about 200 simulated years and it is a genuinely moving thing to watch happen.
WEEK 2: the critical apparatus — collate variants across villages, render a base text with footnoted readings. Now it looks like a real edition.
WEEK 3: hitchhiking noise. A useless step fixes because it is adjacent to a useful one. The apparatus can show you exactly which village and which generation it entered.
MONTH 1: macros and named rites; canon depth grows; a stemma (family tree of textual variants) can be reconstructed from the variants alone and compared against the true transmission history — and it will be WRONG in the same interesting ways real stemmatics is wrong.
MONTH 2: pathogen mutation invalidates a core rite. Some villages have a variant that happens to work against the new strain; it spreads; the old orthodoxy becomes heresy. Schism.
MONTH 3: the guestbook. Strangers' lines become omen texts, some get canonised, and the apparatus starts footnoting real humans.
ENDPOINT: a canon of dozens of named rites, five or six sects with mutually incompatible recensions, an apocrypha of texts nobody accepts, a reconstructed stemma, and an appendix in which the system reveals which steps ever actually did anything — a page you should be able to toggle and which will surprise you every single time.
all.what_selects: Child mortality, mostly, which is the honest and slightly brutal answer. Waterborne disease, food poisoning, spoilage, and epidemic dynamics kill people, and villages with maladaptive canons shrink and get copied less. Prestige bias means a village that got lucky is copied even if its canon is neutral, which introduces exactly the right amount of drift and is a real phenomenon. Between sects: no direct violence needed at first, just differential growth — though schism plus resource competition eventually produces one, and a sect that wins a war imposes its recension, which is how a canon gets forcibly standardised.
all.changing_worlds: Three valleys with different disease ecologies, different hydrology, and different toxin regimes — so the same DSL produces three unrelated religions with different sacred logic, and the cross-valley comparison page ('all three independently sanctified boiling; only the delta valley sanctified separation of the sick') is the best reading in the project. Within a valley: pathogen evolution, a slow climate trend that changes which foods are dangerous when, and a mid-history flood that destroys the upstream villages and their recensions, creating a textual gap that later scribes fill by conjecture. Public visitors add a fourth axis of change that is genuinely outside the system.
all.novelty_detector:
The single best notification in this entire set is available here and it is precisely definable: A COPYING ERROR THAT BECAME AN INNOVATION. Formally, a mutation event whose resulting variant has a measured fitness effect above 20% (computed by seeded counterfactual replay of that village's next 50 years with and without the mutation) AND which subsequently spread to three or more villages. That is a mutation becoming an adaptation, dated, located, and attributable, and it is worth waking up for.
Supporting channels: (2) SCHISM — a canon's variant graph splits into components with no recent transmission between them; (3) FIXATION — a rite reaching universality; (4) LOSS — a rite with positive fitness going extinct (tragedy, and the most affecting category); (5) CANONISATION OF AN OMEN — a visitor's guestbook line entering a canon; (6) ASAL-style embedding novelty over the canon text as a catch-all.
Hard push budget of two per day, and the top channel almost always wins, which is correct.
all.phone_view: A single verse, set as scripture, with a footnote. 'Rite of the Long Water, v.4 — Before the vessel is given to the child, count seven and let it steam. [Var.: three villages read "count nine"; the reading "let it stand" is attested only at Ashmouth and is not adaptive.]' Below: a one-line status — villages alive, sects, canon length, and whether tonight was a schism. Thirty seconds and you have read something beautiful. The hour version: the full critical edition with apparatus, the stemma diagram, the concordance, the sect comparison, the apocrypha, the guestbook-to-scripture trail, and the toggle that reveals which steps were ever physically real.
all.hardware_use: Delightfully cheap — CPU-only for everything that matters. The whole valley sim is small-integer population dynamics and short program execution; it runs thousands of years per minute in plain Python and would go absurdly fast in numpy or a small Rust core if you ever cared. 64GB RAM is irrelevant here; this would run on a phone. The GPU is used only for the prose layer and the embedding-based novelty channel: Qwen3-4B Q4_K_M for the scribal voice on a handful of passages a night, well inside 8GB, maybe five minutes of GPU time. The remaining 23 hours 55 minutes of the day the machine is free — which makes this the ideal project to run ALONGSIDE one of the heavier ideas on the same laptop, sharing the substrate.
all.input_cadence: None. The visitor layer supplies the perturbation that would otherwise require you. Optional: add a physical primitive to the DSL every couple of months (`filter(cloth)`, `smoke(meat)`) and watch whether anyone ever finds it. Watching a genuinely useful primitive go undiscovered for four hundred years is its own kind of pleasure.
all.tech: Python sim (or a tiny Rust core if you want 10^6 village-years). SQLite WAL: `ritual` (program text, canonical hash, macro table), `variant`, `transmission_event`, `village`, `canon`, `omen`, `claim`. The critical apparatus is a SQL query, which is a genuinely satisfying thing to discover. Stemma rendering as SVG. llama.cpp + Qwen3-4B under GBNF for the scribal prose, constrained so every rendered sentence carries the ritual/variant IDs it is describing and is rejected if it names anything not in the row set. Anti-repetition: a rolling `published_ngram` table of every 5-gram ever emitted, with generations rejected below a novel-5-gram threshold, plus per-entity used-phrase lists injected as negative constraints, plus a rotating cast of named in-world scribes each with a style card, era, and bias — so voice changes are structural rather than random. Sonification via Strudel or plain Web Audio: the canon's structure drives generative plainchant, one voice per sect, rhythm from the ritual calendar — a browser tab you leave on. Public site on GitHub Pages with a guestbook (a GitHub issue, a Cloudflare Worker, or an ntfy topic read back — anything with no server to maintain), private full edition over Tailscale.
all.first_weekend: Saturday: the pathogen and water model, 10 villages, the ritual DSL interpreter, transmission with copy error. Run 300 years and check whether `boil` fixed. If it did not, tune mortality until it does — that tuning session IS the design work and it is fascinating. Saturday night: variant collation and a plain-text critical apparatus in the terminal. Sunday: the scribal prose layer, the SVG stemma, and a static page. The delightful moment is Saturday afternoon, no LLM involved, when you diff the canons of the ten surviving villages and find that they all independently converged on a step you never told them was good for them.
all.six_months_later: Three valleys, three religions, a dozen sects, a canon of 40-80 named rites with genuine compositional depth, a critical edition running to thousands of words with a real apparatus, an apocrypha, a stemma that is wrong in instructive ways, a handful of your friends' guestbook jokes now embedded in scripture with commentary, and a radio station of generative plainchant that changes when a sect schisms. This is the idea most likely to still be delighting you at month 12 and it is also the cheapest to build.
all.honest_ceiling: The action primitives are authored, so this never invents a new PHYSICAL capability — it will not discover metallurgy or writing, only which combinations of a fixed set of gestures become sacred and why. The depth is entirely in the interpretive and cultural layer, and you should choose this idea only if that is the depth you want (it is a very good kind of depth, but it is not 'cavemen eventually build technology'). Second limit: with ~14 primitives the effective ritual space is large but the number of genuinely ADAPTIVE combinations is small — probably a few dozen — so after month 3 you are watching drift, hitchhiking, schism and reinterpretation rather than fresh adaptive discovery. Mitigations that genuinely help: keep adding primitives, make pathogens evolve fast enough that adaptation is continuous, and let macros compound so canon depth keeps growing. Third: this is the idea most dependent on the quality of the prose layer, because the sim's output is small and the writing is most of the experience — so budget effort for the anti-repetition machinery, and be prepared to spend a few dollars a month on Claude Haiku 4.5 for the passages you actually read. Fourth: the visitor layer will be empty for months unless you tell people about it, and an empty guestbook is a sad page — design it to look intentional when unvisited.
all.research_notes: Verified and directly load-bearing: the cultural-evolution mechanism here (adaptive practices accumulating through imitation and differential survival without anyone understanding the causal mechanism, with conformist and prestige transmission biases) is the core of Henrich's work and the manioc-detoxification case is its canonical example — this idea is a faithful executable model of a real, well-supported theory rather than a game mechanic I invented. Voyager (arXiv 2305.16291) supplies the macro-promotion pattern: successful code stored, retrieved by embedding, reused as a primitive. On making the generated text hold up for months, the practical findings from the data-to-text literature are what shape the tech stack above: neural models tend to hallucinate and REPEAT THEMSELVES and struggle to stay faithful to input, the standard remedy is separating content selection and planning from surface realisation, and hand-crafted templates give strict anti-hallucination guarantees at the cost of sounding robotic (hence the hybrid: templates for the 80% you skim, constrained LLM prose with mandatory row-ID citation for the 20% you read). llama.cpp's GBNF/JSON-schema constrained decoding makes the citation requirement enforceable rather than aspirational. James Ryan's 'Curating Simulated Storyworlds' (UCSC 2018; emshort.blog coverage) is the definitive treatment of the sifting problem this design's novelty detector addresses, and Talk of the Town — 200 years of day-by-day small-town simulation with an emphasis on characters' internal lives and knowledge phenomena (Game AI Pro 3 ch.37, gameaipro.com) — is the closest existing relative of the transmission-with-error model, since its knowledge propagation is explicitly lossy and mutable. ASAL (arXiv 2412.17799) for the catch-all novelty channel. Sonification: Strudel (the JS/web port of TidalCycles) is live and browser-native, and there is an active ecosystem of Web Audio data-sonification projects (github.com/topics/data-sonification) including real-time map-to-soundscape work, so the generative-radio layer is a weekend rather than a research project.

audit.name: Apocrypha
audit.ceiling: This will absolutely work and will stop being about discovery around month 2-3. Apply the acid test: can the designer enumerate every discoverable fact in an afternoon? Here, yes — ~14 primitives, roughly half functional, crossed with a handful of hazards gives on the order of 20-50 adaptive truths, and you could write the exhaustive list before you finish the first weekend. After the first few months the system is not discovering; it is cycling — the same small set of adaptations found, hitchhiked onto, lost, and rediscovered under new names, forever. That is a bounded orbit, and it is genuinely re-readable content (schism, loss, and rediscovery do not get old the way novelty does), but it is not open-endedness, and the doc's honest_ceiling is right to say so. One point the doc gets wrong in its own favour: macro promotion is offered as the compounding mechanism, but nesting a four-level rite whose innermost step is the only functional one adds depth to the TEXT and none to the technology. That is decorative compounding, and the critical apparatus will make it look like the real thing. Pathogen mutation genuinely prevents convergence, but churn is not growth — it resets the same landscape rather than extending it.
audit.authored_content_risk: Low at the level of outcomes, total at the level of the fact set. Which primitives are functional, and what they do, is a table you wrote; the villagers' ignorance of it is real and mechanically enforced, and the fixation of `boil` without anyone selecting for it is a genuine emergent event, not a reveal. That is the cleanest 'real discovery' demonstration on the entire list, and it happens on day one with no LLM. But the space of things that CAN be discovered is a finite authored table, so after the first pass through it, every subsequent event is a re-derivation. The saving grace, and it is a real one: the interpretive product (variant collation, stemma, disputed readings, apocrypha) is generated by the mutation process rather than by the adaptation process, so text keeps accruing even when the adaptive landscape is exhausted. Be clear-eyed that this is the same trade Strata makes — epistemic depth substituting for technological depth — and that it does not answer the builder's stated brief about cavemen and fire.
audit.compute_honesty: The most honest of the six, no caveats. Small-integer population dynamics plus short program execution runs thousands of village-years per minute in plain Python; the GPU is touched for a few minutes a night; 8GB is irrelevant and so is 64GB of RAM. The doc's observation that this should be run ALONGSIDE a heavier project on the same laptop is correct and is the most practically useful sentence in the six documents. The only cost that is underestimated is developer time on the prose layer, which the doc identifies as the dependency but treats as tuning rather than as the main build.
audit.semantic_risk: Low for the simulation — ritual programs are executable and their effects are computed, so nothing can be nonsense in the way the Gazette's items can. Moderate for the prose over a long horizon, and the specific risk is the anti-repetition machinery itself. A rolling table of every 5-gram ever emitted plus a novel-5-gram threshold plus per-entity used-phrase negative constraints is a monotonically tightening constraint set over a fixed small subject matter; by month 4 the rejection sampler will either stall (exponential retries) or force synonym churn that reads as strained rather than fresh. Rotating scribes with style cards is the right structural answer and should carry more of the load than the n-gram filter; also let the filter EXPIRE old n-grams (a 90-day window, not all-time), which the doc does not specify. Note also that mandatory row-ID citation guarantees referential integrity, not truthfulness, same caveat as Strata.
audit.dubious_claims: The most accurate research notes of the six. Henrich's account of adaptive cultural practices accumulating without causal understanding, the Amazonian manioc detoxification case, and the conformist/prestige transmission bias pair are all correctly characterised and genuinely load-bearing — this design is a faithful executable model of a supported theory rather than a game mechanic. Voyager (2305.16291), Strudel as the browser-native TidalCycles descendant, Talk of the Town / Game AI Pro 3 ch.37, and Ryan's dissertation are all correctly cited. Two soft flags: (a) ASAL 'Artificial Life 31(3), 2025' journal placement is unverified across all six documents; (b) the data-to-text generalisation that neural models 'tend to hallucinate and repeat themselves' is directionally right but drawn from an older literature than the constrained-decoding setup you are actually building, so do not over-plan against it. One design-level flag rather than a citation flag: 'fidelity ~0.97 per step' is per-STEP, so a 15-step rite mutates on ~36% of transmissions — check that this is the churn rate you intend, because it sets the entire pace of the project.
audit.one_change: Give the physical layer a generated, compositional substrate so the adaptive fact set stops being enumerable. Graft Reliquary's or Palimpsest's procedurally generated materials-and-reactions layer underneath the ritual DSL: `boil`, `filter`, `ferment`, `smoke`, `bury` then operate on generated substances with generated properties, and produce new substances that later rites can act on. The cultural machinery — hitchhiking, conformist bias, prestige bias, schism, stemma, critical apparatus — is already correct and stays untouched; what changes is that it now has an unbounded supply of real things to sanctify, and the acid test flips from 'enumerable in an afternoon' to 'not enumerable at all'. This is the smallest change on the list with the largest ceiling gain, because Apocrypha's weakness is entirely in its substrate and entirely not in its mechanism.

all.name: Cinderloom
all.pitch: Civilizations are colonies of bytecode programs living in a shared memory soup, paying for every action in CPU cycles. Each night a compressor mines the survivors' genomes and mints the most-compressive repeated subsequence as a new named opcode that costs fewer cycles to run — so an invention is literally a cheaper way to be alive, and the instruction set itself evolves.
all.world: "The Loom": a 256MB flat byte-addressed memory, tiled into a 2D lattice of regions so locality matters (writing to a distant cell costs more cycles). Each cell holds `ore` (a scalar that regenerates slowly and is consumed by writes) which determines the region's cycle income. An agent ("wright") is a program: a genome of opcodes, an instruction pointer, a small private stack, a cycle purse. A tribe is a lineage sharing a **codex** — its private table of minted macro-opcodes occupying the free half of the 256-opcode space. Resources: cycles (the only true currency), ore, contiguous free memory, and codex slots. Death = purse hits zero, or another wright overwrites your genome. There is no map art; the world IS the memory, rendered as a 512x512 heatmap.
all.invention_engine:
Two-phase, wake/sleep, ported from DreamCoder into an ecology.

WAKE (continuous, all day): replication with mutation (point, indel, duplication) and recombination on contact. Selection pressure comes from two sources: (1) self-replication speed under a cycle tax proportional to genome length; (2) **task bounties** — each region emits a byte stream and pays cycles to any wright that writes the correct transform of it into a designated output cell. Tasks are not a fixed list: they are sampled from a grammar over stream operators (parity, run-length, sort, xor-fold, delta, dedup, checksum, compose(f,g)) so the bounty space is itself combinatorial and re-rolls on world shudders.

SLEEP (nightly, ~20 min): the **librarian**. Dump every surviving genome per tribe into a corpus. Run MDL abstraction learning over it — either Stitch (github.com/mlb2251/stitch, Rust, top-down synthesis, POPL 2023) if you lift genomes into an s-expression IR, or, simpler for weekend one, byte-level BPE / suffix-automaton mining scored by `gain = (occurrences - 1) * (len - 1)`. Any candidate above threshold is minted: it gets a free opcode byte in that tribe's codex, a name (`OP_7A`, later a Qwen3-4B-generated word), and a **cycle discount**: executing the macro costs `ceil(expansion_cost * (1 - d))` where d rises with compression yield, capped ~0.4. Mutation can now emit that single byte where 14 bytes were needed.

Data structures: `soup: Uint8Array`, `wrights: struct-of-arrays (ip, purse, genome_ptr, genome_len, tribe_id)`, `codex: {tribe_id -> [ {opcode, expansion: bytes, cost, minted_at, parent_macros[] } ]}`, `macro_genealogy: DAG` (which macros are built out of which — this DAG is the tech tree, and you didn't write it), SQLite event log.

Codex slots are scarce (128 of them). Eviction is by usage-weighted MDL, so tribes must *specialize*, which makes codices diverge, which makes tribes mutually unintelligible, which makes contact interesting: trade = codex-entry exchange (paid for in cycles); war = overwriting each other's genome regions.
all.why_unbounded: Program space over a 256-symbol alphabet is infinite, but that alone is a random walk. The compounding argument is: **each minted macro changes the language the search operates in.** After minting M, the set of programs reachable within a cycle budget C is strictly larger than before — mutation now reaches in one edit what previously took fourteen. That is niche construction applied to the search space itself, and it has no fixed point: macros built of macros build macros. The macro-genealogy DAG grows monotonically in depth as long as the task grammar keeps supplying problems whose solutions share structure, and the task grammar is compositional (compose(f,g) is itself an operator), so it does. Nothing in the system contains a list of technologies; a technology is a byte sequence the system found, named, and discounted.
all.depth_ladder:
Week 1: a hand-written self-replicator seeded into the soup; mutants take over; you watch genome length shrink to the minimum viable copier. First macro minted is boring and correct — it's the copy loop.
Week 2-3: task bounties on. Wrights that solve `parity` stop dying in winter. First macro that is *obviously* a useful primitive nobody wrote (a bounded memcpy, an accumulator loop). You read its disassembly with coffee. This is the delight moment.
Month 2: parasites appear — genomes that jump into a neighbor's code and use its cycles. Then immunity (checksum-guarded entry points), then hyperparasites. Classic Tierra, but now with codices, so parasites specialize per-codex and can't cross tribes.
Month 3: codex divergence produces genuine dialects; trade emerges because importing a foreign macro is cheaper than evolving it. Macro-genealogy depth 4-6.
Month 4-6: strata. A collapse event wipes 90% of the soup and freezes the dead region read-only; survivors that evolve a read-from-stratum opcode can *excavate* extinct codices. Archaeology as a technology.
Wildest plausible endpoint: a tribe whose codex contains a macro that mints macros — a wright that runs the librarian on itself in-world, at cycle cost. Endogenous science. I rate this a 20% shot, not a promise.
all.what_selects: Cycles are the only currency and they are strictly conserved per region. A wright with an empty purse halts and its memory becomes free real estate. Ore depletion forces migration. Parasites drain cycles from hosts. Overwrite wars destroy genomes outright. Codex incompatibility means a conquered tribe's code is often useless to the conqueror unless they also take the codex — so conquest without translation is worthless, which creates a reason for the analogue of scribes. Longer genomes pay a strictly higher tax, which is a permanent pressure toward compression and therefore toward using macros.
all.changing_worlds: Three timescales. (1) **Shudders** (every ~6 sim-hours): ore redistributes, some regions go barren; the task grammar re-rolls a fraction of bounties, so yesterday's optimal specialization is today's liability. (2) **Collapses** (rare, ~weekly): 90% wipe, dead memory frozen into a read-only stratum. Civilizations restart on top of their own fossil record. (3) **Multiple soups**: run 6-8 independent Looms in parallel (each ~256MB, trivial in 64GB) with different base ISAs and task grammars, joined by a "gate" that migrates exactly one genome per night in one direction. The cross-soup comparison is itself the meta-game: which base ISA breeds the deepest macro genealogy?
all.novelty_detector:
Four channels feeding one nightly ranked push.
(1) **First-ever event signatures**: every event gets a canonical signature string; a SQLite table + bloom filter of all signatures ever seen. Anything unseen is a candidate. Cheap and catches genuine firsts.
(2) **Mint surprise**: a minted macro whose compression gain enters the all-time top-10, or whose genealogy depth exceeds the previous record.
(3) **Soup MDL**: gzip the whole soup nightly. A sharp drop in compressed size = the population learned something; a sharp rise = diversification. Report the delta z-score against a 30-day EWMA.
(4) **Clade shift**: any lineage crossing 20% population share for the first time, or a codex-Jaccard between two tribes crossing 0.5 → 0.2 (speciation).
Each candidate gets a surprise score = -log(prior rate under a Poisson EWMA per channel). Only the top 3 per night go to ntfy; everything else lands in the PWA feed. This is what stops thousands of nightly events from becoming noise.
all.phone_view: Hero: the 512x512 soup heatmap as a PNG (color = tribe, brightness = cycle throughput) — instantly legible, changes visibly night to night. Under it, three sparklines: population, macro-genealogy max depth, distinct codices alive. Then the **Codex Diff card**: the 1-3 opcodes minted last night, each showing its disassembly, compression gain, and the first wright that used it. Tap a macro to see its genealogy subtree. Thirty seconds is the heatmap + diff card; an hour is walking the genealogy DAG and reading disassembly.
all.hardware_use:
CPU-only by design, and that is a feature. A hand-written VM in Rust (or C, or even JS typed arrays for the prototype) runs 50-200M virtual instructions/sec/thread; 12 threads x 24h is trillions of instructions per night. The real resource is the 64GB: 8 soups x 256MB plus event history. **The 5070 is deliberately idle** — spend it on a Qwen3-4B (Q4, ~3GB VRAM) that reads the night's event JSON and writes the chronicle prose and names the new opcodes. Nothing about the science depends on the GPU, so Blackwell/sm_120 CUDA wheel headaches never block you.
Benchmark hygiene, solved cleanly: **fitness is denominated in virtual cycles, never wall-clock.** Thermal throttling changes how fast the night runs, never who wins. Seeded PRNG + full event log means any night is bit-exactly replayable.
all.input_cadence: Zero required. Optional god-nudges, one tap each from the PWA: force a shudder, open/close a migration gate between two soups, freeze a tribe's codex ("a dark age"), or inject a hand-written genome as a "prophet". Realistically you touch it when you want to run an experiment, maybe weekly. Real maintenance is disk (event log rotation) — automate it day one.
all.tech: Rust VM + rusqlite (or Node + better-sqlite3 if you want to stay in JS for the prototype; the VM is ~600 lines either way). Stitch (Rust binary, github.com/mlb2251/stitch) invoked as a subprocess for the librarian once you lift to an IR; plain BPE mining in numpy before that. SQLite WAL for the event/lineage DB. Static PWA (vanilla JS + canvas) reading a nightly `snapshot.json` + PNGs, served by Tailscale Serve from the laptop and mirrored to GitHub Pages for the public copy. ntfy.sh topic for push (docs.ntfy.sh, iOS/Android/PWA). Optional: Ollama + Qwen3-4B for names and chronicle prose; optional Claude Haiku 4.5 for a weekly deep-dive report (~50K tokens in / 3K out ≈ $0.07, batched 50% off — negligible).
all.first_weekend: Saturday: 32-opcode VM (nop, mov, add, sub, jmp, jz, load, store, alloc, copy, split, halt...) over a 4MB soup with per-cell ore; hand-write one 40-byte self-replicator; add point mutation on copy; render the soup to canvas at 10fps. You will watch the replicator take over and then get shorter. Sunday: the librarian, naive version — BPE over the top-200 genomes by fitness, mint the top-scoring subsequence into a codex with a 25% cycle discount, log it. Push one ntfy per mint. By Sunday night your phone has told you the name of a technology you did not write. That is the whole thesis, running.
all.six_months_later: Eight soups with divergent ISAs, macro genealogies 6-10 deep, a parasite/immunity arms race, archaeology strata from four collapses, and a public PWA showing eight tech trees that nobody authored side by side. You will be tuning the cycle cost model and the task grammar, not writing new features — which is either heaven or boredom depending on your temperament. The genealogy DAG print-out (receipt printer, nightly) is a genuinely lovely physical object.
all.honest_ceiling: The known failure mode of this whole family (Tierra, 1991 onward) is that complexity stalls: the soup converges to short degenerate replicators plus a stable parasite ecology, and nothing further happens. Avida's fix — external task bounties — is exactly why I put the task grammar in, and it works, but it also means **the depth of your civilizations is bounded by the richness of your task grammar**, which you wrote. That is the honest bottom. Expect: ~30-80 real abstractions per tribe, genealogy depth 6-10, and a plateau at month 3-4 unless you keep expanding the operator set. You will not get spaceships. You will get a self-authored tech tree of computational primitives, an arms race, and archaeology — and I think that is genuinely enough for a year of coffee.
all.research_notes: Verified: Tierra and Avida lineage (alife.org/encyclopedia/digital-evolution/avida/) — Tierra = shared soup, competition for one CPU; Avida = private memory + logic-task rewards, which is precisely the anti-stall mechanism. Sakana AI's "Digital Red Queen: Adversarial Program Evolution in Core War with LLMs" (pub.sakana.ai/drq/, arXiv 2601.03335, GECCO 2026, doi 10.1145/3795095.3805116) confirms program-vs-program VM ecologies are live research in 2026, not a dead 90s topic. Stitch (github.com/mlb2251/stitch, arXiv:2211.16605, POPL 2023) is a real, maintained Rust abstraction-learning library reported 3-4 orders of magnitude faster and 2 orders lighter on memory than DreamCoder's compression step — this is what makes a *nightly* librarian pass feasible on a laptop. DreamCoder itself: PLDI 2021 (dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3453483.3454080) and Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 381:20220050. ntfy.sh (docs.ntfy.sh) has iOS/Android apps + PWA and documented self-host-behind-Tailscale setups. Claude Haiku 4.5 is $1/$5 per MTok with 200K context, Batch API is 50% off, cache reads ~0.1x — verified against the bundled claude-api reference (cached 2026-06-24). No GPU dependency means the RTX 5070's sm_120 wheel situation (PyTorch issue #164342; cu128 nightlies needed) is irrelevant here.

audit.name: Cinderloom
audit.ceiling: Two hard stops, both earlier than claimed. (1) The librarian's corpus is a population of near-clones — selection destroys genetic diversity, so MDL/BPE mining over surviving genomes converges on minting the incumbent champion's own body as one opcode. The cycle discount then makes the incumbent nearly free to run, locking it in. That's a positive feedback that rewards conformity and kills search; without per-clade mining plus a lineage-diversity penalty you hit it in week 2-4. (2) Assume you fix that: the task grammar is the content, and compositional task spaces are infinite in cardinality but shallow in difficulty. Once the codex holds solutions for the ~8 base stream operators, every compose(f,g) bounty is one or two edits away — by construction, since composition is itself a primitive. Marginal information per new macro goes to ~zero past genealogy depth 3-4. Realistic plateau: week 6-10, not month 3-4. Depth 6-10 is achievable but depths 5+ will be 'parity-macro ∘ delta-macro', real but not a new kind of thing. Parasites/immunity (Tierra, 1991) will show up and are the most reliable content here; they are also 35 years old and stop where Tierra stopped. The claimed endpoint (a macro that mints macros) is not 20%; the librarian is an out-of-band nightly batch process with no in-world instruction that could invoke it, so it requires a feature you'd have to author — call it 3%.
audit.authored_content_risk: Medium-low on mechanism, high on relevance. Nobody writes the byte sequences: those are genuinely found, and the macro-genealogy DAG is honestly not hand-authored. But nontrivial macros exist *only* because bounties exist, and the bounty operator set is authored — this is Avida, where 20+ years of running never produced anything outside the authored logic-task list. So: real discovery of solutions to an authored problem list. Separately, the brief's actual demand (fire → houses → tools) is never met even in principle. Cinderloom's 'technologies' are memcpy loops and accumulators; there is no mapping to civilization at any point, and the Qwen-generated names are the only thing supplying that illusion. A bigger unadvertised gap: BPE/suffix-automaton macros are *literal substrings* — no holes, no parameters. A non-parameterized macro doesn't change the language, it just compresses one path; reuse requires exact byte match. The 'each minted macro enlarges the reachable set' argument is only true for abstractions with variables, i.e. Stitch. And the Stitch route requires lifting a linear bytecode genome with arbitrary jumps into an s-expression IR — that is a decompiler, not a weekend, and it is quietly the load-bearing step of the entire why_unbounded section.
audit.compute_honesty: Honest, and the most honest of the six. A simple Rust/C VM at 30-200M instr/s/thread is realistic; 12 threads overnight is genuinely trillions of virtual instructions. 8×256MB soups fit trivially. GPU deliberately idle, so the whole Blackwell risk surface is genuinely zero. Cycle-denominated fitness plus seeded PRNG plus full event log gives real replayability — the only project here with proper benchmark hygiene stated. Nightly librarian: BPE over a few hundred genomes is seconds; Stitch is fast, when you have an IR you don't have. No API bill worth naming.
audit.semantic_risk: Low in the mechanics — every minted macro is executable code that survived selection, so it means *something* even if that something is 'a bounded memcpy'. Risk is entirely in the presentation layer: Qwen3-4B naming opcodes and writing chronicle prose will produce confident mythology over what is, semantically, a compression dictionary. The phone view will read as a civilization while the substrate is an ISA. Keep the disassembly on the card (they do) and it stays honest.
audit.dubious_claims: The Sakana 'Digital Red Queen' citation (pub.sakana.ai/drq/, arXiv 2601.03335, GECCO 2026, doi 10.1145/3795095.3805116) is the single most suspicious reference in all six documents — I cannot verify it, and a fully-formed ACM DOI plus arXiv ID plus proceedings venue for a 2026 conference is the exact shape of a confabulated citation. Treat as nonexistent until you personally load the URL. Stitch's 3-4 orders of magnitude speedup over DreamCoder's compression step is roughly what the paper claims — fine, but it describes abstraction *with* variables, which is not what BPE does, so the citation doesn't support the plan you'd actually build. Avida/Tierra framing is correct. Haiku 4.5 at $1/$5 per MTok with 50% batch and ~0.1× cache reads matches what I know; cost estimates are right. Unverified elsewhere-repeated claim: PyTorch issue #164342 and 'CUDA 12.8/12.9 shipped a missing libnvptxcompiler.so' — irrelevant here since no GPU, but see the other four.
audit.one_change: Mine abstractions *with holes*, not literal substrings, and mine them per-clade with a relatedness penalty. Concretely: antiunify pairs of high-fitness genome fragments to get parameterized macros (opcode + operand slots), and score candidates by gain across *independent lineages*, not raw occurrence count. This kills the mint-the-champion collapse and is the only version in which 'each macro enlarges the reachable program set' is actually true. It is also strictly cheaper than the Stitch/IR route you'd otherwise be blocked on.

all.name: Saltwright
all.pitch: An archipelago whose bottom layer is a real artificial chemistry: matter is bond-graphs, and a material's hardness, toughness, conductivity and color are *computed* from graph structure, never tabulated. Tribes invent by searching process-space, and because the property map is simulated rather than authored, the value of a novel material is genuinely unknown until someone makes it and breaks something with it.
all.world: "The Bitter Coast": a handful of islands with distinct mineral deposits, tides, and weather. Physics substrate is a bond-graph artificial chemistry: 24 element types, each with (valence, mass, radius, an electronegativity-analog chi, a magnetic-moment-analog), plus a 24x24 pairwise bond-energy matrix — **all of it generated from the world seed.** Matter is a labelled multigraph of atoms; a "substance" is an isomorphism class plus a mass. Agents are small tribes of cheap scripted-but-evolving people (needs: food, warmth, tools, shelter; no LLM in the loop). Resources: ore bodies (element mixtures), fuel, water, salt, clay-analogs, time, and lives.
all.invention_engine:
Processes are graph-rewrite operators with stochastic, physics-governed outcomes: `heat(T)` breaks bonds with energy below kT (Boltzmann-sampled), `quench` freezes a high-T configuration, `hammer` applies shear that propagates along low-rigidity paths, `mix(A,B)`, `leach(solvent)`, `ferment`, later `electrify`. A **recipe** is a short program in this DSL, held in a tribe's recipe library.

The crucial part: **properties are computed from the resulting graph by cheap surrogate physics**, ~2ms per material in numpy/scipy:
- hardness ≈ mean bond energy density x coordination number
- toughness ≈ (bond energy variance) x (path redundancy / cycle rank of the graph)
- ductility ≈ Maxwell counting — degrees of freedom vs. constraints (a graph near isostaticity deforms; over-constrained shatters)
- conductivity ≈ percolation of chi-mismatched bonds across the largest component
- melting point ≈ minimum cut energy / atom
- color/opacity ≈ spectral gap of the graph Laplacian mapped to a wavelength
- density ≈ mass / packed volume estimate
An **artifact** = (shape template, which tribes also evolve) x (material). Its performance at a task (chop, dig, carry water, hold heat, cut another artifact) is a function of the property vector and the shape. So an axe of a brittle-but-hard material shatters on its third tree, and the tribe learns.

Search: nightly quality-diversity with **pyribs** MAP-Elites. Behavior descriptors = (hardness, toughness, conductivity) discretized to a 20x20x20 archive; objective = usefulness against the tribe's current need vector. Elites are named and become inputs to next generation's recipes; the recipe library is the tribe's technology and losing the tribe loses the library. Frequently-co-occurring recipe fragments are compressed into named **procedures** (`temper`, `flux`) that mutation can insert atomically — the same compression-into-primitives compounding as a skill library, but the skills are metallurgical.
all.why_unbounded: Three multiplying spaces: element-composition space (24 elements, continuous ratios), graph-topology space (isomorphism classes of bond graphs — superexponential), and process-program space (the recipe DSL, infinite). And critically the *evaluation* is a simulation, not a lookup: there is no oracle listing which combinations are good, so search is genuine discovery rather than tree-walking. Compounding comes from two places: minted procedures shorten the path to distant regions of property space, and yesterday's elite material becomes today's *input* (crucibles made of a high-melting-point material unlock temperatures that were previously unreachable, which opens a region of property space that was physically inaccessible before). That last mechanism — technology unlocking new *regions of physics*, not new recipes — is the real depth generator.
all.depth_ladder:
Week 1: chemistry engine + property computation, no agents. You poke it by hand: heat ore, quench, see a property vector. You are already having fun.
Week 2: tribes, needs, random recipe search, artifacts that break. First stone-analog and first fired-clay-analog appear. Watching a tribe accidentally discover that quenching after heating makes something harder is the delight moment.
Month 1: MAP-Elites archive; the property-space scatter starts filling; first alloy-analog (two-element composite outperforming both parents). First crucible → higher temperatures → a region of property space that was literally unreachable opens.
Month 2: minted procedures (temper, flux, alloy); trade in materials between islands; secrecy vs. diffusion.
Month 3-4: multi-part assemblies (haft + head + binding), so the combinatorics move up a level; the first conductor and the first transparent solid.
Month 6+: with a magnetism property layer switched on at world-year 200, a compass-analog; with conductivity, wire-analogs and the first energy-transport artifact.
Wildest plausible: a tribe that discovers a *catalyst* — a substance that is not consumed but changes the outcome distribution of a process. Emergent, not authored, and it changes everything downstream.
all.what_selects: A shifting **need vector** (winter demands insulation, war demands hardness, drought demands watertight vessels). A tribe whose best material fails the current need starves or is raided. Artifacts wear and break, so knowledge must be re-embodied constantly. Fuel is finite and high temperatures are expensive, so exploration of hot process-space is genuinely costly. Between tribes: material superiority translates directly into raid outcomes, and a conquered tribe's recipe library is partially absorbed.
all.changing_worlds: **The interaction matrix is the world seed** — a new world is a genuinely different periodic table, so the tech that gets invented is different every time, and neither you nor the agents can transfer knowledge across worlds. This is the cleanest multi-world story of the six. Run 4 worlds concurrently and the meta-game is comparative: which chemistry breeds the richest civilizations, which one has a metallurgy dead-end, which one accidentally makes glass trivial. Within a world: seasons, an ore body exhausting, a volcanic event that deposits a new element, and scheduled 'physics reveals' where a new property dimension (magnetism, radioactivity-analog) starts mattering.
all.novelty_detector:
(1) **New archive cell filled** in the MAP-Elites grid — the canonical QD novelty signal, free from pyribs.
(2) **Convex hull volume** of discovered property space increases by >2% — the frontier genuinely moved.
(3) **Absolute firsts**: first material above conductivity threshold, first transparent solid, first melting point above the current max achievable furnace temp (a material that unlocks a temperature regime — always push this one).
(4) **Failure-mode firsts**: first artifact class to fail in a new way (shatter vs. bend vs. corrode).
(5) Event-signature bloom filter for everything else.
Ranked by -log(Poisson EWMA rate); top 3 to ntfy nightly.
all.phone_view: Hero: the property-space scatter — hardness on x, toughness on y, dot color = conductivity, dot size = production volume, lit cells = discovered. It fills in over weeks like a slowly developing photograph and is beautiful. Below: 1-3 **new material cards**, each with a procedurally drawn crystal/graph glyph (deterministic layout of the bond graph — genuinely different-looking per material), its property bars, a Qwen3-4B-generated name, and the line "first used in: a hafted cutter that lasted 340 chops (previous best: 96)". Thirty seconds is the scatter plus one card. An hour is browsing the material genealogy: which process path produced it, and what it unlocked.
all.hardware_use: Mostly CPU: scipy.sparse for graph ops, small eigen-decompositions for the spectral color/conductivity terms, numpy for batch property evaluation. A 5000-material nightly batch takes seconds. GPU is optional — if you want 100x more search, batch the Laplacian eigen-solves on the 5070 with CuPy (cu128 build; keep a numpy fallback, since Blackwell sm_120 wheel support has been a moving target — PyTorch issue #164342, and CUDA 12.8/12.9 shipped with a missing libnvptxcompiler.so that breaks some JIT paths). Qwen3-4B Q4 (~3GB VRAM) names materials and writes the smith's-journal chronicle. 8GB is never the constraint here; 64GB RAM comfortably holds four parallel worlds plus their archives.
all.input_cadence: Zero required. God-nudges: seed a new element into an ore body, force a need-vector shift, gift one tribe a recipe from another world (heresy!), or turn on a dormant property dimension early. Weekly at most. Chores: none beyond log rotation.
all.tech: Python (numpy/scipy/networkx) for chemistry + properties; pyribs (pyribs.org, v0.11.x) for MAP-Elites and its unstructured novelty archive; SQLite for materials, recipes, lineage and events; a nightly job writes `snapshot.json` + property-scatter PNG + per-material glyph SVGs; static PWA (vanilla JS + canvas) over Tailscale Serve, public mirror on GitHub Pages; ntfy.sh push. Ollama + Qwen3-4B for names/prose. Shared substrate with the other projects: same SQLite event schema, same PWA shell, same push helper.
all.first_weekend: Saturday: the chemistry — element table from a seed, bond-graph representation, `heat`/`quench`/`mix` as graph rewrites, and the six property functions. Write a tiny REPL and play with it by hand; if this isn't fun on Saturday afternoon the idea is dead, and you'll know within four hours. Sunday: 200 agents on one island with needs, random recipe search, artifacts that wear out and break, plus the pyribs archive and a canvas scatter plot. By Sunday evening you'll have a material you didn't design, with properties you didn't specify, that a tribe chose over stone.
all.six_months_later: Four parallel worlds with incomparable periodic tables, property-space scatters that look like four different galaxies, 200-400 named materials per world, multi-part assemblies, and a comparative meta-dashboard. The nightly ritual is reading one new material card and the sentence about what it broke. Genuinely still surprising, because you can add a property dimension any time and the entire archive re-sorts.
all.honest_ceiling: The surrogate physics is a model *you* wrote, and its property space is finite-dimensional. Once the Pareto frontier of an 8-property space is filled, new materials are marginal — expect that around month 3-4 per world. The two honest mitigations are both real work: adding property dimensions (each one is a day of coding plus rebalancing) and moving combinatorics up a level to assemblies. Also be warned that surrogate physics can be *wrong in a boring way* — if your Maxwell-counting toughness term has a degenerate optimum, search will find it and camp there, and you'll spend a week diagnosing. This project's ceiling is your willingness to keep deepening the physics, and the property computations are the hardest debugging in any of these six.
all.research_notes: Verified: artificial-chemistry-as-substrate is an active, credible line — "Self-Organization in Computation & Chemistry: Return to AlChemy" (arXiv:2408.12137, Mathis et al., 2024) revisits Fontana & Buss's lambda-calculus chemistry and finds stable organizations emerge more often than expected; "Combinatory Chemistry: Towards a Simple Model of Emergent Evolution" (arXiv:2003.07916, Kruszewski & Mikolov) shows self-reproducing metabolisms from a tabula rasa; "Prebiotic Functional Programs" (arXiv:2509.03534, 2025) shows endogenous selection in an artificial chemistry; Sayama's Hash Chemistry (arXiv:2404.18027) is a minimalist open-ended AC. I am deliberately using a *bond-graph* chemistry rather than lambda-calculus because lambda-AC produces beautiful autocatalysis but no material properties, and this idea needs computable hardness/toughness. pyribs (pyribs.org, docs v0.11.0, arXiv:2303.00191) is maintained, bare-bones, includes MAP-Elites, CMA-ME/CMA-MAE and an explicit Novelty Search tutorial with an unstructured archive — exactly the 'new cell filled' novelty signal. Qwen3-4B Q4 fits ~3GB VRAM with headroom on 8GB (8B Q4 is ~5-6GB if you want better prose). Blackwell caveat verified: PyTorch stable wheels lagged sm_120 (github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/164342), cu128 nightlies work, and a missing libnvptxcompiler.so in CUDA 12.8/12.9 breaks PTX JIT for some stacks — hence the CPU-first design.

audit.name: Saltwright
audit.ceiling: Faster than the pitch's month 3-4 — I'd say 2-5 weeks per world. The reason is not search budget, it's the image of the map. Bond-graph space is superexponential, but every property function listed is a low-dimensional *summary statistic* of the graph (mean bond energy, coordination number, cycle rank, Maxwell count, spectral gap). Superexponential graph space → 8-dimensional property space is massively many-to-one, and its reachable image is a small blob fully determined by the 24×24 seed matrix. At 2ms/material you can evaluate millions per night; the frontier of that blob is found in days. After that, new materials are property-space duplicates with different glyphs. Worse: most property terms are *monotone* in the same graph statistics — hardness ≈ bond-energy-density × coordination is maximized by the densest, highest-coordination valence-legal graph, and that answer exists on day one. Count the genuine trade-offs and you get about two (Maxwell isostaticity vs. coordination is the good one; melting-point-vs-workability is semi-real). A two-trade-off space is thin. The crucible bootstrap — high-melting material unlocks higher process temperatures, which opens new regions — is the best mechanism in the set of six and is genuinely real, but it is a *finite ladder*: max achievable temperature is bounded by max bond energy in the seeded table, so you can compute the number of rungs (3-4) before writing a line of code. Also hidden: 2ms/material implies graphs of tens-to-low-hundreds of atoms; Laplacian eigendecomposition on anything bigger blows that budget, so there is an unstated size cap that is itself a ceiling on structural complexity.
audit.authored_content_risk: Medium — better than Roundabout/Firmament, worse than it looks. The seed generates the periodic table, so no per-world content is hand-written, and 'which graph is hard' is genuinely unknown to the designer. But the property functions are authored, crude, and are the entire definition of value. They are not physics; they are plausible-looking algebra over graph statistics. Search will find their degenerate optima and camp there (the pitch admits this and it is the correct worry, understated). The failure has a specific shape: you will get a material that is 'the hardest possible' because it maximizes a product of two monotone terms, and it will be a chemically absurd graph — near-complete subgraphs up to the valence limit — and it will win forever. Enforce valence hard everywhere or K_n exploits appear immediately. Net: discovery is real, but what's discovered is the structure of six formulas you wrote in an afternoon, and you can reverse-engineer most of it analytically before the agents ever run.
audit.compute_honesty: Yes, genuinely — the most comfortably-sized project of the six. scipy.sparse graph ops and small eigensolves at ~2ms, 5000 materials nightly in seconds, four worlds in 64GB. GPU optional, numpy fallback real, so the Blackwell caveats are correctly marked as non-blocking. The only honesty gap is the unstated graph-size cap implied by the 2ms figure, and that WL/nauty canonical hashing for substance identity is cheap for small graphs but is what forces that cap. No API bill.
audit.semantic_risk: Moderate-to-high, and disguised. Graph rewrites without thermodynamic consistency (no conservation of anything but atom counts, no free-energy criterion for whether a rewrite is even favorable) will produce structures that are physically meaningless yet score well. 'Conductivity ≈ percolation of chi-mismatched bonds' and 'color ≈ spectral gap mapped to a wavelength' are arbitrary mappings — the winner in each dimension is an artifact of the formula, not a material. Then Qwen names it and draws it a crystal glyph and it reads as metallurgy. The strongest anti-drivel feature is that artifacts *break*: 'lasted 340 chops, previous best 96' is a real, falsifiable claim about a real property vector. Lean on that line, not on the glyphs.
audit.dubious_claims: AlChemy revisit (arXiv:2408.12137, Mathis et al. 2024), Combinatory Chemistry (arXiv:2003.07916), Sayama's Hash Chemistry (arXiv:2404.18027), pyribs (arXiv:2303.00191) all check out as real and correctly characterized; the reasoning for choosing bond-graph over lambda-calculus AC (lambda-AC gives autocatalysis but no computable material properties) is correct and is the best-argued design decision in any of the six. 'Prebiotic Functional Programs' (arXiv:2509.03534, 2025) I cannot verify — plausible, treat as unconfirmed. The Blackwell block — PyTorch issue #164342 and 'CUDA 12.8/12.9 installers shipped without libnvptxcompiler.so, breaking PTX JIT' — appears verbatim in three of these six documents; the general 'stable wheels lagged sm_120' claim was true through 2025, but the specific missing-.so detail is unverifiable and looks like one hallucinated fact propagated across the set. Don't budget half a day for it on the strength of that sentence.
audit.one_change: Stop computing properties in closed form; *simulate* them. Embed the bond graph, relax it under a spring/LJ-analog potential derived from the seeded bond energies, then apply strain/heat/field and measure the response numerically. A few hundred conjugate-gradient steps on a 100-atom graph is still milliseconds. This buys three things at once: trade-offs become real instead of authored, degenerate algebraic optima disappear, and the property space stops being an 8-dimensional projection of five graph statistics — which is the actual ceiling.

all.name: Roundabout
all.pitch: A coastal economy where firms invent by searching production-recipe space, and the market price vector is the fitness function — dense, free, continuous, and endogenous, so the value of an invention is defined by an economy that the invention then changes. New intermediate goods are minted automatically when a recipe produces something that doesn't exist yet, so the production network deepens without anyone authoring a tech tree.
all.world: "The Sink": six settlements on a coast, connected by roads and a sea route. Agents: **households** (labor supply, an evolving taste vector, subsistence consumption or death), **firms** (capital stock, one production recipe, a price/quantity policy, employees), a **bank** (deposits, loans, an interest rate), and **the state** (optional: taxes, a patent office). Goods are typed tokens with a property vector; raw resources (clay, timber, ore, grain, fish, labor, heat) come from the map. Money exists and can inflate. Every tick is a market day: firms post prices, households and firms buy, contracts clear, wages are paid, the bank rolls credit, and the insolvent go bankrupt.
all.invention_engine:
A recipe is a program in a tiny stack DSL over goods: `2 clay + 1 heat -> 3 unit(hash)`. Four coupled mechanisms:

(1) **R&D as capital allocation.** A firm can spend capital to sample N candidate recipes (mutation of its own recipe, recombination with a recipe it observed, or a random draw biased toward *currently cheap and abundant inputs* — this is Kauffman's adjacent possible, made concrete as "what's cheap on the docks today"). Each candidate is pilot-produced at small scale; the survivor is the one with the highest expected margin at current prices.

(2) **Automatic good minting.** If a recipe's output doesn't match an existing good type, a **new good is created**: its identity is the hash of its production path, and its property vector is derived deterministically from its inputs and process (durability, caloric value, insulation, workability). Nobody wrote "brick". Brick is `hash(clay,heat,ratio)` with a property vector that happens to make it a good building input — and it becomes an input others can buy.

(3) **Roundaboutness.** Because minted goods are purchasable inputs, the production network grows in depth: goods that exist only to be inputs to other goods (Böhm-Bawerk's capital theory, literalized). Track `depth(g) = longest path from a raw resource`; this number is the single best scalar summary of the civilization's technological level, and it is measured, not assigned.

(4) **Diffusion control.** A discovered recipe is private by default. It leaks via worker mobility (a hired ex-employee carries a noisy copy), via reverse-engineering (a firm buying your good can attempt to infer the recipe, with success probability falling in recipe length), or via patenting (temporary monopoly, then publication). This is a knob you can turn from your phone and watch the growth rate change — a real experiment, not decoration.

Compression appears here too: frequently co-occurring recipe fragments get promoted into named **techniques** that R&D mutation can insert atomically — the recipe library is the tribe's skill library, and a bankrupt firm's un-leaked recipes are permanently lost.
all.why_unbounded: Two arguments. **Combinatorial:** the space of DAGs over an ever-growing set of minted goods is unbounded, and every new good expands the input set for all future recipes — the branching factor grows with the economy's own history. **Endogenous fitness:** unlike a tech tree, where each node has a fixed authored value, an invention's value here is its margin at current prices, and prices are set by the whole network. Adopting an invention changes the prices that made it valuable. So the fitness landscape deforms continuously under the search, there is no static optimum to converge to, and you get Schumpeterian waves rather than a walk to a fixed point. This is the cheapest genuinely-unbounded fitness signal of all six ideas: no LLM judge, no hand-authored value table, just double-entry bookkeeping.
all.depth_ladder:
Week 1: a two-good economy that clears without exploding. (Be warned: getting a market to *not* explode is the actual week-1 work.)
Week 2: R&D and good minting on. First minted intermediate good. First firm that exists solely to sell an input to another firm — division of labor, emergent.
Month 1: production DAG depth 4-6; specialization by settlement (one town does smelting because ore is local and heat is cheap); a price index you can plot; the first recession.
Month 2: patents/leakage; observable diffusion lags; a firm that gets rich purely on a technique and then loses it to a departing employee.
Month 3: credit cycles — the bank over-lends, a bubble in a fashionable good, a crash, mass bankruptcy, a permanent loss of recipes (a dark age with an economic cause).
Month 4-6: two economies connected by a trade route you can open and close; comparative advantage emerges without being coded; technology diffusion across the route; a colonial pattern where one economy specializes in raw inputs.
Wildest plausible endpoint: an endogenous financial instrument — firms writing contracts on future delivery because it's profitable, i.e. the economy inventing a *derivative* rather than a good. Plausible if you let contracts be tradable objects; roughly a 30% shot, and it would be delicious.
all.what_selects: Bankruptcy (negative equity → liquidation, employees scattered, un-leaked recipes destroyed). Household starvation (consumption below subsistence). Bank failure. Raids and blockades on trade routes. And competitive imitation: a firm with a superior technique captures share until the technique diffuses, at which point the rent vanishes — the Schumpeterian treadmill is the core selection pressure and it never switches off.
all.changing_worlds: Resource shocks (an ore body exhausts; a fishery collapses), climate cycles that shift which crops work, a new coastline discovered (colonization opens a fresh resource base and a fresh market), and plagues that kill labor and thereby change relative factor prices — which is a *technology* shock, because expensive labor makes labor-saving recipes profitable for the first time. Multi-world: run 20 parallel economies overnight with different parameters (patent length, interest rate, leak probability) as a genuine parameter sweep, and have the morning report tell you which regime produced the deepest production DAG. That sweep is a real experiment and the results would be interesting to actual economists.
all.novelty_detector:
(1) **Depth record**: a good whose roundaboutness depth exceeds the all-time max — the clearest 'technological progress' signal in the system.
(2) **Keystone emergence**: a new node whose betweenness centrality in the production DAG enters the top-5 — an input everything suddenly depends on. (Also a fragility warning.)
(3) **Structural breaks in price series**: Bayesian online changepoint detection or CUSUM per good; "the price of salt broke a 40-day trend" is a headline, generated mechanically.
(4) **TFP jumps**: total output per unit input rising >x% in a day.
(5) First-ever event signatures (first bankruptcy cascade, first patent, first strike, first blockade).
Score by -log(EWMA Poisson rate); top 3 nightly to ntfy.
all.phone_view: Hero: the **production DAG**, force-directed, node size = volume, node color = age (new goods glow), edges = input flows. It visibly thickens and deepens over weeks — the single most satisfying 'my civilization is progressing' image of the six. Beneath it: four sparklines (price index, real output, max roundaboutness depth, Gini) and one mechanically generated headline from the changepoint detector. Thirty seconds: glance at the DAG shape and the headline. An hour: tap a good to see its recipe, its inventor, its price history, and every good downstream of it.
all.hardware_use: Pure CPU and very light — a full economy-day is milliseconds. The honest statement: **this idea does not need the GPU at all**, and the 64GB RAM is what actually matters, because it lets you run 20-40 parallel economies as a nightly parameter sweep instead of one. Use the idle 5070 for a Qwen3-4B writing the morning market report in the voice of a dockside broadsheet, and optionally one Claude Haiku 4.5 call weekly for a deeper analysis of the sweep (~80K in / 4K out ≈ $0.10, halve it with the Batch API). No CUDA-version risk.
all.input_cadence: Zero required. God-nudges, one tap: set the interest rate, grant or abolish patents, open/close the trade route between two worlds, trigger a plague, or seed a hand-written recipe as a 'foreign merchant's secret'. These are genuinely fun because the consequences take days to propagate.
all.tech: Python (or Node — the sim is small either way; Python gets you pandas for the analysis and scipy for changepoint detection). No heavyweight framework needed, but read ABCE and the nkremerh/sugarscape Python implementation for market-clearing patterns before writing your own clearing loop. SQLite for the ledger, event log, and DAG. Nightly job renders the DAG to SVG (deterministic force layout so it doesn't jump between nights — important) plus `snapshot.json`. Static PWA + Tailscale Serve + GitHub Pages mirror + ntfy.sh. Sonification is unusually natural here: map the price index to a drone pitch, transactions to clicks, bankruptcies to a low thud — a generative radio station of a working economy, via Tone.js in the PWA.
all.first_weekend: Saturday: goods, firms, households, a double-auction or simple posted-price clearing, wages, and bankruptcy. Get money to not explode; log everything to SQLite. Sunday: R&D + automatic good minting + the DAG renderer. The delight moment is specific and reliable: you refresh the page and there is a node in the graph you did not name, produced by a firm that exists to sell to another firm.
all.six_months_later: A production network 8-12 deep with a few hundred minted goods, recurring credit cycles, two connected economies with emergent comparative advantage, and a nightly parameter sweep whose morning report tells you which policy regime grew fastest last night. The DAG image on your phone genuinely looks like a civilization's technology, and every node in it has a birth certificate.
all.honest_ceiling: Two real bounds. First, **the debugging is market microstructure**, not civilization design — expect 60% of your first month on clearing rules, money supply, and bankruptcy cascades, and expect degenerate attractors (monopoly, hyperinflation, everyone producing one good) that need mechanism fixes rather than parameter tweaks. Second, growth stalls if demand is finite: if households want a fixed basket, the network deepens until it's efficient and then stops. The mitigation — evolving taste vectors with a novelty-seeking term, so fashion keeps reopening demand — is essential, not optional, and it is somewhat arbitrary (you're authoring the appetite for novelty). Also: goods here have *derived* property vectors, so they never feel as physically real as Saltwright's materials. This idea is the most likely to produce something intellectually publishable and the least likely to feel like a world you'd want to live in.
all.research_notes: Verified: ABCE (A Python Library for Economic Agent-based Modeling) provides production/consumption/trade/communication as built-in agent methods and parallelizes across cores — worth reading even if you write your own. nkremerh/sugarscape is an actively maintained Python implementation of Epstein & Axtell's Growing Artificial Societies, the canonical demonstration that realistic inequality and trade patterns are generatively sufficient from thin assumptions — the right reference for market microstructure and for how little you need to get emergence. "Data-Driven Economic Agent-Based Models" (arXiv:2412.16591) confirms the field is active. Theory grounding is W. Brian Arthur's "technology is combination" and Böhm-Bawerk's roundaboutness for the capital-depth metric; Kauffman's adjacent possible maps exactly onto "what inputs are cheap and available today". Tone.js is the standard browser sonification path and is well documented for generative sequencing. No GPU, no CUDA-version exposure. Claude Haiku 4.5 at $1/$5 per MTok with 50% Batch discount makes a weekly deep-analysis call effectively free (verified against the bundled claude-api reference, cached 2026-06-24).

audit.name: Roundabout
