audit.ceiling: This one fails at a specific line the pitch spends one parenthesis on: a minted good's property vector is 'derived deterministically from its inputs and process'. That derivation function is the entire technology of the world, and both possible forms of it are fatal. If it's a mixture/average of input properties, no combination ever beats its best input, roundaboutness has no payoff, and the DAG stops at depth 2-3 within a week. If it's nonlinear/hash-like, then property vectors are effectively random draws, 'brick' was a lottery ticket rather than an invention, and depth grows without meaning. Real economies get depth because physical processing genuinely creates use-value; a hash gives you no such structure and an average gives you no gain. Second failure: the headline metric is gameable. depth(g) = longest path from a raw resource grows monotonically if the derivation ever rewards processing at all, so firms will spin arbitrarily long chains of junk intermediates and the phone-view DAG will thicken nightly while nothing is invented. You will be watching a metric inflate. Third: with novelty-seeking taste vectors (which honest_ceiling correctly says are *essential*, not optional), demand rewards newness per se — so the fitness signal explicitly pays for churn. The genuinely emergent things here (specialization, comparative advantage, credit cycles, diffusion lags) are real and worth having, but they are emergent *social* structure, not technological depth, and every one of them was already demonstrated by Nelson-Winter, Epstein-Axtell and thirty years of ACE literature.
audit.authored_content_risk: Highest of the six. The claim 'nobody wrote brick' is false in the way that matters: brick's value is whatever your derivation function returns for hash(clay, heat, ratio), so you wrote brick's value, you just wrote it implicitly and in bulk. This is the textbook version of the fatal flaw — the designer's content revealed in random order — with the extra twist that if the function is hash-like, what's revealed is noise, which is worse than authored content because it can't even be interestingly authored. The endogenous-price argument is genuinely good and genuinely distinguishes this from a tech tree (an invention's value deforms under adoption; Schumpeterian waves are real and free). But endogenous *valuation* of goods whose *capabilities* come from a fixed derivation rule only shuffles the order in which the rule's outputs get discovered.
audit.compute_honesty: Fully honest, and the cheapest of the six — an economy-day is milliseconds, 20-40 parallel economies overnight is real, GPU genuinely unnecessary, no CUDA exposure, weekly Haiku call is pennies. Its honest_ceiling's warning that 60% of month one goes to market microstructure is if anything understated: getting a double auction with money, endogenous credit, bankruptcy cascades and dynamically-minted goods to avoid hyperinflation and monopoly attractors is an open research problem, and most published economic ABMs hard-code clearing precisely to dodge it. Budget more like two months, and expect mechanism rewrites rather than parameter tweaks.
audit.semantic_risk: High. Goods are content-hashes with derived vectors and LLM-generated names, arranged in a force-directed graph. That is the most convincing-looking tech tree of the six and the least substantiated one — 'Vessel of Karn ← 2 clay + 1 heat' is a hash table with typography. Nothing in the system can distinguish a meaningful intermediate good from a junk one, because nothing ever physically *uses* a good except another recipe whose output is also derived from the same rule. There is no grounding anywhere in the loop.
audit.dubious_claims: ABCE, nkremerh/sugarscape, and the Arthur / Böhm-Bawerk / Kauffman theory framing are all real and correctly attributed — the roundaboutness-as-depth-metric idea is a genuinely nice literalization. arXiv:2412.16591 'Data-Driven Economic Agent-Based Models' I cannot verify; plausible. The overclaim to strike is 'that sweep is a real experiment and the results would be interesting to actual economists' — a parameter sweep over patent length and interest rate in a toy ABM with an invented good-derivation rule is not publishable and would not interest economists; the ACE literature has done this since Nelson & Winter (1982), and the results would be artifacts of your derivation function. Also 'this is the cheapest genuinely-unbounded fitness signal of all six' is wrong as stated: prices are unbounded and endogenous, but they price capabilities that come from a bounded authored rule, so the fitness signal is unbounded in range and bounded in content. Tone.js sonification claim is fine.
audit.one_change: Delete the derived property vector. Give goods no intrinsic properties at all, and let value arise only from *use*: households and firms have physical needs (warmth, shelter, calories, cutting) evaluated by an actual simulated use-test — bolt Saltwright's material evaluator or Hivewright's physics under the recipe DSL so a good's worth is measured, not derived. Prices then price something real, roundaboutness depth stops being inflatable with junk, and the Schumpeterian machinery — which is the genuinely good part of this design — finally has something worth competing over.

all.name: Psalmdrift
all.pitch: The replicating unit is not a person or a gene but an *idea* — a tiny executable rule that spreads by being taught, mutates in copying, and lives or dies by whether its hosts survive and keep talking. Technology and religion are the same data type here, which is both the joke and the depth: some memes are true, some are merely contagious, and a few are parasites that kill their hosts while spreading faster than ever.
all.world: "The Long Shelf": a chain of twelve valleys along a mountain range, connected by passes that close in winter. People are cheap agents (needs: food, warmth, safety; no LLM anywhere in the mechanics) with a **belief inventory**: a bounded set of memes. A meme is `WHEN <predicate over perceivable state> DO <action> [BECAUSE <symbol>]` — predicates and actions come from a small composable DSL over the world's affordances (forage, cache, burn, build, move, share, avoid, kill, teach). The BECAUSE symbol carries **zero mechanics** and is exactly what makes memes cluster into doctrines. Each valley also holds a **shrine** with an omen text. Resources: food, fuel, safety, and attention (you can only teach k memes per encounter — this bottleneck is the engine).
all.invention_engine:
Memes replicate by teaching, under three pressures:

(1) **Copy error**: predicates and actions mutate on transmission (a threshold drifts, a conjunct is dropped, an action is swapped). Most mutants are worse; some are better; a few are neutral-but-catchier.

(2) **Recombination**: two memes sharing a BECAUSE symbol can fuse into a compound rule. Doctrine is therefore a *recombination substrate* — belonging to the same religion literally makes your ideas breed with each other. This is a mechanism, not a metaphor.

(3) **The transmission bottleneck** — Kirby-style iterated learning. A learner sees only k examples of the teacher's practice and must generalize a rule from them. This provably amplifies weak biases toward compressible, compositional structure: over generations the meme pool becomes a *grammar of practice* rather than a bag of rules. This is the mechanism that makes the system produce structure rather than drift, and it is the strongest theoretical foundation of any engine in these six ideas.

On top: a **naming game** (Metropolis-Hastings Naming Game, arXiv:2305.19761) for symbols referring to materials, places, and actions. Symbols converge inside a valley and diverge between valleys → dialects → mutual unintelligibility → cultural speciation. And because a more efficient dialect encodes more memes per encounter, **language quality is itself a technology under selection** — a beautiful closed loop.

Technology = memes whose effect on survival is positive. Religion = memes whose effect on transmission is positive. Both are the same struct, and the system does not distinguish them; you do, at analysis time, via counterfactual replay.
all.why_unbounded: Meme space is program space over a *growing* symbol vocabulary — and the vocabulary grows because the naming game mints new symbols whenever agents need to distinguish referents they previously conflated. So the alphabet expands, which expands the program space, which expands what can be distinguished. Add frequency-dependent selection: a meme's fitness depends on the current meme pool (a contrarian practice thrives precisely when the common practice is crowded), so there is no static optimum. And iterated learning supplies a *directional* pressure toward compositional structure that keeps generating new structure rather than random-walking. Honest boundary: memes can only be true *about* things the world affords, so the DSL's predicate/action set is the real cap — see honest_ceiling.
all.depth_ladder:
Week 1: people, needs, memes as rules, teaching with copy error. Watch a useful meme (`WHEN cold DO burn fuel`) sweep a valley. Watch a useless one sweep too, because it was taught by someone popular.
Week 2: the bottleneck and iterated learning. Rules start getting *shorter and more general* on their own — a mutation from `WHEN cold-and-night-and-winter` to `WHEN cold`. That compression happening without you coding it is the delight moment.
Week 3-4: BECAUSE symbols and doctrine clustering; the first syncretism when two valleys' doctrines merge after a marriage-analog.
Month 2: naming game; dialects; first mutual unintelligibility; the first valley that can't learn from its neighbors and stagnates.
Month 3: parasitic memes — high prevalence, negative marginal survival, detected by counterfactual cohort replay. A push notification reading "a practice has spread to 71% of the Shelf that is killing its hosts" is the single best notification any of these six ideas can send.
Month 4-6: doctrine wars, prophets (agents with anomalously high teaching weight), heresies (a mutant BECAUSE symbol forking a doctrine), and canonization (the shrine text stabilizing because copies converge).
Wildest plausible: a meme complex that *protects itself* — a rule of the form `WHEN taught-a-rival-doctrine DO avoid` that measurably raises the fitness of its co-doctrinal memes. Emergent memetic immunity. I'd put this at 50%, and it's the kind of thing that would genuinely startle you.
all.what_selects: Famine, cold, and predation kill hosts, and a meme dies with its last host. Plague spreads along the same encounter graph as teaching, so a highly social doctrine is also an epidemiological liability. Raids destroy valleys and their libraries. Doctrine wars: valleys with incompatible BECAUSE-clusters fight, and a conquered valley's memes are partially absorbed (syncretism, with the conqueror's symbols relabelling the loser's practices). Attention is scarce: the belief inventory is bounded, so every new meme evicts an old one — memes compete directly for a fixed number of slots in every skull.
all.changing_worlds: Climate cycles on a long period (a 40-year cold snap makes half the practical memes wrong at once — mass extinction of technologies). Passes freeze and thaw, changing the transmission topology from a chain to isolated islands and back, which is the classic driver of cultural divergence and re-convergence. An ice age empties the northern valleys and forces migration, which mixes previously isolated meme pools. And a slow drift in what the world affords (new plants, new predators) that quietly invalidates old rules.
all.novelty_detector:
(1) **Conversion events**: any meme crossing 50% Shelf-wide prevalence for the first time.
(2) **Coinage**: a new symbol minted by the naming game and adopted in ≥3 valleys.
(3) **Parasite detection**: for the top-20 memes by prevalence, run a counterfactual replay on a small cloned cohort with the meme suppressed; report any meme with high prevalence and significantly negative marginal survival. Expensive but done nightly on 20 memes it's cheap, and it produces the best notifications in the project.
(4) **Semantic novelty of scripture**: embed the current shrine texts (all-MiniLM or a small Qwen embedding, milliseconds on the 5070) and report when a text's nearest neighbor in the all-time archive exceeds a distance threshold — the scripture has drifted somewhere genuinely new. This is the ASAL trick (foundation-model embedding distance as an open-endedness measure) applied to text.
(5) First-ever event signatures via bloom filter.
all.phone_view: Hero: **today's verse** — the current scripture of the dominant doctrine, in big type, rendered from symbol-strings into readable liturgy by a local Qwen3-4B (flavor only; mechanics stay in the DSL so everything remains debuggable). Below: a stream-graph of the top-10 memes' prevalence over the last 60 days, which looks like a Spotify Wrapped for beliefs and is instantly readable. Then at most one alert card: "HERESY" (a doctrine forked), "PARASITE" (a meme is killing its hosts), or "COINAGE" (a word was invented). Sonification is exceptional here: each valley's dominant doctrine maps to a musical mode and a drone pitch; conversions are audible as a valley's drone sliding to a new mode; leave the radio on while you work and you hear the Shelf converting.
all.hardware_use: CPU for the sim — twelve valleys of a few hundred agents is trivial, and 64GB lets you run many Shelves in parallel with different bottleneck sizes k (k is the single most theoretically interesting parameter you have; sweep it nightly). GPU: a sentence-embedding model for scripture novelty (tiny, <1GB) and Qwen3-4B Q4 (~3GB) for the nightly liturgy rendering — comfortable inside 8GB with room to spare. No training, no CUDA-version brinkmanship beyond getting llama.cpp/Ollama running, which works fine on Blackwell.
all.input_cadence: Zero required — and this is the idea that most benefits from *other people* instead of you. The public PWA has a **guestbook**: every line a visitor types is injected as the omen text at a random shrine. Agents cannot read it, but the shrine's omen seeds a BECAUSE symbol, which enters the doctrine, mutates for two hundred generations, and reappears months later as scripture that is a garbled descendant of what a stranger typed in March. That is free, genuinely non-stationary perturbation and the best possible reason for the artifact to be public. Your own god-nudges: send a prophet, close a pass, trigger a cold snap.
all.tech: Python or Node for the sim (it's small); the meme DSL is an AST interpreted directly, ~300 lines. SQLite for memes, lineages, prevalence time series, shrine texts, and events. sentence-transformers (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) or a small Qwen embedding for scripture novelty; Ollama + Qwen3-4B for liturgy prose. Nightly job writes `snapshot.json` + the stream-graph PNG. Static PWA (canvas + Tone.js for the doctrine radio) over Tailscale Serve, public mirror on GitHub Pages with the guestbook backed by a tiny Node endpoint (or a GitHub issue-comments hack if you want zero server). ntfy.sh push. Receipt printer prints the day's verse each morning — an unusually good physical artifact for this one.
all.first_weekend: Saturday: agents with needs, the meme DSL and interpreter, teaching with copy error, and the k-example bottleneck. Plot prevalence over time. Sunday: BECAUSE symbols, doctrine clustering, and the guestbook → shrine → BECAUSE pipeline, plus the stream-graph. By Sunday night, a rule you never wrote will be at 60% prevalence in a valley, and you'll be able to read its ancestry back to the mutation that made it.
all.six_months_later: Twelve valleys with distinct dialects and doctrines, a scripture archive you can scroll like a sacred text with all its variant readings, a documented history of at least one parasitic belief and one heresy war, and a guestbook line from a stranger that is now, in mutated form, the central tenet of a religion. The doctrine radio is on in the background most days.
all.honest_ceiling: The hard bound is that **memes can only be about what the world affords**. With a thin physical world, the meme pool saturates: after a few weeks the true rules have all been found, and further evolution is churn in the BECAUSE layer — which is entertaining (religion keeps mutating forever, because it's unconstrained by truth) but is not *technological* depth. The mitigation is to widen the world's affordances every few weeks (fire, storage, building, boats, agriculture), and each one costs you a day of work and re-opens the space for maybe two weeks. So the honest characterization is: the religion/memetics layer is genuinely open-ended and will still be surprising at six months; the *technology* layer is bounded by your DSL and will plateau around week 6 unless you keep feeding it. Also, be honest with yourself that counterfactual parasite detection is O(cohort replays) and will be the slowest thing in the system.
all.research_notes: Verified: the Metropolis-Hastings Naming Game (arXiv:2305.19761) gives a principled probabilistic-generative-model formulation of symbol emergence in multi-agent systems — communication as MH sampling over a shared generative model, converging to a shared lexicon; SimSiam Naming Game (arXiv:2410.21803) unifies emergent communication with representation learning. Kirby's iterated learning / transmission-bottleneck result is the load-bearing theory: repeated imitation under a bottleneck exponentially amplifies weak biases toward simple, compositional, generalizable representations — this is confirmed as the central theoretical result in the current literature (transmission-chain experiments; Mesoudi's 2025 R tutorial 'Simulation Models of Cultural Evolution in R', bookdown.org/amesoudi/ABMtutorial_bookdown, has runnable Bayesian iterated-learning and social-learning-strategy models worth stealing structure from). 'Cultural evolution in populations of Large Language Models' (arXiv:2403.08882) provides an LLM-population framework with network-structure manipulation — useful as a comparison point, though I keep LLMs out of the mechanics here deliberately for debuggability. The embedding-distance-to-archive novelty measure is the technique validated in Sakana/MIT's ASAL (github.com/SakanaAI/asal, arXiv:2412.17799), which uses foundation-model representations to score temporally open-ended novelty in ALife systems. Qwen3-4B Q4 ≈3GB VRAM leaves ample room alongside a MiniLM embedder on 8GB. ntfy.sh + Tailscale + PWA path documented at docs.ntfy.sh.

audit.name: Psalmdrift
audit.ceiling: The technology layer stops in days of compute, not the week 6 the pitch claims. The set of *true* rules is literally enumerable: |predicates| × |actions| over a thin affordance set, so with a handful of affordances you're looking at dozens-to-low-hundreds of survival-positive memes, all findable by a few hours of mutation. Everything after that is drift in the BECAUSE layer, which carries zero mechanics by explicit design. So the honest characterization is sharper than 'religion keeps mutating forever': the open-ended part is provably content-free, because the field it churns in is one the designer defined as inert. That's not a bug in the sim, it's an accurate model of one thing about religion, and it is not what the builder asked for. Widening affordances buys ~2 weeks each at a day of work, which is a treadmill, not a ceiling-raiser. Second problem, unadvertised: recombination via shared BECAUSE symbol partitions the mating pool *arbitrarily*, so fused memes are conjunctions of causally unrelated rules; most will be strictly worse, and the doctrine layer is a random mating structure dressed as a semantic one. Third, the parasite detector — the best notification in all six — is statistically unsound as specified: with a bounded belief inventory, suppressing meme X changes which meme fills the slot, so the counterfactual measures 'X vs. its replacement', not X's marginal effect; and a single cohort replay of a high-prevalence meme in a chaotic system is one draw from a huge variance. You will ship 'PARASITE' pushes generated by noise. Matched cohorts across many seeds fixes it and multiplies the cost by ~50.
audit.authored_content_risk: Highest theory-laundering risk of the six, and it's in the part the notes call the strongest foundation. Kirby's iterated-learning result is that a transmission bottleneck *amplifies the learner's prior* toward compressible, compositional mappings — it requires a structured meaning space and a learner performing induction with an inductive bias. Here 'the learner sees k examples and must generalize a rule' means you wrote the generalizer, and whatever compositional structure emerges is the structure your generalizer prefers. So the week-2 delight moment — 'rules get shorter and more general on their own, and that compression happening without you coding it' — is precisely backwards: you coded it, in the induction step, and the bottleneck's job is to make your bias visible. Related and load-bearing: iterated learning without a countervailing expressivity/communicative-success pressure collapses to degenerate languages (the standard two-pressure result). The naming game supplies that pressure for symbols; nothing described supplies it for memes, so the meme pool's most likely long-run state is a small set of maximally general, nearly-contentless rules. That is the opposite of depth and it will look like 'elegant compression' while it happens.
audit.compute_honesty: Yes — trivially laptop-scale for the sim (twelve valleys × a few hundred agents), and MiniLM plus Qwen3-4B Q4 sits comfortably in 8GB with room. The one real cost is the counterfactual replay, correctly flagged as the slowest thing in the system; if you fix its statistics as above it becomes the dominant cost and 20 memes × N cohorts × replay length needs an actual budget. Sweeping k nightly across many Shelves is genuinely feasible and is the best use of the RAM in any of the six.
audit.semantic_risk: The highest gap between perceived and actual meaning of any project here, and it's structural rather than incidental. The hero card is Qwen-rendered liturgy generated from symbol strings that carry *zero mechanics by design*. The most beautiful, most shareable, most emotionally compelling output of the whole system is by construction the part with no information content, and it will confabulate coherence — theology out of an arbitrary tag. Meanwhile the mechanically real layer (rule ASTs, prevalence curves) is the boring-looking part. That's an inverted signal-to-beauty ratio and it will fool you, not just visitors. The guestbook→shrine→BECAUSE pipeline is the best idea in the six for cheap non-stationary perturbation, but note it is unmoderated public text injection into a public artifact and needs a filter on day one.
audit.dubious_claims: MH Naming Game (arXiv:2305.19761) and 'Cultural evolution in populations of LLMs' (arXiv:2403.08882) are real and fairly characterized; ASAL (arXiv:2412.17799) is real; Mesoudi's bookdown ABM tutorial is real. SimSiam Naming Game (arXiv:2410.21803) plausible, unverified. The claim to reject is 'this is confirmed as the central theoretical result in the current literature' about iterated learning — overstated, and it papers over the fact that the result amplifies *the prior you install*, which is exactly the critique above; the degenerate-collapse condition is a standard caveat that goes unmentioned. Second flag: applying ASAL's foundation-model-embedding novelty measure to shrine texts is the one clean application of that trick in these six documents (text is in-distribution for the embedder), but 'distance to nearest archive neighbor exceeds threshold' on LLM-generated liturgy will mostly detect stylistic drift in the *renderer*, not doctrinal drift in the sim — embed the symbol strings, not the prose.
audit.one_change: Make affordances endogenous instead of hand-widened. Let memes produce artifacts/state that become new predicates and actions for other memes — a practice whose output is itself a perceivable, actionable thing — so the world's affordance set grows from within rather than costing you a day of coding every two weeks. Cheapest concrete version: memes can reference the *outputs* of other memes, and any stable practice-product gets minted as a new world affordance. Failing that, run the meme layer on top of a substrate that genuinely can't be exhausted (Hivewright's physics), which is the only other way the technology layer outlives month two.

all.name: Firmament
all.pitch: Each world's physics is generated from a grammar, so its laws are genuinely unknown — and the civilizations living in it must discover those laws by running experiments that cost resources and sometimes kill the experimenter. Technology is not a recipe here but a *theory*: a symbolic expression fitted to observations, which lets a tribe compute a good design instead of stumbling onto one, and a paradigm shift is something you can trigger from your phone by nudging a hidden constant.
all.world: A world generated in two layers. The **visible layer** is an ordinary survival landscape: terrain, weather, ore, timber, rivers, tribes, winters. The **hidden layer** is 6-10 latent relations drawn from a law grammar over in-world observables — e.g. `flux = a * mass / dist^p`, a conserved quantity `k = v^2 + c*h`, a threshold phenomenon (`if T > T_crit, phase change`), a resonance (`efficiency peaks at f = sqrt(tension/density)`), an inverse-square field, a decay with a hidden half-life. These laws are the *actual* physics: they compute whether a kiln fires, whether a bridge holds, whether a boat capsizes, how far a signal carries, how fast a disease spreads. Nobody in-world can see them. Neither can the agents' code — the sim evaluates them, the agents only see outcomes.
all.invention_engine:
Science, mechanized, in three coupled loops — a wake/sleep flywheel where the library is a library of *laws*.

(1) **EXPERIMENT (wake).** A tribe builds an apparatus: a parameterized rig (a kiln with a chosen chimney height and fuel load, a bridge with a chosen span and thickness, a sling with a chosen tension). Building costs materials and labor; running it produces one observation row `(inputs..., outcome)` into the tribe's observation table. Some experiments kill the experimenter, and dead experimenters teach nothing.

(2) **THEORY (sleep, nightly).** Run **PySR** (github.com/MilesCranmer/PySR, arXiv:2305.01582 — Julia backend, genuinely excellent multicore CPU scaling) over each tribe's observation table. The output is a Pareto front of (accuracy vs. complexity) symbolic expressions: **the tribe's book of laws.** This is DreamCoder's compression step with equations instead of lambda terms — and the compounding is the same: a law once found is a named primitive that later theories can reference (`the flux law` becomes a term in the efficiency law).

(3) **DESIGN OF EXPERIMENTS (the auto-curriculum).** Pick the next experiments by maximizing disagreement among the top-k Pareto theories — query-by-committee / Bayesian optimal experimental design. Where the theories disagree most is where a measurement is worth the most, so **the tribe's theories tell it what to try next.** This is the piece that makes the whole thing feel alive: the curriculum is not authored, it is derived from the current state of ignorance.

And the payoff loop that makes theory *be* technology: with a law in hand, a tribe designs by optimization (solve for the chimney height that maximizes the law's predicted efficiency) instead of by grid search. Concretely: theory-less tribes burn 20x the fuel to find a mediocre kiln; theory-having tribes compute a near-optimal one on the first build. Better theory → better artifacts → more surplus → more experiments. That is a compounding advantage with no ceiling except the truth.
all.why_unbounded: Two nested spaces. Across worlds: the law grammar (compositions of operators over observables, with continuous constants) generates a combinatorially vast family of possible physics, so no amount of play teaches you the answer — every world is a fresh science. Within a world: symbolic-expression space is infinite, and engineering built on laws composes continuously (a heat law plus a pressure law makes an engine-analog whose design space is a continuous manifold you optimize over). Additionally, **emergent laws never finish**: include latent regularities about the agents' own aggregate behavior — epidemic thresholds, price dynamics, crowd flow — which are endogenous and shift as the civilization changes, so there is a class of laws that cannot be permanently solved.
all.depth_ladder:
Week 1: the law grammar, the hidden-law evaluator, and one apparatus type (a kiln). Hand-play it: build kilns with different chimney heights, look at the observation table, run PySR yourself and see if *you* can find the law. If it's fun for you it will be fun to watch.
Week 2: tribes doing random experiments, PySR nightly, a Pareto front per tribe. The first time a tribe's fitted expression matches the true law to within a constant is the delight moment, and it will happen in week 2.
Month 1: the design-of-experiments loop; watch experiment choices concentrate exactly where theories disagree. Watch a tribe with a good law out-build a tribe without one, and outlive it through a winter.
Month 2: multiple apparatus types and composed laws; theft and teaching of theories, including **garbled transmission** (a corrupted law is worse than none — a tribe confidently building to a wrong formula and collapsing is genuinely dramatic).
Month 3: emergent-law layer (epidemiology, crowd dynamics) that never fully resolves.
Month 4-6: the paradigm-shift game — perturb a hidden constant at midnight and watch anomalies accumulate, predictions degrade, a crisis of confidence in the old law, and PySR refit onto a new expression. A Kuhnian revolution on a schedule.
Wildest plausible endpoint: a tribe that discovers a law it cannot yet exploit (knows the resonance condition but can't build the apparatus), retains it as inert scripture for fifty years, and cashes it in when a materials advance arrives. Latent knowledge with a delayed payoff — this happens naturally and it is thrilling.
all.what_selects: Bad theory kills. Winter demands a kiln that holds temperature; a flood demands a bridge that holds; a voyage demands a boat that doesn't capsize. Experiments consume scarce materials and sometimes the experimenter. Rival tribes with better laws outbuild you and take your valley. Theories are stolen, taught, and garbled — and a confidently wrong law is *more* dangerous than ignorance, because you build big with it.
all.changing_worlds: This is the idea whose core loop is worlds changing. Every world seed is a new physics, and worlds are **consumable**: when a civilization has recovered the true laws, that world is largely solved and you retire it to an archive and start another. Run 3-4 concurrently. Within a world: your god-nudge is `perturb constant p by 10% at midnight`, which is a paradigm shift on demand; also available are revealing a new observable (giving them an instrument), and hiding one (blinding them).
all.novelty_detector:
(1) **New law discovered**: a tribe's Pareto front gains an expression that dominates the previous best on both accuracy and complexity — mechanically detectable from PySR's own output, no heuristics needed.
(2) **Correctness crossing**: symbolic distance (tree edit distance on canonicalized expressions, or agreement of predictions on a held-out grid) between the tribe's law and the *true* law crossing a threshold — you're the only one who can compute this, and "they got it right" is a wonderful notification.
(3) **Anomaly / crisis**: predictive residuals against a tribe's own best law spiking above a control limit — their physics just broke, either because you perturbed a constant or because they extrapolated outside their data.
(4) **First exploitation**: the first artifact designed by optimization-under-theory rather than search, and its performance delta over the search-designed baseline.
(5) First-ever event signatures.
all.phone_view: One card per tribe, and it is the best 30-second view of the six because you are reading someone else's science over their shoulder while holding the answer key. Each card shows: the tribe's current best law rendered as readable math, the **true law** beneath it (visible only to you), an accuracy dial, the number of experiments run, deaths from experiments, and a small trend line labelled "days until they figure it out" extrapolated from residual decay. Plus a running headline feed: "the Ashfolk have stopped believing in the old flux law." An hour of bingeing is scrolling a tribe's experiment log and watching their theory evolve expression by expression.
all.hardware_use: CPU-dominant and a genuinely good fit for this machine: PySR's Julia backend parallelizes across cores and 64GB is plenty for many concurrent searches; a nightly pass over 8 tribes x 4 worlds is comfortably an overnight job. **The GPU is largely idle** unless you make the visible world grid-based (then diffusion/flow on the 5070 via CuPy). Use spare VRAM for a Qwen3-4B writing the natural-philosopher's journal. Setup honesty: PySR requires Julia and a first-run precompile (~30 minutes of installation pain, once). Benchmark hygiene: never make fitness wall-clock-dependent — cap PySR by **iteration count and population size, not seconds**, so a thermally throttled night produces the same science as a cool one.
all.input_cadence: Zero required. God-nudges are the best in this set and all one tap: perturb a hidden constant (paradigm shift), reveal a new observable (invent the thermometer for them), gift a true law to one tribe (revelation) and watch whether they can transmit it intact, or hide an observable (a fog descends). Weekly at most, and each nudge produces days of consequences.
all.tech: Python sim + PySR (Julia backend) for the theory step; sympy for canonicalizing and comparing expressions to ground truth; scipy.optimize for the design-under-theory step; a small custom module for the law grammar and the hidden-law evaluator. SQLite for observations, theories (versioned per tribe per night), artifacts, and events. Nightly job writes `snapshot.json` + rendered law cards. Static PWA over Tailscale Serve + GitHub Pages mirror + ntfy.sh. Optional Claude Haiku 4.5 weekly to write a history-of-science essay from the theory-version log (~100K in / 5K out ≈ $0.13, halved with the Batch API).
all.first_weekend: Saturday: law grammar + hidden evaluator + one apparatus (a kiln with 3 design parameters) + an observation table. Generate 200 random experiments, run PySR on them yourself, and see whether the true law is recoverable — this is the single most important feasibility test in the whole idea and you can do it in four hours. If PySR recovers your seeded laws from noisy observations, the project is real. Sunday: tribes, resource costs for experiments, nightly PySR per tribe, and the law card renderer. By Sunday night your phone shows a tribe's guess at a law you generated randomly on Saturday morning.
all.six_months_later: An archive of a dozen retired worlds, each with a history-of-science log showing which laws were found, in what order, by which tribe, and which were never found at all. Three live worlds mid-discovery. A documented paradigm shift you triggered and its aftermath. And a genuinely interesting empirical question you'll have data on: which *kinds* of laws are hard for a civilization to discover, and does the structure of the true law predict the shape of the wrong theories that precede it?
all.honest_ceiling: **Within one world, science finishes.** With 6-10 laws and a working design-of-experiments loop, expect a competent civilization to recover most of the true laws in days to a few weeks — and then that world is a solved crossword. Firmament is therefore a world-factory, not a single eternal world, and if you don't enjoy the meta-game of comparing worlds you'll get bored. Two other honest limits: PySR recovers clean low-dimensional laws well but degrades fast with noise, with more than ~4-5 interacting variables, and with laws outside its operator set — so your law grammar is constrained to what symbolic regression can actually find, which is a real design shackle you'll feel. And the emergent-law layer (the part that genuinely never finishes) is the hardest to build and the least likely to survive contact with your first month.
all.research_notes: Verified: PySR (github.com/MilesCranmer/PySR, arXiv:2305.01582, reviewed in Genetic Programming and Evolvable Machines) is the leading open-source practical symbolic-regression tool, Julia-backed with strong multicore scaling — the right engine and a genuinely good match for a 64GB laptop with an idle GPU. Active 2025-26 work confirms the area is alive: an ANN-PySR hybrid for identifying governing PDEs from sparse noisy data (Zhang et al., June 2025, ~2 orders of magnitude speedup), symbolic quantile regression (Hoekstra et al., Aug 2025), a Feb 2026 review of symbolic regression for automated equation discovery, and Bayesian symbolic regression from a physicist's perspective (Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 384:20250089). LaSR is the most relevant extension: it augments genetic symbolic search with zero-shot LLM prompts and a learned *concept library*, outperforming plain PySR on the Feynman benchmarks — which is a direct, tested route to adding library learning to the theory step later. The design-of-experiments-by-committee-disagreement loop is standard Bayesian optimal experimental design. The auto-curriculum framing (archive of what's been learned, propose the next interestingly-new thing) is validated by OMNI-EPIC (arXiv:2405.15568, ICLR 2025). PySR is CPU/Julia so the RTX 5070's sm_120 wheel situation is a non-issue.

audit.name: Firmament
audit.ceiling: Per world: days, not the 'days to a few weeks' claimed, and this is the tightest ceiling in the set. With 6-10 laws in ≤4-5 variables each, a working query-by-committee DoE loop, and PySR — which recovers clean low-dimensional laws from a few hundred good observations in minutes — a single overnight run plausibly solves a whole world. Six months is then ~60-100 retired worlds, and the meta-game's surprise is constant in *kind*: 'they found it / they didn't'. That's a puzzle generator, not an open-ended civilization. Two structural problems make it worse. First, laws never compose in the *world's* ontology, only in the tribes' notation — a tribe referencing 'the flux law' inside a later expression is bookkeeping, not new physics — so there is no depth axis at all, just a checklist of 6-10 items. Second, the only genuinely never-finishing component (latent regularities about the agents' own aggregate behavior — epidemics, prices, crowd flow) is exactly the regime symbolic regression is *worst* at: high-noise, non-stationary, many interacting variables. PySR will emit confidently-wrong expressions there every night and the residual-based 'crisis' detector will fire constantly. So the open-ended layer and the chosen engine are structurally mismatched, and honest_ceiling is right that it won't survive month one. Also note one of the six named law archetypes — the threshold/phase change — is piecewise-discontinuous, a known SR weak spot; your grammar and your engine are already in tension.
audit.authored_content_risk: This is the purest instance of the fatal pattern in all six: generate a hidden target from a designer grammar, let agents find the hidden target, notify when found. The grammar is procedural rather than hand-written per world, which is a real defense — but the space of discoverable truths is still enumerated by the operator set, and worse, it's enumerated by *what PySR can find*, which honest_ceiling concedes is a real shackle. The mitigating half is genuine and worth crediting: the *process* around the answer — costly experiments, dead experimenters, garbled transmission of theories, a tribe confidently building to a wrong formula and collapsing, latent knowledge held as inert scripture until materials catch up — is simulated, not scripted, and none of the other five produce drama that legible. But 'science as process' being emergent doesn't make 'the laws' emergent, and the depth claim rests on the laws.
audit.compute_honesty: Mostly honest, with two omissions. PySR across 8 tribes × 4 worlds = 32 searches per night is feasible on multicore in an overnight window, though each Julia worker carries a few hundred MB and the parallel-search memory footprint is heavier than implied; the ~30-minute one-time Julia precompile is correctly disclosed. Capping by iteration count rather than seconds is exactly the right benchmark hygiene and nobody else in this set states it as clearly. Omission one: PySR is stochastic, so refitting a tribe nightly on a growing observation table yields a *different* expression most nights from search noise alone — your 'new law discovered' and 'crisis' notifications will fire on nondeterminism unless you warm-start, pin seeds, and accept only Pareto-dominating changes. Omission two: symbolic distance to ground truth via tree edit distance on canonicalized expressions is fragile (algebraically identical laws canonicalize differently); score by prediction agreement on a held-out grid instead, which they list as the alternative — make it the primary.
audit.semantic_risk: Lowest of the six, and by a wide margin. Expressions are checkable against a known ground truth, so 'they got it right' has a crisp definition and cannot be faked by pretty rendering. The phone view — their guess above, the true law below, an accuracy dial — is the only card in these six where the reader can verify the claim being made. The Haiku-written history-of-science essay is decoration over a substrate that is actually verifiable. If you want the project least likely to fool you, it's this one; that's the flip side of it being the one whose content you authored.
audit.dubious_claims: PySR (arXiv:2305.01582) is real and correctly characterized, including its noise/dimensionality limits. OMNI-EPIC (arXiv:2405.15568) is real; the ICLR 2025 acceptance I can't confirm. LaSR — LLM-guided symbolic search with a learned concept library beating PySR on Feynman — is real and is genuinely the right pointer for adding library learning later. The 2025-26 citation cluster is where I'd stop trusting the notes: an 'ANN-PySR hybrid for governing PDEs, June 2025, ~2 orders of magnitude speedup', 'symbolic quantile regression, Hoekstra et al., Aug 2025', 'a Feb 2026 review of symbolic regression for automated equation discovery', and 'Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 384:20250089' are all unverifiable to me and several post-date what I can check; the volume/article numbering is the kind of detail that gets confabulated. None of them is load-bearing for the design, so just don't cite them at anyone. 'Design of experiments by committee disagreement is standard Bayesian OED' is correct and will work as described.
audit.one_change: Make the true laws something you also cannot write down. Derive the hidden layer from a lower-level simulation — a coarse particle/field/agent substrate whose closed form nobody has — and let 'the law' be whatever regularity that substrate actually exhibits. There is then no answer key, worlds don't complete because the regularities are approximate and regime-dependent, tribes' theories are permanently improvable, and the emergent-law layer you rated most valuable becomes the *default* rather than a month-three add-on you'll never build. Cost: you lose the 'true law shown beneath their guess' phone card, which is your best UI — replace it with held-out predictive accuracy, which is what real science uses anyway.

all.name: Hivewright
all.pitch: Colonies of near-mindless workers follow local build-or-dig rules, and the mounds they raise have real thermal and airflow function computed by a physics solve — so a chimney, a heat exchanger, or a humidity trap is *discovered*, never authored. Each night the system mines frequent structural motifs out of the mounds that survived and promotes them into named building blocks that mutation can place as a unit, so architecture compounds from chamber to mound to district to city.
all.world: "The Mound": a 512x512 grid (2.5D — a height/material stack per cell) with four coupled continuous fields solved every tick — heat diffusion, humidity, CO2, and water flow — plus a solar cycle and seasons. The crop is a fungus-analog that only grows in a narrow (temperature, humidity) band and is the colony's entire food supply, so **climate control is survival**. Workers are ~12 bytes of state each and are genuinely mindless: read the local 5x5 neighborhood (material tags + field values), then deposit, remove, or lay pheromone. A colony's genome is a **construction grammar**: a set of `local pattern -> action` rules, i.e. stigmergy, exactly as real termites do it. Resources: soil, water, fungus, worker-hours.
all.invention_engine:
Function is computed by physics, never assigned. A mound's ventilation, thermal inertia, and moisture retention fall out of its geometry via the field solve — so a novel structure has genuinely unknown value until it's built and a summer passes.

WAKE: colonies reproduce with grammar mutation and crossover; a colony dies if the fungus chamber leaves the viable band for too long, floods, overheats, starves, or is raided.

SLEEP (nightly), two passes:
(1) **Motif mining.** Hash every 5x5x3 patch of every surviving mound; rank candidates by lift (`P(patch | survivor) / P(patch | all)`) and by their marginal contribution to a thermal-stability score measured by ablation (rebuild the mound without the patch, re-solve, measure the damage). High-lift, high-contribution motifs are promoted into the colony's **module library** with a name, and mutation can thereafter insert the whole module as a single edit. This is the compression-into-primitives move — the same compounding as a skill library — applied to architecture: modules made of modules give you a real scale hierarchy (chamber → mound → district → city).
(2) **Quality-diversity archive.** pyribs MAP-Elites over behavior descriptors (mound height, porosity, thermal stability, colony size, water storage), objective = fungus yield through a full year. This keeps a *library of architectures* rather than one champion — so when the climate shifts, there are weird elites in the archive that suddenly become correct.

Once colonies neighbor each other, a second level opens without new mechanism: shared walls, roads worn by traffic (stigmergy again), canals, and contested boundaries — inter-colony structures with their own emergent function.
all.why_unbounded: Grammar space is infinite, and unlike a recipe list the *evaluation* is a physics solve, so the value of a novel geometry cannot be looked up — only simulated. The compounding comes from module promotion: each promoted module shortens the mutational path to structures that were previously astronomically unlikely, and modules compose hierarchically, so the reachable structural complexity grows with the library rather than staying fixed. And niche construction closes the loop: a built mound changes the local fields, which changes which rules fire, which changes what gets built. Honest boundary: **function is bounded by the physics you simulate** — see the ceiling.
all.depth_ladder:
Week 1: grid, heat + humidity diffusion, workers with a handful of hand-written stigmergic rules, canvas render. You will get a pile. Piles are correct for week 1.
Week 2: fungus with a viability band, colony death, grammar mutation and selection. The first mound with an *interior* that holds temperature better than outside — the delight moment, and it arrives fast.
Week 3-4: motif mining; the first promoted module, which will probably be a wall-with-a-gap (a vent). You didn't write it and you can see it in cross-section.
Month 2: MAP-Elites archive filling with structurally distinct architectures; the first genuine chimney (a vertical shaft driving convective flow) — verifiable in the airflow field, not just visually.
Month 3: multi-colony contact; walls, roads, and the first shared canal; raids.
Month 4-6: climate drift makes existing architecture lethal and you watch retrofit — old chambers sealed, new vents cut into hundred-day-old structures. Then a load/collapse physics layer, and mounds get *tall* with buttresses that were never designed.
Wildest plausible endpoint: a district-scale structure whose function only exists at district scale — a shared thermal mass or a canal network that no single colony's grammar encodes, arising from the interaction of several grammars. Emergent infrastructure. Maybe 40%, and it would be the single best screenshot of any of these six ideas.
all.what_selects: Overheating, mold (humidity too high), desiccation, flooding, starvation when the fungus band is missed, structural collapse when overbuilt, and raids from neighbor colonies. All of it is cheap to compute and brutally legible — a dead colony's mound stays on the map as ruin, and neighbors build into it.
all.changing_worlds: Climate drift is the core: the viable (temperature, humidity) band slowly moves, so architecture that was optimal becomes lethal and colonies must retrofit or die — this is the most viscerally satisfying 'the world changed' mechanic in the set, because you can *see* the retrofit in cross-section. Plus seasonal floods, a multi-year drying that forces water infrastructure, a wet period that rewards drainage, and occasional fires. Multiple worlds: different climate regimes (arid, monsoon, temperate) run in parallel produce visibly different architecture, which is a lovely comparative gallery.
all.novelty_detector:
(1) **New MAP-Elites cell filled** — free from pyribs, and the canonical QD signal.
(2) **Motif promotion with no prior occurrence in any world** — a genuinely new building block, checked against a global motif hash table.
(3) **Functional firsts**: first mound to hold the fungus band through an entire summer; first structure whose ablation costs >30% of thermal stability (a load-bearing *function*, discovered).
(4) **Visual novelty**: perceptual hash or a tiny convolutional autoencoder embedding of the mound cross-section, nearest-neighbor distance against the all-time archive above threshold — the ASAL embedding-novelty trick, applied to pictures of buildings.
(5) First-ever event signatures.
Top 3 nightly to ntfy, each with the cross-section image attached — ntfy supports image attachments, so the push itself is the artifact.
all.phone_view: Hero, and it is the strongest visual of the six: a **rendered cross-section of last night's best mound**, with airflow arrows and a temperature colormap overlaid. It is beautiful, instantly legible to anyone, and changes every day. Below it: the MAP-Elites archive as a small heatmap grid (filled cells = discovered architectures), and 1-2 **new module cards** showing the promoted 5x5 patch, where it appears in the mound, and its ablation cost. Thirty seconds is the cross-section alone. An hour is scrubbing a colony's build history as a time-lapse. The physical artifact writes itself: a receipt printer producing a dot-matrix cross-section every morning is a genuinely covetable object.
all.hardware_use: **This is the one that actually uses the RTX 5070.** Four coupled diffusion/flow fields on 512x512 grids are pure GPU work: a 512² float32 field is 1MB, so 8GB holds hundreds of fields — you can solve 100+ colonies' local environments in parallel. CuPy with a cu12x build is the lowest-friction path; JAX or raw CUDA also work. **Honest caveat, verified:** Blackwell sm_120 needs CUDA 12.8+ and recent wheels — stable PyTorch wheels lagged sm_120 (pytorch issue #164342; nightlies from Aug 2025 onward work with cu128), and CUDA 12.8/12.9 installers shipped without libnvptxcompiler.so, which breaks PTX JIT for some stacks. Budget half a day for the CUDA setup, and write a numpy CPU fallback path first so you are never blocked (CPU is ~30-50x slower but perfectly fine for a single colony while you develop). 64GB RAM holds the mound archive and history comfortably.
all.input_cadence: Zero required. God-nudges: shift the climate band, start a flood, set a fire, open a pass between two colony clusters, or transplant a module from one colony's library into another's (technology transfer). Weekly at most. The only real chore is disk: mound snapshots are images, so rotate aggressively — keep dailies for 30 days, then keep only archive elites.
all.tech: Python + CuPy (numpy fallback) for the field solves and the worker update (vectorized over all workers — they are 12 bytes each and update in lockstep, which is exactly the shape GPUs like); the construction grammar and motif mining in plain Python (hash-based patch mining is fast; upgrade to gSpan-style frequent subgraph mining later if you want). pyribs for the archive. SQLite for colonies, grammars, module libraries, lineage, events. Nightly job renders cross-section PNGs + `snapshot.json`. Static PWA (canvas) over Tailscale Serve, public mirror on GitHub Pages, ntfy.sh with image attachments. Shared substrate with the others: same event schema, same PWA shell, same push helper.
all.first_weekend: Saturday: the grid, heat + humidity diffusion (a 20-line explicit solver is fine), workers with 6 hand-written stigmergic rules, and a canvas render of the top-down view plus a cross-section. Watch a pile become a pile with a hole in it. Sunday: fungus viability band, colony death, grammar mutation, and 50 colonies competing. Render the best mound's cross-section and push it to your phone. By Sunday evening you'll have a mound with an interior microclimate that no rule you wrote specified — the physics found it.
all.six_months_later: A gallery of architectures across three climate regimes, module libraries 40-80 entries deep with visible hierarchical composition, documented retrofits after climate shifts, multi-colony districts with shared walls and canals, and a printed stack of six months of daily cross-sections that is honestly the nicest physical artifact any of these ideas produce. Still surprising, because every physics layer you add (load, light, fire, predators) reopens the whole space.
all.honest_ceiling: Function is bounded by the physics you simulate, and that bound is tighter than it feels. With heat + humidity + flow you should expect roughly 15-30 genuinely distinct functional motifs before saturation — probably month 3 — after which new mounds are recombinations that look different but do the same things. The mitigations are real work: adding structural load and collapse (the best single addition, and it's a week), light, fire spread, and predators. Second honest limit: **it will look far more impressive than it is** for a while, because emergent architecture photographs beautifully even when the underlying discovery has stalled — so lean hard on the ablation-based functional metrics, not the visuals, to know whether it's still inventing. Third: multi-colony infrastructure is the exciting endgame and also the part most likely to just not emerge; do not build the roadmap assuming it will.
all.research_notes: Verified: pyribs (pyribs.org, docs v0.11.0, arXiv:2303.00191, GECCO 2023) is the maintained bare-bones QD library — Archive/Emitter/Scheduler decomposition, MAP-Elites, CMA-ME, CMA-MAE, plus an explicit unstructured-archive Novelty Search tutorial; 'new cell filled' is the free novelty signal. Sakana/MIT's ASAL (github.com/SakanaAI/asal, arXiv:2412.17799, Artificial Life 31(3):368) is JAX-based, end-to-end jittable, and works across Lenia, Boids, Particle Life and neural CAs — both a direct precedent for GPU-accelerated ALife on modest hardware and the source of the foundation-model-embedding novelty measure I'm using for cross-section novelty; QD-AF (arXiv:2312.02231, 'Quality Diversity in the Amorphous Fortress') is a live precedent for QD over 0-player-game-like systems. DreamCoder's compression-into-named-primitives (PLDI 2021; Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 381:20220050) and Stitch's MDL formulation (github.com/mlb2251/stitch, arXiv:2211.16605) are the theoretical basis for module promotion. Hardware verified honestly: PyTorch stable wheels lagged sm_120 (github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/164342), cu128 nightlies from Aug 2025+ detect it, community build guides exist (github.com/bajegani/pytorch-build-blackwell-sm120), and a missing libnvptxcompiler.so in the CUDA 12.8/12.9 installers breaks PTX JIT on Blackwell for some stacks — so plan a CPU fallback and prefer CuPy over exotic JIT paths. ntfy.sh supports image attachments in pushes (docs.ntfy.sh).

audit.name: Hivewright
audit.ceiling: Functionally, ~2-4 weeks, well before the claimed month 3 — and the reason is the objective, not the search. The colony's entire fitness reduces to keeping one chamber inside a (T,H) band. A scalar objective over smooth diffusion fields admits about four physical strategies: thermal mass, convective venting, evaporative cooling, water storage. Those are the functional motifs; everything after is parameter tuning and morphological variation on four ideas. MAP-Elites will diligently fill cells with mounds that are structurally distinct and functionally identical, which is exactly the failure honest_ceiling warns about, arriving sooner than it expects. Two mechanism-level problems compound this. (1) 2.5D — a height/material stack per cell cannot represent overhangs, arches, enclosed horizontal galleries, or a chimney with a lateral duct, i.e. most of what makes real termite architecture interesting; the 'cross-section with airflow arrows' hero image will be rendering a heightfield's implied interior, which is a visualization more than a structure. (2) The claimed hierarchy does not follow from the mechanism. Promoting a 5×5×3 *literal patch* to a single mutation stamp gives you a bigger brush, not a nonterminal — a bigger patch is just a bigger patch. 'Modules made of modules → chamber → mound → district → city' requires the construction grammar to gain composable, parameterized nonterminals; patch hashing cannot produce that, and the entire why_unbounded argument rests on it. Also, lift over survivors is confounded by shared ancestry (same flaw as Cinderloom's librarian): survivors are relatives, so high-lift patches are mostly 'wall texture from the dominant clade'.
audit.authored_content_risk: Lowest of the six, and this is the project's real strength. Function is *computed* by a field solve, so nobody tabulates that a chimney works — thermal stability under ablation is a measurement, not an assignment, and 'first structure whose removal costs >30% of thermal stability' is a genuinely non-authored discovery event. The stigmergic rules are also the right level of abstraction: local pattern → action, exactly as real termites do it, with the mound's own fields feeding back into which rules fire. Niche construction here is real and closes properly. The authored parts are the physics you chose to simulate and the single scalar objective — and those bound *what can be discovered*, not *whether discovery is real*. That's the honest and favorable distinction.
audit.compute_honesty: The weakest compute story in the set, and ironically it's the one claiming to be GPU-honest. Do the arithmetic the pitch skips: four coupled fields on 512² is ~1M cells × 4; explicit diffusion needs small dt, so realistically tens of substeps per tick; a 'full year' evaluation is >10³ ticks. That's roughly 10¹¹-10¹² cell-updates per colony-year. A well-fused bandwidth-bound stencil on a 5070 might sustain ~10¹⁰-10¹¹ updates/s, so one colony-year is seconds to a minute — and a QD generation needs thousands of evaluations per night. 5000 evals × 30s = 42 hours. It does not fit, and shrinking to fit (128² grid, compressed year, fewer colonies) directly shrinks the structural space that was supposed to provide the depth. Then the nightly ablation pass re-solves the mound *per candidate motif* — hundreds of extra full solves — which by itself likely exceeds the entire wake phase. Overall the compute claim is optimistic by roughly one to two orders of magnitude. The tell is in the text: 'a 512² float32 field is 1MB, so 8GB holds hundreds of fields' quotes *capacity* where *throughput* is the binding constraint. The Blackwell caveats and the numpy-fallback-first discipline are, in contrast, sensible and correctly prioritized.
audit.semantic_risk: Low for function, high for perception — and the document says so itself, which is to its credit. Physics validates whether a vent vents, so a promoted motif with a measured ablation cost means something real. But emergent architecture photographs beautifully whether or not discovery has stalled, and this project's whole phone experience is a gorgeous cross-section. The receipt-printed daily section is a lovely object that will keep looking like progress for months after progress stops. Second, narrower risk: the ASAL-style embedding novelty applied to mound cross-sections is a misapplication — synthetic grayscale texture images are far out of distribution for the embedder, and nearest-neighbor distance there is dominated by low-level image statistics, so channel (4) will fire on noise. Drop it and rely on ablation-based functional metrics, exactly as honest_ceiling advises.
audit.dubious_claims: pyribs (arXiv:2303.00191), ASAL (arXiv:2412.17799), QD-AF / Amorphous Fortress (arXiv:2312.02231), DreamCoder PLDI 2021 and Stitch (arXiv:2211.16605) are all real and reasonably characterized. Two flags. First, the Blackwell block — PyTorch issue #164342, 'cu128 nightlies from Aug 2025 onward', 'CUDA 12.8/12.9 installers shipped without libnvptxcompiler.so breaking PTX JIT', plus a named community build-guide repo — is the most specific version of a claim that appears verbatim in three of these documents; the broad 'stable wheels lagged sm_120' part was true through 2025, but the missing-.so detail and the repo name are unverifiable and read as one hallucinated fact propagated across the set. Budget the half-day if you like, but don't trust the diagnosis. Second, citing DreamCoder/Stitch as 'the theoretical basis for module promotion' is a category error given the implementation: those learn abstractions *with variables* by MDL over program structure; hash-based patch mining learns literal fixed images. The citations describe the mechanism you'd need, not the one specified.
audit.one_change: Go to coarse true 3D voxels (128³ or even 96³) and add structural load with collapse. This is the single change that multiplies functional motif count rather than morphological variety: arches, buttresses, spans, galleries, load paths and enclosed chimneys all become real design problems, load conflicts genuinely with ventilation and thermal mass (giving you the conflicting objectives the current scalar band lacks), and 'a wall you can't remove' becomes structurally as well as thermally measurable. It also costs less than it sounds — 128³ is 2M cells, comparable to the 512² you were already solving four fields on, and dropping resolution buys back the throughput the honest arithmetic above says you don't have. If you can smuggle in a second change, make module promotion mint parameterized grammar nonterminals rather than patch stamps; without that the hierarchy in why_unbounded is not implemented anywhere.

ranked.name: Palimpsest (chronicle lens — bands, generated materials, encyclopedia)
ranked.why: Best-integrated instance of the only mechanism in the pool where an invention is a named, executable, inspectable object with a birth certificate: Stitch (stitch_core, POPL'23, verified real and genuinely 3-4 orders faster than DreamCoder's compressor) mines abstractions out of programs that actually kept a band alive, LILO-style auto-documentation names them, and the citation DAG IS the tech tree. Crucially it does NOT author the materials — a per-world generated table of substances plus a reaction map means the semantics are unauthored too, which is what separates it from Emberlisp's hand-written ignition thresholds. The builder can literally read `bank-the-coals`, print its body, see its three ancestors, and verify nobody wrote it. First weekend is real (VM + 15 primitives + enumerative search + `pip install stitch_core` + print the top abstraction) and the Sunday-afternoon payoff — the compressor names a subroutine you never wrote and Monday's search USES it — is the most reliable delight moment in the entire pool. Encyclopedia-with-etymologies is a genuine hour-long binge; the 30s card (new word, gloss, ancestry breadcrumb, bits saved) is tight. CPU-dominant, GPU only for naming, no API bill worth naming.
ranked.risk: The audit's corpus-homogeneity ceiling is correct and arrives ~week 8: world-derived tasks are bimodal (trivially solved or unreachable), so nightly MDL delta collapses and Stitch returns refactors of a solved corpus forever. Second: Stitch maximises compression, not meaning — roughly 3 in 4 abstractions will be positional plumbing that a 4B model will confidently christen anyway, manufacturing the appearance of depth exactly where there is least. Also literal: the PyPI package is `stitch_core`, and a stateful lisp with named binders does NOT pipe into Stitch unchanged — desugar to de Bruijn lambdas or it will treat variable names as primitives. Budget a day.
ranked.depth_verdict: Real but ceilinged at the task distribution, not the compressor. Depth is genuine through ~2 months and then flat unless the curriculum is made endogenous. With an autotelic goal generator bolted on it is the strongest depth engine here; without one it is a very good two-month project.

ranked.name: The Slow Kiln (library-learning lens — the artificial-chemistry one)
ranked.why: The single best first-weekend-to-surprise ratio in the pool, and the cleanest argument for why compressed fragments mean something. Author ~15 guarded reaction rules over composition multisets, not recipes; brute-force 100k random process programs on Saturday afternoon and you are already looking at products you did not anticipate BEFORE any agent exists. Then Stitch over the corpus of successful recipes mines the recurring fragments — and this is the one place in the whole pool where MDL and physical significance genuinely coincide, because a repeated 'hold above T then quench' really is a unit process. That is a much stronger claim than any other Stitch-based entry can make. Compute honesty is the best of all thirty ideas: recipes are PURE functions of a substance record, so observational-equivalence dedup and memoisation are cheap in the way DreamCoder's are and embodied variants' are not; interned substances plus a `(rule, inputs, conditions)` memo makes chemistry effectively free after first evaluation. Property-grid phone view (hardness × toughness, cells shaded by recency, tonight's substances as bright dots) shows progress as territory and is instantly legible. RAF closure detection is ~50 lines and gives a genuinely non-arbitrary threshold event.
ranked.risk: Two real ones. Substances saturate into sludge — rule-based chemistries have thermodynamic attractors and ~60% of recipes will terminate in three products by week three; the used-vs-produced ratio is the honest telemetry and must ship in week one, not later. And the RAF headline is at high risk of being an authored artifact: with 15 hand-written rules a self-sustaining set is usually either present on night one or structurally impossible, decided by you when you write rule 7. A threshold event that fires once and never again is a screenshot, not a mechanism.
ranked.depth_verdict: Real at the process layer, shallow at the substance layer. Its own audit's fix — replace 15 authored rules and 7 property functions with a generative core of ~50 per-element numbers (affinity, valence, mass, enthalpy contribution) and derive both guards and properties from them — is cheap, converts the chemistry into a mutable genome, and is the highest value-per-line edit anywhere in this pool. Do that and it stops being an authored gradient.

ranked.name: Glyphworks
ranked.why: The only design whose depth mechanism changes what is POSSIBLE rather than what is cheap, and that distinction is the whole ask. A works is a built object that installs a place-indexed primitive AND reaches a physical regime bare hands cannot — a hearth that sustains a temperature no `heat` call can hold. So each realised technology expands the boundary of what is realisable next, computed rather than enumerated: Kauffman's adjacent possible with an actual mechanism under it. Second-order works (built from a material only another works can make) is a real, detectable industry threshold. It also has the best bullshit detector of any idea in the pool: the map. A field of never-used buildings is self-evidently a bug, whereas a list of 90 named abstractions looks like success. The map-as-check-in plus tap-and-hold time-lapse of the whole valley history is the most shareable artifact here.
ranked.risk: Hardest engineering in the pool and it is not close. Place-indexed enumeration with context-partitioned observational equivalence is a cache-coherence problem, not a partitioning problem — works are built and decay, so the context signature at a site mutates and invalidates bank entries keyed to it. Get it wrong and you either blow 64GB or silently share banks across incompatible contexts and get wrong search results that are miserable to debug. Expect the first month to be the enumerator, not the watching. Two authored seams to close: the stationarity heuristic that promotes abstractions to blueprints (you will tune it until it promotes the buildings you hoped for) and the hand-written syntax→build-cost table, which is a recipe book in disguise.
ranked.depth_verdict: Highest genuine ceiling in the pool, but it grows in STOREYS and you author how many exist — ~3-5 with a fixed rule set. Its audit's one change is the real unlock and I endorse it strongly: rewrite the physics as ~6 rule SCHEMAS with open constants, and let a works instantiate a schema with constants it can physically sustain. Then the built environment extends the RULE SET rather than reaching further along a fixed one, storey count stops being authored, and the syntax→cost table deletes itself. Build it weekend 3-4 on an existing substrate, never standalone.

ranked.name: Emberlisp
ranked.why: The crispest specification of the core engine — tables, primitives, budgets, gates, phone view — and the one I would hand to a solo builder as the reference implementation of wake/sleep-in-a-world. Death is real, population is search budget (surviving buys more invention, and the death spiral is watchable in the numbers), use-it-or-lose-it demotion prunes MDL junk, and the ntfy line 'The Ash clan invented SPARK-ON-DRY-MOSS (fn_3, arity 2) — compresses 14 programs, MDL -22%' is exactly the 'you wrote no such word' moment the brief is asking for. Benchmark hygiene is correct and stated: node expansions and interpreter steps, never wall-clock, so a hot laptop and a cool one produce identical history. The transfer test across valley resets (does this abstraction survive relocation — local trick or law?) is a free, computed, unauthored classification of depth.
ranked.risk: Two, both real. The physics is 12 rules and 14 property records, so the SET of reachable qualitative effects is small enough that you could enumerate it in an afternoon — 'fire' is fully pre-figured because you wrote the ignition threshold and the percussion-sparks rule. What is genuinely emergent is the ORDER and the CHUNKING, not the menu. Second and more urgent: unlike pure DreamCoder domains, evaluating a candidate here means ROLLING OUT a stateful world, so observational-equivalence dedup is far weaker and a Python tree-walker gives you maybe low millions of nodes per core-night against a need for 10^6-10^7. 'Port to Rust only if profiling demands it' is wrong — profiling will demand it in week one.
ranked.depth_verdict: Real chunking over an enumerable effect set. Its own one-change (MAP-Elites over composite property space as the task generator, so goals grow as fast as the material space the abstractions open) is ~80 lines and converts a flat 4-10 week plateau into a receding frontier. Ship that in month one, not as a fallback.

ranked.name: Sandwright
ranked.why: The best answer in the pool to semantic risk: no LLM anywhere in the adjudication loop, so nothing can be invented that does not physically work, because working is defined by simulation. The oxygen-starved charcoal pile really is a consequence of rules you wrote that you did not anticipate — you authored a GENERATOR, not a catalogue, which is precisely the distinction the brief demands. And it has by a distance the best watchability of anything here: a three-second looping WebP of the new machine actually running, autoplaying on the card. Scrolling a catalogue of little machines your laptop invented is a genuinely great evening, and nothing explains a machine faster than watching it. Receipt-printer blueprint is the right physical artifact.
ranked.risk: Three, and one is hidden where the depth is supposed to be. (1) Falling-sand CA is NOT embarrassingly parallel — movement has write conflicts and update-order dependence, so a GPU port needs Margolus/block partitioning or atomics, which CHANGES the dynamics; the recommended 'debug on CPU then port' plan will shift the fitness landscape under you and may invalidate every archive elite. Pin determinism early. (2) MODULE INSERTION is much weaker than advertised: CA sub-assemblies couple non-locally through shared heat/pressure/flow fields, so measured transfer functions do not compose, and the 'physics surprise' detector (>3σ from linear composition of parts) will fire constantly because non-additivity is the default. (3) The 2D CA cannot represent rigid bodies, rotation or sealed pistons, so the month 3-6 ladder (heat engines, trip hammers) is unreachable; what it actually reaches is the thermal/fluid/chemical family, ~15-30 machine classes.
ranked.depth_verdict: Authentic but kind-bounded. Genuine unauthored emergence for 6-10 weeks, then MAP-Elites fills cells with mechanically valid near-duplicates while archive coverage keeps rising — progress that photographs beautifully and means nothing. Budget for redesigning descriptors twice, and treat 'add one material rule' as the scheduled, measurable, actually-fun maintenance ritual it is.

ranked.name: LOAM
ranked.why: The strongest evidence-of-depth artifact anywhere in the pool, and it is a chart: mean yield-gene inside versus outside tribal territory, diverging over months. Domestication here is not a recipe unlocked, it is directional selection on an evolving genome distribution driven by the tribe's own harvesting preference — which is the actual archaeological signature, arises with no clever policy required, and is a real emergent event with a real number attached. Semantic risk is essentially nil: every technology is a physical pattern in a raster with a measurable consequence on yield, water or erosion. Nothing can be drivel. The map-with-hot-diff-overlay is a superb four-second check-in because you see the SHAPE of what they built, and e-ink on the wall refreshed at dawn is the best off-screen ritual proposed. Cheapest GPU story that still uses the GPU sensibly.
ranked.risk: The ladder splits and only the bottom half is safe. Domestication lands; landscape engineering probably does not. Burn→delayed nutrient→plant, or dig a 20-cell channel whose water arrives 300 ticks later, is a sparse-reward long-horizon spatially-extended construction problem where a half-built channel pays strictly negative — the exact shape Craftax exists to demonstrate PPO fails at, and Craftax-MA's own conclusion is that IPPO/MAPPO/PQN all fail its long-horizon credit assignment. So months 2-4 (irrigation, terracing, a map a stranger can read) are at serious risk of never arriving. Also the novelty detector as written is a noisy-TV machine: prediction ERROR on a stochastic raster spikes on rain fronts and its own optimiser, not on the first channel. Use compression PROGRESS on held-out replay, not error.
ranked.depth_verdict: Real, narrow, honest — and it tops out at the neolithic by construction, with no channel to materials or mechanisms. Its fix is an option layer: parameterised multi-tick construction routines searched by quality-diversity over spatial descriptors, so a channel is one decision rather than four hundred.

ranked.name: Ashcairn
ranked.why: Near-twin of Emberlisp with two mechanisms worth stealing outright. First, the transmission bottleneck as a selection pressure on the LIBRARY rather than the tribe: only K functions can be demonstrated per season, so a large library is a liability for a small band and tribes with smaller, better-compressed libraries outcompete hoarders. Watching a civilization refactor its own tech tree for teachability is genuinely counter-intuitive and not authorable. Second, multi-world migration as an EXPERIMENT the system runs on itself nightly: a function that survives transplant into a differently-generated world is the strongest available evidence that the abstraction is real rather than overfit. The audit is right that this should be promoted from validation to training-data generation for the search prior.
ranked.risk: Two errors in the pitch are load-bearing. 'MDL compression IS metabolic efficiency' is a category error — Stitch minimises corpus AST size, not execution cost, and a four-token abstraction can loop 40,000 VM steps, so the compressor and the survival selector will fight. Re-rank Stitch candidates by amortised step savings before admitting them. And the higher-order endgame (`repeat_until_stable(f)`, `teach(f, learner)`, an abstraction that constructs abstractions) is fantasy as described: Stitch finds maximal-compression subtree patterns with term holes; it does not synthesise combinators or metaprograms. Separately, a bigram prior over a growing library gives almost no guidance and will stall at depth 2-3, not 6 — the neural recogniser is the plan, not the fallback, and it is the one job worth giving the idle 5070.
ranked.depth_verdict: Lowest authored-content risk of the combinatorial group and the compounding is measured in bits, so you will never wonder whether it is working. But abstraction count plateaus at ~30-80 and depth 3-4 on a world-derived task distribution, well short of the claimed 150-400 at depth 8-12.

ranked.name: Apocrypha
ranked.why: The cheapest project here and the one most likely to still be delighting at month 12 — and it earns that with a mechanism that is a faithful executable model of a well-supported theory (Henrich's account of adaptive practice accumulating through imitation and differential survival with nobody understanding why; the manioc-detoxification case). Watching `boil` reach fixation in surviving villages without anyone selecting for it, on Saturday, with no LLM in the loop, is a genuine and moving day-one payoff. The hitchhiking mechanic — a useless step fixes forever because it sat next to a useful one, and the critical apparatus can name the village and generation it entered — is the best single piece of unauthored drama in the pool.
