The critical edition (variant readings, apparatus, stemma, apocrypha) is a real hour-long binge and the phone card is a single verse with a footnote, which is a lovely ten-second read. Runs on nothing; correctly identified as the project to run ALONGSIDE a heavier one on the same laptop, which is the most practically useful sentence in all thirty documents.
ranked.risk: The adaptive fact set is enumerable in an afternoon — ~14 primitives, half functional, crossed with a handful of hazards gives maybe 20-50 truths, all found within weeks. After that the system cycles rather than discovers, and the open-ended layer (BECAUSE symbols, doctrine) is content-free BY DESIGN, which is an accurate model of one thing about religion and not what the builder asked for. Also note the anti-repetition machinery: an all-time n-gram ban over a small subject matter is a monotonically tightening constraint that stalls or forces strained synonym churn by month 4 — window it to 90 days and let rotating scribes with style cards carry the load.
ranked.depth_verdict: Bounded but genuinely unauthored within its bounds, and its own one-change points straight at the hybrid: graft a generated chemistry substrate under the ritual DSL so the cultural machinery — hitchhiking, conformist and prestige bias, schism, stemma — has an unbounded supply of real things to sanctify. Smallest change in the pool with the largest ceiling gain.

ranked.name: The Long Teaching
ranked.why: Contributes the two mechanisms I would put in whatever gets built, regardless of which engine wins. (1) Knowledge is embodied: `knows(agent, abstraction, fidelity)`, teaching is a costed program, and when the last carrier dies the abstraction is deleted and every dependent entry recursively invalidated — a dark age with a stack trace. A non-monotonic history genuinely cannot be faked with a tech tree, and 'the Reed clan has forgotten TWIST-CORD (age 611 nights, 9 dependents orphaned)' is a devastating notification that requires no LLM to be moving. (2) The rediscovery detector: a new abstraction whose behaviour signature on a fixed probe set matches a previously-deleted one but whose BODY differs. That is convergent re-invention, computed, and it is the only signal in the entire pool that cannot be fooled by a naming model. Make it the centrepiece, not a bullet.
ranked.risk: Weak as a standalone. Nine tribes on one machine is ~1/9 the node budget each on top of an enumerator that was already the bottleneck, and forgetting actively destroys accumulated depth, so expect per-tribe depth 3-4 and 20-40 live abstractions. Convergence is worse than stated: contact, trade and raid are all homogenising, so nine tribes under one rule set will hold maybe 6-10 genuinely distinct abstractions wearing nine generated names. And the headline rung — writing, via `mark`+`read` composing into a durable decodable encoding — is out-of-horizon, not hard: the payoff accrues to a different agent after the inventor is dead, and a per-night budget searching survival predicates has no credit-assignment path to it. Score the idea on the rungs below rung 5.
ranked.depth_verdict: No independent depth mechanism; it is a transmission and loss layer. But it is the best such layer available, and its fix for writing is historically right as well as computationally possible: give marks an INTRAGENERATIONAL payoff (pay ticks to read a mark and skip part of a re-derivation, now, in this program) so writing arrives by exaptation instead of foresight.

ranked.name: Marginalia
ranked.why: The best mutation operator in the pool and the best binge screen, both cheap. Scribal error — dittography, haplography, homoeoteleuton, numeral corruption, and above all marginal-gloss absorption (a copyist's note copied INTO the recipe body, historically the single most productive corruption there is) — is a real, ~120-line, structurally productive variation mechanism that nobody else proposed. Copy_of_id gives you an exact stemma for free, so the manuscript family tree with version diffs is genuinely an hour you lose without meaning to. The historian's chronicle written ONLY from surviving texts, then diffable against ground truth, is the best writing constraint in all thirty documents and costs nothing.
ranked.risk: No invention engine at all — it borrows one, and its own technology curve is flat by week 4-8 because line-level edits to ASTs have no smooth genotype-phenotype map and the beneficial mutations you do get are overwhelmingly deletions of redundant steps (efficiency, not capability). LLM interpretation of damaged text adds prior-biased variation, which beats white noise but regresses toward plausibility, i.e. it is a contracting operator. Institutions are parameterized authorship dressed as emergence: scriptorium is a building with an error-rate modifier, canon is a rich-get-richer rule you wrote, schism is a threshold you chose. Vary the thresholds and confirm the phenomena persist before believing them. And a public write endpoint feeding a corpus you publish is a permanent adversarial moderation obligation, not a cheap classifier call.
ranked.depth_verdict: A transmission simulator with a mediocre invention engine — correctly self-diagnosed. Bolt it onto a compression engine operating on the same DSL and the abstractions get minted by Stitch AND corrupted by copying, which is strictly better than either alone.

missing_angles: THE AUTOTELIC GOAL GENERATOR IS THE MISSING FIRST-CLASS COMPONENT. Roughly a dozen independent audits converge on the same diagnosis — the compressor is not the bottleneck, the TASK DISTRIBUTION is — and not one design ships a curriculum engine as a primary mechanism; it appears only as remedial advice. This is well-trodden ground and cheap: OMNI-EPIC (arXiv 2405.15568, ICLR 2025, code at github.com/maxencefaldor/omni-epic) is the archive-plus-interestingness-model reference; MAGELLAN (arXiv 2502.07709) does learning-progress prediction over large goal spaces; minimal-criterion coevolution gives you the goldilocks band with no handcrafted fitness. The laptop version is ~150 lines: keep a generated goal only if it is unsolved at budget B and solved at 3B, retire it once cheap. That single loop is the difference between plateauing at depth 4 in month two and continuing to compound.

NOBODY BUILDS A NULL CONTROL, AND SEVERAL OF THESE DESIGNS ARE MACHINES FOR FOOLING THEIR AUTHOR. Sandwright's archive coverage keeps rising while filling with near-duplicates; Emberlisp's library keeps growing after invention stops; Kithmind's dendrogram separates on sampling noise; Hivewright photographs beautifully after discovery has stalled. The fix is one extra process and one strip on the phone card: run a matched control world nightly — same seed, same physics, invention engine disabled (or abstractions admitted at random instead of by MDL) — and render both. If your headline metric moves the same in both, the engine is not the cause. Also ship a spoiler toggle showing ground truth beside the narrated version, and check it weekly; the alternative is discovering your sim is thin slowly and painfully over three months.

SEEDED COUNTERFACTUAL REPLAY SHOULD BE THE UNIVERSAL NOVELTY DETECTOR, NOT ONE IDEA'S NOTIFICATION. Grist proposes it and nobody else adopts it: for the ten most-adopted inventions per night, re-run N sim-years from a locked seed with the invention suppressed and report the survival delta. That converts 'a thing was invented' into 'a thing MATTERED', which is what a front page needs and what every first-ever/MDL-shock detector fails to measure. Every deterministic design in this pool can afford it on ten candidates a night. Do it with MATCHED cohorts across several seeds, not one draw, or you will ship notifications generated by variance.

THE 8GB GPU IS IDLE IN ALMOST EVERY SYMBOLIC DESIGN, AND THERE IS EXACTLY ONE JOB IT SHOULD BE DOING. Every library-learning audit independently concludes that a bigram prior over a growing library stalls at depth 2-3 and that the DreamCoder recognition model is the actual plan rather than the fallback — and every one of those designs then assigns the GPU to naming things. A ~200k-parameter recogniser trained nightly on dreamed replays is the correct use of the card, and the naming pass is what should be squeezed into the leftovers. Related and unaddressed: dreaming on one small world overfits the prior to that world's tasks, so the multi-world transplant machinery should be promoted from validation to training-data generation.

THE SHARED SUBSTRATE IS NAMED EVERYWHERE AND SPECIFIED NOWHERE. A dozen ideas say 'same event schema, same PWA shell, same push helper' and none of them writes down the contract. It is the one deliverable that makes project #2 cost a weekend instead of a month, and it is small: a versioned SQLite schema (events with canonical signatures, a lineage/parent-edge table, a novelty_scores table with per-channel z-scores, a nightly snapshot.json), a novelty ranker that takes channel scores and emits at most 3 pushes, a static PWA shell that renders one hero card plus sparklines from snapshot.json, and an ntfy helper. Build it as its own thing in weekend one and version it, or you will rewrite it four times.

THE PASSIVE AND PHYSICAL CHANNELS ARE ALWAYS GARNISH, NEVER THE PRIMARY. Sonification appears in six pitches and the receipt printer in five, each time as a bullet at the end. But the brief explicitly values the most passive possible check-in, and an ambient channel has a property no phone card has: it runs while you are doing something else, so it costs zero attention and still tells you when something changed. A nine-voice drone where a voice drops a note when a tribe forgets something, or a chemistry that sounds like rain on a roof on a productive night, is a better 24/7 monitor than any dashboard. Design one channel to be primary-passive and let the phone be the drill-down.

THE PUBLIC-PERTURBATION LAYER IGNORES ITS TWO ACTUAL FAILURE MODES. Guestbook-as-omen shows up constantly and is genuinely the cheapest non-stationarity available, but nobody addresses (a) the empty guestbook — a hobby page linked nowhere gets zero entries a month, which makes an idea whose long-term novelty depends on strangers plateau exactly like the ones that do not, and (b) the permanent adversarial moderation obligation created by a public write endpoint feeding a corpus you publish and print in your house. The cheap fix nobody proposes: skip the anonymous internet and give six named friends a private write endpoint. It gets used, it needs no classifier, and the perturbations are funnier.

NOBODY PLANS FOR THE RUN DYING AT 3AM. 'Near-zero chores' requires a heartbeat, not just an absence of chores. Every one of these is a 24/7 process on a laptop that will sleep, thermally throttle, OOM, or hit a Python exception in the enumerator, and the failure mode is silent: the morning digest simply stops, and you notice on day three. A watchdog that pushes 'the sim has not ticked in 90 minutes', a per-night checkpoint you can resume from, and event-log rotation automated on day one are the difference between an unattended project and a project that needs attending. Related: several designs put nightly compression, QLoRA, and a validation sweep in the same overnight window without checking that they fit in it.

THE VERIFICATION LOOP EXISTS IN EXACTLY ONE PITCH AND SHOULD BE RAIDED FROM IT. Firmament is the only design where the builder can hold the answer key: hidden laws generated from a grammar, tribes discovering them by costly experiment, PySR fitting symbolic expressions nightly, and 'their guess' rendered above 'the true law' on the phone. Its own ceiling is fatal as a standalone — a world with 6-10 laws and a working design-of-experiments loop completes in days, and its own audit's fix (derive the hidden regularities from a lower-level simulation so there is no closed form and no answer key) is correct. But the LOOP is worth stealing wholesale into any of the top-ranked designs: let tribes hold explicit THEORIES about the substrate, fitted from their own observation tables, choose the next experiment by disagreement among top-k theories, and design by optimisation-under-theory rather than by search. That is the mechanism that makes a civilization feel like it figured something out rather than merely having it selected for — the coldness the symbolic designs all share.
verdict.synthesis:
Build ONE project, in this order, and name it after its substrate rather than its story. Spine: Palimpsest's wake/sleep library learning (Stitch as the compressor, LILO-style naming) running over The Slow Kiln's GENERATED chemistry — with Glyphworks' works-as-rule-schema-instances as the depth mechanism, and three cheap mechanisms stolen from elsewhere.

Weekend 1 — chemistry, no agents. Author a GENERATIVE CORE, not rules: ~40 element tokens with a seeded table of about fifty numbers (valence, mass, affinity, an electronegativity analog, an enthalpy contribution, phase thresholds). Reaction guards and product property vectors are both DERIVED from that table by fixed formulas, so nobody — including you — has a list of what can be made, and a new world is a new draw of fifty numbers rather than a rewrite. Intern substances by canonical hash, memoise every (rule, inputs, conditions) tuple, then brute-force 100k random process programs and read what came out. Do this before any agent exists; it is the fastest genuine surprise available in the whole pool and it also measures, on day one, the single number that decides whether the project is interesting: the size of the reachable closure from the feedstock set. If that number is a few hundred, tune the core before writing anything else.

Weekend 2 — the engine. A typed process lisp (~28 primitives) over substances and sites, run by a deterministic VM that charges INTERPRETER STEPS and never wall-clock, so a thermally throttling laptop cannot reshape history. Bottom-up enumerative search with observational-equivalence dedup. One lethal survival predicate. Then `pip install stitch_core`, desugar your binding forms to de Bruijn lambdas first (budget a day for this — a named-binder lisp does not pipe into Stitch, whatever the pitches say), and mint the top abstraction as a new primitive. Re-run and confirm the same task now solves in a fraction of the nodes. Wire ntfy. That night your phone tells you a word you did not write.

The three gates that separate this from a junk generator, all in weekend 2: an abstraction is admitted only if it (a) clears an MDL threshold, (b) delivers amortised INTERPRETER-STEP savings across the corpus — this fixes Ashcairn's compression-is-metabolism category error, since Stitch minimises AST size and will otherwise mint short expensive abstractions your survival selection then punishes — and (c) is used by at least two bands on at least two distinct task templates before it earns a NAME. Everything else stays `unnamed fragment #331`. The naming model is the component with the least epistemic content and the most persuasive output; do not let it christen plumbing.

Weekends 3-4 — the two things that make month three unpredictable. First, WORKS: rewrite the derived physics as ~6 rule schemas with open constants, and let a stationary expensive abstraction be built as a works that instantiates a schema with constants it can physically sustain. A kiln does not cache a recipe — it makes a region of the reaction space reachable that no hand-executed program can reach at any budget. That is the difference between "cheaper" and "possible", and it is the only mechanism here where the built environment extends the rule set rather than reaching further along a fixed one. Key the observational-equivalence bank by (eval vector, works-context bitset, site EPOCH) — works are built and decay, so this is a cache-coherence problem, and getting it wrong gives you wrong search results that are very hard to debug. Second, the AUTOTELIC TASK GENERATOR, which every audit in the pool independently names as the real bottleneck: a MAP-Elites archive (pyribs, v0.11.0 stable) over composite property space — hardness × toughness × ignition × conductivity — emitting "produce an object landing in an empty cell" as goals, filtered by learning progress (keep a goal unsolved at budget B and solved at 3B, retire it once cheap). Survival predicates stay the lethal floor; property-frontier cells become the receding ceiling. Without this the whole thing plateaus in six weeks; with it, the goal set grows exactly as fast as the works stack opens new regions of chemistry.

Then the culture layer, which is what makes it a world rather than a chart. Knowledge is carriers: `knows(agent, abstraction, fidelity)`, teaching is a costed program, fidelity falls with DAG depth, and when the last carrier dies the entry is deleted and every dependent recursively invalidated. Add Marginalia's scribal-error operator on transmission — dittography, haplography, numeral corruption, marginal-gloss absorption — as a second, free variation channel alongside search, since a corrupted recipe occasionally outperforms its parent and you get the stemma for nothing. Run 3-4 worlds with different element genomes and transplant abstractions nightly: an abstraction's GENERALITY SCORE (fraction of foreign chemistries where it still earns call-sites) is a computed, unauthored classification into law versus local trick, and it is the cheapest real measure of depth in this entire pool.

Novelty, ANDed hard down to at most three pushes a day plus a guaranteed 07:00 digest: FIRST-EVER canonical hash; a new works opening a physical regime never before reached (the headline — this is "max achievable temperature" as the one gauge that says how advanced the world is); KEYSTONE (articulation point in the tech DAG, Tarjan, milliseconds); FORGETTING and REDISCOVERY (same behaviour signature on a fixed 64-state probe, different body — the one signal that cannot be fooled by a naming model); and SEEDED COUNTERFACTUAL CONSEQUENCE on the top ten adopted abstractions, matched cohorts across several seeds, reporting survival delta, so the feed reports what MATTERED rather than what was new. Run a matched null world with library learning disabled and put it as a thin strip on the phone card; if your curves move the same in both, the engine is not the cause and you want to know that in week two, not month four.

Phone: one hero card — the new named thing, its five-line ancestry as plain text, the works glyph on a small map, and one gauge. Binge: the encyclopedia — etymology DAG, who currently knows it, what dies without it, and the graveyard of lost techniques with the name of the last person who knew each one. Local Qwen3.5-4B Q4_K_M (~3GB, real and released March 2026, comfortable on 8GB with a bge-small embedder resident) under GBNF for names; one nightly Claude Haiku 4.5 batch pass over the ~30 most consequential entries for the chronicle voice, which at $1/$5 per MTok with the 50% batch discount and ~0.1x cached reads is roughly $0.20 a night. The LLM never touches adjudication. The GPU's real job is the ~200k-parameter recognition MLP that keeps enumerative search from stalling at depth 3 as the library grows — that is the job every audit says is required and every pitch assigns to naming.

What you get that no hand-authored tree gives you: month three contains a nine-step composite whose property vector nobody planned, standing in a works whose sustained regime was unreachable in month one, held by four people in one band, with a printable body and a lineage you can walk — and a number telling you whether it also works under a different periodic table.
